items.description: Brooke Bowen explores spiritual questions as she creates, drawing closer to her Heavenly Parents while pondering and painting motherhood. Walter Rane illustrates scenes from scripture, but also feels the reality of Christ through abstract artwork.

items.title: James Rees / Gwyneth Thompson-Briggs
items.description: James Rees explores the unique burdens we carry every day through his monotypes. Gwyneth Thompson-Briggs portrays the saints of her Catholic faith through her oil paintings.

items.title: Annie Poon / Greg Olsen
items.description: Annie Poon draws inspiration from her faith and her experience with depression to create artwork that shares how she found spiritual healing. Greg Olsen seeks to capture the character of Christ, centering the Savior in his life and paintings.

items.title: Leroy Transfield / Rose Datoc Dall
items.description: Leroy Transfield expresses his faith through sculpture. Rose Datoc Dall uses her skills as a painter to depict scenes of the Savior.

items.title: Sarah Winegar / Ron Richmond
items.description: Sarah Winegar uses reduction woodcuts and relief paintings to articulate her feelings about the human experience. Ron Richmond paints to explore spiritual allegory and metaphor.

items.title: Sunny Taylor / Jack Baumgartner
items.description: Abstract painter Sunny Taylor learns that joy and sorrow are intertwined like bittersweet vines, and that there is beauty in experiencing both. Jack Baumgartner recognizes his divine identity as much through painting as he does through farming.

items.title: Lisa DeLong / James Madison
items.description: Lisa DeLong uses geometry to reflect the order of the universe through artistic traditions rooted in sacred beliefs. James Madison is a Tulalip carver who keeps his culture alive with every totem pole he carves.

items.title: Behnaz Karjoo / Justin Hackworth
items.description: Behnaz Karjoo creates illuminations of Islamic geometry that reflect God's love and unity. Justin Hackworth is a portrait photographer who finds that God enters his life through those who step into his studio to have their picture taken.

items.title: Abigale Palmer / Fernando Cidoncha
items.description: Abigale Palmer loves color and discovers that difficult experiences, though uncomfortable, help us learn to communicate with Heavenly Father. Fernando Cidoncha creates sculptures and paintings that connect faith communities to their higher power.

items.title: Tyler Swain / Noémie Pons
items.description: Tyler Swain paints often-overlooked subjects and realizes that God's beauty exists all around us. Multidisciplinary artist Noémie Pons learns to see how people are transformed when they connect with the divine.

items.title: Ryan Moffett / Liz Lemon Swindle
items.description: After contracting Multiple Sclerosis, Ryan Moffett rediscovers his faith by sculpting. Liz Lemon Swindle thinks her art days are behind her until she finds inspiration in The Chosen, and a new appreciation for the life of Christ.

items.title: Kat Elliott / Jenedy Paige
items.description: Kat Elliot depicts God’s mercy through sculpture, using discarded objects to create works of art. Jenedy Paige finds inspiration in the memory of her son, and gives new meaning to the Nativity and healing from loss.

items.title: Jeff Hein / Jeanette Kuvin Oren
items.description: Jeff Hein explains how his health problems led to his devotion to painting Christ. Jeanette Kuvin Oren creates a torah cover for scriptures that survived the Holocaust.

items.title: Nicole Woodbury / Joshua Meyer
items.description: Nicole Woodbury is a sculptor who sees God in the patterns of biology. She finds inspiration on her journey to motherhood. God's creations in the Torah leads Joshua Meyer examines his relationship to light in his “Eight Approaches'' piece.

items.title: Irina Bradley / Qashif Masud
items.description: Irina Bradley shares how a battle with cancer inspired her to pursue iconography. Qashif Masud is a craftsman and woodworker who connects with God and his family history through carved calligraphy.

items.title: Esther Hi'ilani Candari / Bruce Smith
items.description: Esther Hi’ilani Candari tells how she switched from sculpture to painting, and why she paints the female religious experience. Bruce Smith shares how he came to paint religious art with techniques from the Old Masters.

items.title: Michael Malm / Kichaa Man Chitrakar
items.description: Michael Malm encounters challenges while creating a painting for his church. Kichaa Man Chitrakar draws closer to his family through his artwork.

items.title: Nativity
items.description: Painter Rose Datoc explores the role of Mary as the mother of the Savior through her art.

items.title: Fiona Rew / Jeff Pugh
items.description: Fiona Rew shares how she has felt inadequate throughout her life. Her glasswork encompasses the beauty of the growth she has experienced. Jeff Pugh’s depression in his life lead to the realization that we are not alone. His art shows how God has save

items.title: Amber Eldredge / Santiago Michalek
items.description: Amber Eldredge shares how God creates beauty from ashes and how she seeks to do the same with her art. Santiago Michalek focuses on portraying horses and automobiles with exact detail and strength in his paintings, inspired by his grandfather.

items.title: Blair Barlow / Kwani Winder
items.description: Blair Barlow finds comfort from prayer, inspiration from Catholic art, and bravery from St. Joan of Arc. Kwani Winder connects her heritage as part of the Santa Clara Pueblo tribe with her religion and uses that connection to build God's kingdom.

items.title: David Sandum / Elise Wehle
items.description: David Sandum discusses how artists Edvard Munch and Vincent Van Gogh helped him through depression to create art of his own. Elise Wehle talks about the process that lead her to printmaking with plants and natural materials.

items.title: Emily Hawkins / Bruce Naigles
items.description: Emily Hawkins began making art when she became a mother and uses her work to express her feelings about her children and motherhood. Bruce Naigles uses sculpting to answer his questions about life, focusing on staying joyful despite hard times.

items.title: Elizabeth Sanchez / Tenzing Rigdol
items.description: Elizabeth Sanchez discusses how she finds personalities in her art and how her work helped her through depression. Tenzing Rigdol connects with his culture and his parents' culture through different artistic techniques.

items.title: Kristin Carver / Gary Ernest Smith
items.description: Kristin Alley Carver creates art to connect to a higher power and to balance her experience with motherhood. Gary Ernest Smith reflects on how his roots in farming and his time in the military influenced his art.

items.title: Valerie Atkisson / David Dibble
items.description: Valerie Atkisson uses her art to remember her family, both living and dead, as well as to cope with her chronic disease. David Dibble grew up on a farm and discusses how his childhood inspires the nature that he paints as an adult.

items.title: Dan Wilson / Kazuko Covington
items.description: Dan Wilson discusses how his paintings have uplifted and encouraged faith within his family and in those around him. Kazuko Convington shares her process of making quilts to show her faith to everyone around her, including her ancestors.

items.title: Negyem Adonoo / Richard Adusu
items.description: Negyem Adonoo believes in energetically expressing his faith in God and his obedience through his paintings. Richard Adusu discusses how art helped him through the darkest times of his life and allowed him to express himself.

items.title: Expressions of Jesus
items.description: In this special episode of Artful, ten artists share their unique expressions of Jesus. Through intimate looks inside their studios and artistic process, these artists share their visual and spiritual testimony of the Savior, His life, and His works.

items.title: Paige Payne / Yongsung Kim
items.description: Paige Payne creates a community around the art that helps her overcome mental health struggles. Yongsung Kim reflects on his difficult journey to becoming an artist and the peace that painting brings him.

items.title: Pia Soriano-Gatdula / Rogério Pedro
items.description: Pia Soriano’s faith and love of painting guided her to create iconography pieces. Rogério Pedro finds joy in sharing his love of painting with his family.

items.title: Robert Besana / Pamela Salinas
items.description: Painter and art instructor Robert Besana paints a commentary on an issue he is passionate about. Pamela Salinas celebrates science and religion through her handmade, nature centered artworks.

items.title: Julie Yuen Yim / Anthony Sweat
items.description: Julie Yuen Yim inspires others with her traditional Chinese style artwork representing Christ. Instead of choosing between a career in art and a career as a religion instructor, Anthony Sweat embraces both.

items.title: Farkhondeh Ahmadzadeh / Ki-Woong Park
items.description: Painter and calligrapher Farkhondeh Ahmadzadeh creates detailed Persian miniatures that capture the spiritual essence of Sufi poetry. Sculptor Ki-Woong Park works with stainless steel and glass to create delicate expressions of faith and Christ.

items.title: Rodrigo Andriàn / Veronika Bianchi
items.description: Rodrigo Andriàn shares the joy of creation with his students, inspiring a new generation of painters. Veronika Bianchi makes a pact with God to become an artist and blazes a trail forward.

items.title: Maxwell Boadi / Taiichi Aoba
items.description: Maxwell Boadi’s dreams for a better life are fulfilled through God. Taiichi Aoba takes a new direction in his work after he joins the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

items.title: 12 Bands of Christmas
items.description: Discover the power of music as twelve local bands, including Fictionist, Ryan Innes, and Mindy Gledhill, perform Christmas songs old and new.

items.title: Baby in a Manger
items.description: Child protective services officer Alison and police officer Brock are both sworn to protect children, so when a lost infant shows up in the local church's nativity scene, they are both on the case.

items.title: Back of the Net
items.description: Science whiz Cory Bailey hops on the wrong bus and ends up at a soccer academy instead of her science program. Determined to beat a rival’s team, she combines her science smarts with her new friends’ skills to win the national tournament.

items.title: BYU Broadcasting HD Truck/Carillon Bell Tower
items.description: A behind-the-scenes look at the HD truck used to broadcast live BYU football games and the history and sounds of the Centennial Carillon Bell Tower.

items.title: BYU Cheer Squad/Mormon Tabernacle Choir
items.description: The BYU cheer squad talks about the trust and dedication they have toward each other and the BYU Army ROTC demonstrate their upper body strength as well as their strength of character.

items.title: BYU Broadcasting Master Control/Dancesport
items.description: George Tate, manager of Broadcast Operations for BYU Broadcasting, talks about the 24-hour, 7-day-a-week responsibilities of Master Control and students working for BYU Arts and Production revealing the hidden duties that make shows run smoothly.

items.title: BYU Scene Shop
items.description: A glimpse into the scene shop that creates the sets for BYU productions in the Harris Fine Arts Center and the people responsible for organizing, making, and distributing concessions at the LaVell Edwards Stadium.

items.title: BYU Creamery/BYU Bowling Alley
items.description: The BYU basketball camera crew talks about their efforts to get the best shot of the games in the Marriott Center while the LaVell Edwards Stadium field painters show off their hand-painting skills.

items.title: BYU Planetarium
items.description: The Royden G. Derrick Planetarium provides opportunities to educate students and the public about the heavens while the BYU grounds crew works hard to keep campus beautiful and safe all year round.

items.title: BYU Photo Archives
items.description: A look into the preservation of photographs and film in the Special Collections and the creation of a new student film called Heaven Under a Table.

items.title: BYU Special Collections
items.description: The Special Collections archive brings many different types of artifacts to BYU like a first edition book of Mormon and James Stewart’s accordion while the work of the Carpenter Shop can be seen in every building on campus.

items.title: BYU Piano Technicians
items.description: Listen to tales of piano tuners as they make sure all 433 pianos at the Harris Fine Arts Center are ready to play every day and to the mechanics who ensure that all 625 campus vehicles run smoothly for all who depend on them.

items.title: BYU Homecoming Spectacular
items.description: A behind the scenes look at BYU’s Homecoming Spectacular by the art director and some of the performers and of the collections and education provided at the Monte L. Bean Museum.

items.title: BYU Paint Shop
items.description: Librarians at the Harold B. Lee Library talk about the circulation process of the over 4 million books in this library and students of puppetry show off their projects.

items.title: BYU Library
items.description: A look at the different departments in the Harold B. Lee Library and the changes made to address student needs and a behind-the-scenes glance of the Mormon Tabernacle Choir Christmas Concert.

items.title: Ballet West's The Nutcracker Celebration
items.description: This immersive presentation of Ballet West’s “The Nutcracker” commemorates the 75th anniversary of Willam Christensen staging the first full-length production of the ballet in America with performances and interviews.

items.title: Ballet West's The Nutcracker
items.description: This special performance of Ballet West’s “The Nutcracker” commemorates the 75th anniversary of Willam Christensen staging the first full-length production of the ballet in America, featuring his original choreography.

items.title: Sanchez vs. Perkey
items.description: The Sanchez family faces off with the Perkey family in a generational battle of skill and wit, with a $10,000 prize up for grabs.

items.title: Wood vs Finn

items.description: The Bates family has an adventurous dad, a theater loving teen, and a singing grandma. The Witt family has a sporty dad, an aspiring crew member teen, and an ultra-competitive grandpa. They face off in an all out generational battle of skill and wit.

items.title: Warner vs Maggio

items.description: The Hintze family has a hippo-loving kid, a nurse and a grandma of 30. The Weir family has a dressy teen and his sock-loving family. They challenge each other to games like Flyover, Fan Armies, and Couch Potato.

items.description: The Disney-loving Gwilliam family competes with the academic Merrill family in games like Inseparable, Substitute Suzie, Re-enaction Star, and the Timeline Challenge.

items.title: Taylor vs Richards
items.description: The fashionable Taylor family and the spirited Richards family go head to head in challenges like Tag Me In That, Throwback Thursday, Here’s The Pitch, and Spoiler Alert.

items.title: Gardner vs Kener
items.description: The Gardner family challenges the Kener family in the games Ball of Ages, Re-enaction Star, and Feelin’ It; the parents go back in time with our Time Traveler; the teens take a swing at Here’s The Pitch.

items.title: Otsuji vs. Echavarria
items.description: The Otsuji family has a former sushi chef, an overly confident teen, and a retired teacher. The Echavarria family has a world-traveling mom, a teen soccer player, and a skydiving grandmother. They go head to head in games to test their knowledge.

items.title: Robertson vs Bevan
items.description: The Robertson family competes against the Bevan family. The grandparents take flight in a game of Flyover; the teens play Make This Work.

items.title: Free vs Wixom
items.description: The fun-loving Free family and the acrobatic Wixom family face off in challenges like Smack-A-Fact and Throwback Thursday; the grandparents meet the Couch Potato; the teens take flight with Flyover.

items.title: Broshinsky vs. Clegg
items.description: The brainy Broshinsky family plays the competitive Clegg family in games like The Movie Guy and What’s That Noise. Who will win the $10,000 prize?

items.description: On this special Christmas episode, the Marriott family and the Kawai family play holiday-themed games like Zoom Zoom, Unboxing, and Spoiler Alert.

items.title: Michelle Spencer: Measuring a Life of Service
items.description: Sam Houston's motto is "The Measure of a Life is its Service" and Alum Michelle Spencer lives this everyday. Here is her journey in helping the community of Walker County in Huntsville, Texas by operating the local Boys and Girls Club.

items.title: Hayden Hawks: All Heart
items.description: Hayden Hawks is the embodiment of heart. After his baseball dreams fizzled out Hayden found a love of running that his led to him to not only a successful career as a professional ultra-marathon runner, but also as a loving husband, father, and man.

items.title: Arkansas: Blending of Culture
items.description: Arkansas takes pride in the diversity found on their campus. They strive to include people from all backgrounds in their mission to make the world a better place.

items.title: Joey Su'a: 54 Days
items.description: Joey Su'a has overcome the odds as a deaf athlete for the Arkansas Football team. After a scare with death the Su'a family used their faith in God to help Joey reach his goals and his full potential.

items.title: Brandon Burlsworth
items.description: The inspiring story of Arkansas legend Brandon Burlsworth. His journey of self belief led him to the highest heights of Arkansas Football. Though his life ended early Brandon's legacy continues on as his life has inspired many to reach their goals.

items.title: The Arkansas Mission
items.description: The University of Arkansas is striving to represent the State of Arkansas with pride. Highlighting character, accountability, and unity is apart of the mission undertaken by the Razorback faithful.

items.title: Folds of Honor
items.description: Kansas alumni Lieutenant Colonel Dan Rooney created the Folds of Honor Foundation as a way to assist families of fallen soldiers.

items.title: The Rock Chalk Roundball Classic
items.description: Brian Hanni is known by Kansas fan as the voice of the Jayhawks. However, his desire to serve others led him to create the Rock Chalk Roundball Classic, a charity alumni basketball game. This event has helped aid hundreds of children battling cancer.

items.title: The Miracle Workers of UC Health
items.description: Damar Hamlin's life threatening experience on January 2, 2023 shook the entire world. Thanks to the efforts of medical staff from UC Health, training staff from the Bills and Bengals, and the support of millions Damar Hamlin has made a full recovery.

items.title: TCU’s Fellowship of Christian Athletes
items.description: Learn about TCU’s Fellowship of Christian Athletes and how the program helps athletes in their walk with Christ.

items.title: TCU’s FCA Bible Study with Lindsey Middleton
items.description: BYU’s Track and Field Athlete Lindsey Middleton attends TCU’s FCA Bible Study and talks about religion while being an athlete.

items.title: Be the Change
items.description: Red Raider defensive lineman, Tony Bradford Jr., patrols the line of scrimmage and the streets of Lubbock. Bradford Jr. is an aspiring police officer who spends most of his downtime assisting local law enforcement during ride alongs and traffic stops

items.title: The Shepherd of Lubbock
items.description: Pastor Bobby Dagnel is a volunteer chaplain for the Texas Tech football team who found his path later in life. After a life-changing conversation with a former co-worker, he has now become a Shepherd for many student athletes and patrons.

items.title: Mariachi Los Matadores
items.description: Dr. Lauryn Salazar has blown the roof off of conventional musical studies at the collegiate level. She has turned her cultural anthem of Mariachi into a pathway for education and success for students in Texas and across the country.

items.title: Royal Legacy
items.description: Legendary Texas football coach, Darrell Royal, helped change the lives of countless players and fans within the Texas community during his career as head coach. After he retired, he set up the Darrell K. Royal Fund to help others.

items.title: Iowa’s Innovators
items.description: Innovation isn’t a buzzword, it’s the Iowa State way of life. Iowa State University has become one of the nation’s hubs in innovation, paving the way for the future one idea at a time while being fueled by the desire to make the world a better place.

items.title: Jack Trice: The Spirit of Ames
items.description: Jack Trice was the 1st African-American football player in the country in 1923. His legacy is still alive and well in Ames, IA 100 years after his untimely death due to injuries sustained in a football game.

items.title: The Cowboy Code
items.description: Oklahoma State President Kayse Shrum blazes a new trail as the first woman to lead a public research institution in the state of Oklahoma. As a native Oklahoman, President Shrum has seen and lived “the Cowboy Code” first-hand.

items.title: Dynasty of Dominance
items.description: The Oklahoma State wrestling program has produced Olympians, world champions, and more importantly, world-class men. Led by arguably the greatest American wrestler of all-time in John Smith, the Cowboy wrestling program has its grips on history.

items.title: Baylor's Purpose
items.description: Located in the heart of Texas, Baylor University has become a destination for students who want to live a higher law of life, one where they strive to be the best versions of themselves both spiritually and physically.

items.title: S. U. R. E
items.description: Dr. Saleha Khumawala is helping change business culture one person at a time. She is the head of The SURE™ program at the University of Houston, where she helps students and entrepreneurs through an innovative, experiential learning program.

items.title: The Dream
items.description: Walter Thane Baker had a dream to run in the Olympics. After a work accident left metal in his knee, doctors told him to give up on his dream. He didn’t. And ended up winning 4 medals in 2 Olympiads.

items.title: Space U: Ever Upward
items.description: UCF was designed after JFK’s “Moonshot” speech as a pipeline for engineers to work at Cape Canaveral and aid the U.S efforts into space. Every year since 2017, UCF hosts a “Space Game” as tribute to the university's legacy and history with NASA.

items.title: For All Walks of Life
items.description: TCU’s Interfaith Initiative invites, welcomes and is a safe haven to all religions and students on campus. Rev. Todd Boling and Rev. Lea McCracken serve as Chaplains who champion each student’s individual journey of faith no matter what religion.

items.title: Proven
items.description: Throughout Kayleb Wagner’s life, he’s had to constantly prove himself. Despite being born with limb-differences, he excelled in sports, breaking records and stereotypes. This path also led Kayleb to Southern Illinois University.

items.title: City Futsal: A Mariel Family Legacy
items.description: In 2012, an immigrant family started a City Futsal league that changed the community and their family forever. Esteban and Manuel Mariel, twins, and graduates of SMU, along with their family, have created City Futsal as a safe space for fun.

items.title: Jacey Hupp: Be the Buffalo
items.description: Despite losing most of her vision in her right eye from a goat roping incident, Jacey Hupp excelled at every level in South Dakota rodeos. However, when a family tragedy shook her to the core, Jacey relied on her faith to keep riding forward.

items.title: Revival: the Bill Snyder Story
items.description: When Bill Snyder took over as the head coach of Kansas State football, the Wildcats were dubbed the worst team in the country. His emphasis on caring for the individual helped lead his team on one of the greatest turnarounds in college football.

items.title: Payton Washington: You Only Live Once
items.description: Before she became a national champion, Payton Washington overcame death and defied the odds of being able to live and walk again, let alone becoming the best in the country.

items.title: Be Golden
items.description: While playing for the Kansas City Chiefs, Robert Golden felt that his life was intended for something greater. He left the NFL and started Golden Charter Academy in his hometown of Fresno, California. The academy is helping others BE GOLDEN.

items.title: Trust Yourself
items.description: Taylor Roe is the most decorated athlete to come through the Oklahoma State T&F/X-Country program. Along the way to the pinnacle of her sport, Taylor overcame self-doubt and anxieties as she learned to trust herself and her instincts.

items.title: Bono Baseball: More Than a Game
items.description: Twin brothers Kyle and Ryan Bono are stitched together through their family’s bond with baseball. Their love of the sport has been passed down from their parents to them and now to their own kids. Bono Baseball is more than a game, it’s a way of life

items.title: Hayes Tough
items.description: Steve and Savanna Tate lost their son Hayes to cancer when he was just a toddler. In his honor, they set up the Hayes Tough Foundation to help ease the financial burdens of other families that are suffering from their own medical struggles.

items.title: Eric Weddle: Let’s Be Great Today!
items.description: During his time at the University of Utah and in the NFL, Eric Weddle exemplified his personal mantra of “Let’s be great today!” Weddle’s tenacity earned him success wherever he went, and now he’s teaching young men how to be great in his new role.

items.title: Utah - 3 Values
items.description: The University of Utah is dedicated to education, innovation, and community service, inspiring students to embrace challenges and contribute to society. The students, professors, and alumni are committed to being positive changemakers in the world.

items.title: Darrell Stuckey: Above and Beyond
items.description: After a successful career in the NFL, Darrell Stuckey has returned to the University of Kansas as a member of the coaching staff. Stuckey uses his faith and the lessons he learned growing up in adversity to help the next generation succeed.

items.title: Tony Achille: Until the end…
items.description: Ever since Tony Achille put on his skates for the first time he dreamt of playing division one hockey. Despite being diagnosed with cancer as a teenager, Tony worked harder than ever to pursue his dream and make it a reality.

items.title: Noah Guzman: No regrets
items.description: Noah Guzman worked his whole life to achieve his goal of playing football in college. After a freak injury threw all of his hard work into jeopardy, Noah turned to his faith and leaned on help from others to live with "no regrets."

items.title: Assane Diop
items.description: University of Colorado Men's Basketball forward Assane Diop's remarkable journey began in 2020 when he left his home in Dakar, Senegal to pursue his athletic and academic dreams in the United States.

items.title: Oscar Robertson: Leading the Way
items.description: An inspiring look back at remarkable faith and dedication of basketball legend Oscar Robertson—voted College Player of the Century in 2000 by the National Association of Basketball Coaches—from playing basketball with the University of Cincinnati.

items.title: Julius Thomas | Portland State
items.description: Portland State Basketball and Football alum and former NFL tight end Julius Thomas reveals the pivotal moments in his collegiate and professional athletic career that inspired his new career as a psychologist and mental health advocate.

items.title: Spencer Jones | Stanford
items.description: Stanford basketball alum Spencer Jones recalls the people and pivotal moments that led to his budding NBA career with the Denver Nuggets. Hear from his parents, former coaches, and Jones himself as he honors his past and looks forward to his future.

items.title: Lex Gillette | East Carolina
items.description: East Carolina University alum and Paralympian Lex Gillette shares his incredible story of how he lost his sight, then went on to become one of the most decorated totally blind long and triple jumper in US history.

items.title: Peggy Coppom | Colorado
items.description: 100-year-old Peggy Coppom has missed only a handful of University Colorado football games since 1966. Through her devotion, her friendship with Deion Sanders, and her faith, she’s become the cornerstone of the CU community.

items.title: Kevin Pittsnogle | West Virginia
items.description: When West Virginia University power forward/center Kevin Pittsnogle moved on from basketball, he struggled to find an identity outside of sports. Now, he’s made a difference in countless lives as a principal at North Middle School in Martinsburg, WV.

items.title: Amanda Beard | Arizona
items.description: Amanda Beard was 14 when she won her first Olympic gold medals. But success at such an early age came at a price. While attending college at the University of Arizona, Beard found the strength and support she needed to continue her Olympic journey.

items.title: Jordan Gross | Utah
items.description: Former Carolina Panther and Utah Ute Jordan Gross looks back on his successful football career and shares his current love of coaching high school football in his hometown of Fruitland, Idaho.

items.title: Spence Eccles | Utah
items.description: As one of the University of Utah’s most prominent alumni, Spence Eccles has dedicated countless hours making the state of Utah a better place. Now, Eccles reflects on the profound impact of his alma mater in shaping his faith, family, and character.

items.title: Carr Family | Iowa State
items.description: It began with Iowa State alum Nate Carr’s quest for Olympic gold. Now, Nate’s son, David, wrestles at his father’s alma mater with the same goal. Discover the inspiring story of one family’s journey of true greatness, on and off the mat.

items.title: Graham Harrell | Texas Tech
items.description: Texas Tech football legend Graham Harrell shares three miraculous experiences that reaffirmed his faith in God and brought his family even closer.

items.title: Dr James Cash Jr. | TCU
items.description: TCU basketball legend Dr. James Cash Jr. reflects on his transformative years playing for the Horned Frogs—a journey that changed hearts and minds and propelled his academic career to teaching at Harvard.

items.title: Rich Franklin | Cincinnati
items.description: University of Cincinnati alum Rich Franklin sees God’s hand guiding him throughout his life, from educator to three-time UFC middleweight champion and beyond.

items.title: Latavius Murray | UCF
items.description: After the tragic death of his best friend Jon Diaz, former UCF and NFL running back Latavius Murray commits to serving and inspiring youth in his hometown of Nedrow, NY by building the Jon Diaz Community Center.

items.title: Pickleball | Utah Tech
items.description: Utah Tech has quickly become the first dynasty in college pickleball, earning several national titles and a world championship in just a few short years.

items.title: Lance Briggs | Arizona
items.description: Arizona alum Lance Briggs’ childhood love of superheroes taught him to never give up, a lesson that pushed him through tremendous adversity into becoming an NFL Pro Bowler and one of the great linebackers of the modern era.

items.title: Zack Golditch | Colorado State
items.description: When a mass shooting shattered his community, Zack Golditch refused to give up football. His resilience inspired those around him, and after playing for Colorado State and the NFL, he continues serving others and giving back in meaningful ways.

items.title: Sydney Feager | TCU
items.description: After a horrific car accident left her unable to move, TCU equestrian Sydney Feager overcame impossible odds to walk, then ride, and finally, compete for her school.

items.title: Alli St. John | Iowa State
items.description: As a young girl, Alli St. John knew she wanted to wrestle competitively. Now, she blazes a new trail as Iowa State University's first-ever women's wrestling coach.

items.title: Chris Zorich | Notre Dame
items.description: Notre Dame football legend Chris Zorich shares his inspiring story of growing up in Chicago, playing for Notre Dame, his career in the NFL, and the incredible people who shaped his life—especially his mother.

items.title: Shaquill and Shaquem Griffin | UCF
items.description: Twin brothers Shaquill and Shaquem Griffin share their incredible story of how their unbreakable bond led them to play for both the UCF Knights and the Seattle Seahawks

items.title: Jalen Klemm | Arizona State
items.description: ASU offensive lineman Jalen Klemm’s future was bright, until a health scare no one saw coming threatened his life. Determined to overcome, Klemm relied on his faith and began the hard work of re-learning how to play football.

items.title: Garett Bolles | Utah
items.description: Former Ute and current Denver Broncos OT Garett Bolles knows what it's like to face the impossible. After a rough childhood, Bolles found his footing thanks to the right people who saw his potential for true greatness.

items.title: Jonathan Tchamwa Tchatchoua | Baylor
items.description: Former Baylor basketball power forward and current assistant coach Jonathan “Everyday Jon” Tchamwa Tchatchoua shares how a near-career-ending injury brought him closer to God.

items.title: Dan Fitzgerald | Kansas
items.description: University of Kansas baseball coach Dan Fitzgerald reveals how being the parent of a son with autism inspired him to provide opportunities for other families with autistic loved ones to enjoy watching baseball in a stadium.

items.title: NEW SHOW: Braver
items.description: Seven teens coping with various mental health issues leave behind their cell phones and embark on a survival adventure to learn how to reconnect with themselves and heal from their past. With the help of two seasoned survival experts and one group therapist, they must learn to survive with the bare essentials and face their demons. Can they learn from nature, or will their fears get the better of them?

items.title: Off the Screen and Into the Wild
items.description: Seven teens are selected to spend two weeks in the wilderness without their phones. As they hike to their campsite, Ryan is appointed the first group leader, but he must confront his own anxieties and self-doubt to become the leader the group needs.

items.title: A Storm is Brewing
items.description: This week, some members struggle with negative inner voices. John learns success isn’t defined by others, while the group leader takes charge with ease but struggles to open up to Dr. Z during their one-on-one.

items.title: Cracks on the Surface, Storms Underneath
items.description: As the group journeys to the third campsite, homesickness sets in for some campers, and tension begins to grow. Things take a turn when John suffers an injury and paramedics have to be called in.

items.title: Trial by Fire
items.description: Haunted by a past of bullying, John digs deep to overcome his anxiety, forming new bonds and stepping up to lead the group through an intense fire vigil challenge.

items.title: We're Cooked!
items.description: Tensions rise as the group splits, with Ravon, Jessica, and Yani forming a new clique that clashes with Kitana. Meanwhile, the group faces a grueling trek to two separate campsites and must take on back-to-back challenges over the next two days.

items.title: Who's Got Beef?
items.description: When Dr. Z's fireside chat fails to ease tensions, the team organizes their own discussion. However, conflicting views on the seriousness of the situation only deepen existing rifts and spark new in-group conflict.

items.title: Suffer Well
items.description: As the days draw to a close, each group member takes time for quiet reflection, contemplating their journey and personal growth. In a moment of vulnerability, Jessica confides in Dr. Z about the profound loss of her father.

items.title: Together
items.description: Battling exhaustion and poor nutrition, the group struggles to keep their raft afloat and push toward the finish line. Ravon overcomes his fear of the water by bravely volunteering to test the raft.

items.title: Fousseyni Traore at the Big 12 Media Days
items.description: Fousseyni Trarore sits down with BYUSN to talk about the team, the new conference, and expectations for the season.

items.title: Spencer Johnson at the 2023 Big 12 Media Days
items.description: BYUSN chats with Spencer Johnson about family life, excitement for the new season, and being able to compete together as a team.

items.title: Bright Lights in the Desert: The Latter-day Saints of Las Vegas
items.description: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints settled in the Las Vegas area in 1855 and it has flourished into a strong community. Interviews of Las Vegas citizens reveal how far the city has come and the history behind the original settlement.

items.title: Dallin H. Oaks | The Student Body and the President
items.description: President Dallin H. Oaks of Brigham Young University. "This fall I have felt impressed to speak to you about yourselves and about myself, a kind of centennial review of the student body and the President."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson | As a Chosen Generation, Be Prepared
items.description: Thomas S. Monson of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We have the potential to be a chosen generation. Truth, service, and love will help us be prepared to reach that potential and attain the Lord's approval."

items.title: Bruce R. McConkie | Who Shall Declare His Generation?
items.description: Bruce McConkie of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "I consider [this] to be the third greatest miracle that has ever occurred in all eternity...the miracle of creation: the fact that God, our Heavenly Father, brought us into being."

items.title: L. Tom Perry | The Church and the American Bicentennial
items.description: L. Tom Perry of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Let us all show justice, kindness, and charity toward our fellowmen. Let us demonstrate the love and reverence we should exhibit toward our Almighty God."

items.title: Marion G. Romney | America's Fate and Ultimate Destiny
items.description: Marion G. Romney, Second Counselor- First Presidency; the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "In God's economy, America is now and has always been a choice and favored land. God has decreed for her a final, great, and glorious destiny."

items.title: Ernest L. Wilkinson | America 1776-1976
items.description: BYU President Ernest L. Wilkinson. "Some of the events which history records took place preparatory to and necessary for the formation of our country and the restoration of the gospel, and whether this nation will continue to survive as a nation."

items.title: Dallin H. Oaks | Expectations at BYU
items.description: Dallin H. Oaks, President of Brigham Young University. "I will describe nine expectations...It is no exaggeration to say that these mutual expectation explain why we, teachers and students, have chosen to pursue our work at BYU."

items.title: Bruce R. McConkie | Jesus Christ and Him Crucified
items.description: Bruce R. McConkie of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Repentance means that we have faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, that we forsake our sins, that we come into the church and kingdom of God on earth and receive the Holy Ghost."

items.title: LeGrand Richards | The Prophets and the Scriptures
items.description: LeGrand Richards of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "If we'll walk in the way of the Lord and follow his holy prophets, as Peter said, we'll have a more sure word of prophecy. We'll never go astray."

items.title: L. Tom Perry | "I Need Thee Every Hour"
items.description: Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Grow mentally each day. Prepare yourself for the eternities to come. Be close to the Lord. Understand the potential within you.”

items.title: Elder Thomas S. Monson | Decisions
items.description: Elder Thomas S. Monson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The counsel of prophets and the power of prayer, together with the will to act, will guide us to our potential.”

items.title: Elder Gordon B. Hinckley | Forget Yourself
items.description: Elder Gordon B. Hinckley of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The happiest people I know are those who lose themselves in the service of others."

items.title: President Ezra Taft Benson | A Vision and a Hope for the Youth of Zion
items.description: President Ezra Taft Benson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of latter-day Saints. "I hope that you recognize in the gospel of Jesus Christ a solution to our problems, temporal and spiritual.”

items.title: Elder Bruce R. McConkie | Celestial Marriage
items.description: Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "[An obligation] rests upon Latter-day Saints to create for themselves eternal family units patterned after the family of God."

items.title: Elder Bruce R. McConkie | Joseph Smith: A Revealer of Christ
items.description: Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We are here to see if we will believe eternal truth and if we will conform to the principles so accepted and so learned.”

items.title: Jeffrey R. Holland | "That Our Children May Know"
items.description: Jeffrey R. Holland, President of Brigham Young University. "Will there be times in your life or theirs that they will need the substance of the gospel in a way that only you can teach it?"

items.title: Justice Dallin H. Oaks | Revelation
items.description: Dallin H. Oaks, Justice of the Utah Supreme Court. "I know that God lives and that revelation to his children is a reality. I pray that we will be worthy and willing, and that he will bless us to grow in this principle of revelation."

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | Meekly Drenched in Destiny
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Furthermore, whether you realize it or not, you are a generation drenched in destiny."

items.title: Jeffrey R. and Patricia T. Holland | However Long and However Hard the Road
items.description: Jeffrey and Pat Holland, President of Brigham Young University and Wife. "You [may] not see the full meaning of your effort in your own lifetime. But your children’s children will, until finally you, with all of them, can give the Hosanna shout."

items.title: Jeffrey & Patricia Holland | A Robe, a Ring, and a Fatted Calf // Walking on the Water
items.description: President Jeffrey R. Holland and Sister Patricia T. Holland, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "I want to give to you today the message that we can be washed and pronounced clean if we will but honor the Lamb of God."

items.title: Elder Russell M. Nelson | Begin with the End in Mind
items.description: Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Shape your own destiny...The development of your career, your family, and your faith in God is your individual responsibility."

items.title: Elder Marvin J. Ashton | What is Your Personal Ranking?
items.description: Elder Marvin J. Ashton of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The word is 'Remember.' I promise you without any hesitation it can help in your ranking with yourself and God."

items.title: Neal A. Maxwell | If Thou Endure Well
items.description: Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles; the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "None of us...will be immune from the trials of life...if we learn to endure our struggles well, they will be turned into blessings in eternity."

items.title: President Jeffrey R. and Patricia T. Holland | Some Things We Have Learned - Together
items.description: President Jeffrey R. Holland and Sister Patricia T. Holland, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Life ought to be enjoyed at every stage of our experience and should not be hurried... to fit an unnatural schedule."

items.title: Elder James E. Faust | A Message to Our Granddaughters
items.description: Elder James E. Faust of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You also have a great mission, a great errand, and a great calling. The work of God was devised by God for both men and women."

items.title: Jeffrey R. and Patricia T. Holland | "Unless You're a Mormon"
items.description: Jeffrey R. Holland, President of Brigham Young University and his wife, Patricia T. Holland. "God bless you to have a beautiful and rewarding new school year. Make it that way because you are Mormons."

items.title: President Jeffrey R. and Sister Patricia T. Holland | The Bitter Cup and the Bloody Baptism // The Soul's Center
items.description: President Jeffrey R. Holland and Sister Patricia T. Holland, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Our health and our wholeness are unquestionably linked with our holiness."

items.title: Jeffrey R. Holland and Patricia T. Holland| "Who We Are and What God Expects Us to Do" // Fear Not
items.description: Jeffrey R. Holland and Patricia T. Holland, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "He expects us to remember we are heirs of a gospel dispensation that had among its earliest commandments the challenge to ‘seek out of the best books.'"

items.title: President Jeffrey R. Holland and Patricia T. Holland | At Their Most Enlightened and Alert // Be Renewed in the Spirit of Your Mind
items.description: President Jeffrey R. Holland and Patricia T. Holland, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "There must be no concession to escapism here, that we must not be 'soothed' regarding sacrifice and learning."

items.title: President Jeffrey R. and Patricia Holland | The Will of the Father // Filling the Measure of Your Creation
items.description: President Jeffrey R. Holland and Sister Patricia T. Holland, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife. "So what can I be? What can be? We can be what heavenly parents designed us and intend us and help us to be."

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | "A Wonderful Flood of Light"
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Even as you and I come to love him, God loved us first all while he endures our insensitivity, our ingratitude, and our relapses."

items.title: Elder Russell M. Nelson | Reflection and Resolution
items.description: Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "This evening is a real milestone—the first Sabbath day of new semester, of a new year, and of a new decade."

items.title: President Rex E. and Janet G. Lee | Find Beauty in the Storm
items.description: President Rex E. and Janet G. Lee, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "I have grown to understand that to have ultimate faith in God is to know he is with us and will give us unfailing strength to help us through life’s challenges."

items.title: Eder Neal A. Maxwell | The Children of Christ
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We must, like the prodigal son, arise and go to our father and be prepared for that resplendent reunion."

items.title: Elder Boyd K. Packer | The Edge of the Light
items.description: Elder Boyd L. Packer of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "I feel contrary breezes blow and see dark clouds appear. It is them that I cry out in my prays at night."

items.title: Elder L. Tom Perry | Where There Is No Vision
items.description: Elder L. Tom Perry of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Never be satisfied with where you are. Always be reaching out to make the world a better place, to make your sacrifice for the benefit of your fellowmen."

items.title: Elder Richard G. Scott | The Fruits of Obedience
items.description: Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Yours is a future without limit because you have decided to be unwavering in obedience to the Lord."

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Sin and Suffering
items.description: Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Repentance, which is an assured passage to an eternal destination, is nevertheless not a free ride.”

items.title: Elder Howard W. Hunter | No Less Serviceable
items.description: Elder Howard W. Hunter of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Serve and grow, faithfully and quietly. Be on guard regarding the praise of men."

items.title: President Rex E. and Janet G. Lee | Keeping an Open Mind about Things that Matter
items.description: President Rex E. and Sister Janet G Lee, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Keep an open mind about things that really matter.”

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | Out of Your Experience Here
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, 1st Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We can offer our own witness of the truth, quietly, sincerely, honestly, but never in a manner that will give offense to others."

items.title: Elder Russell M. Nelson | Standards of Standard-Bearers of the Lord
items.description: Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Living in accord with these twelve standards will help us be worthy standard-bearers of the Lord."

items.title: President Rex E. Lee | The Constitution and the Restoration
items.description: Rex E. Lee, President of Brigham Young University. "I am satisfied that whatever else may eventually hang in the constitutional balance, this much is clear: The continuation of the blessings of liberty depends finally on our spiritual righteousness."

items.title: Elder Boyd K. Packer | "I Say unto You, Be One"
items.description: Elder Boyd K. Packer of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Each of us must accommodate the mixture of reason and revelation in our lives. The gospel not only permits but requires it."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson (3-3-91)
items.description: Highlights of the Church in 1990

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | "In Him All Things Hold Together"
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Oh, how we adore Jesus for his atonement! For his free gift of immortality to all!”

items.title: Elder Marvin J. Ashton | "And in Everything Give Thanks"
items.description: Elder Marvin J. Ashton of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Truly, if we love God, we will serve him now, and give thanks now."

items.title: President Thomas S. Monson | Be Thou an Example of the Believers
items.description: President Thomas S. Monson, Second Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You have the tremendous power to set an example for others who may come to know Christ through you."

items.title: Elder Howard W. Hunter | The Dauntless Spirit of Resolution
items.description: Elder Howard W. Hunter of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "It is worthy to make resolutions regarding our behavior, goals, or pursuits. Such resolutions become mileposts to guide our lives."

items.title: Elder Russell M. Nelson | Jesus the Christ-Our Master and More
items.description: Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Sinless and flawless as Jesus was in mortality, even He had to endure to the end. Can you and I be expected to do any less?"

items.title: Elder L. Tom Perry | "And Jesus Increase in Wisdom and Stature, and in Favour with God and Man"
items.description: Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints "Learn to appreciate the power and potential in your heads. Get out of your comfort zone! Expand your vision!"

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | This I Believe
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, First Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Everyone of us is largely the product of his or her beliefs. Our behavior is governed by these."

items.title: Boyd K. Packer (3-29-92)
items.description: Boyd K. Packer speaks to BYU students about "The Fountain of Life."

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Our Strengths Can Become Our Downfall
items.description: Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "A person who engages in self-congratulation over a supposed strength has lost the protection of humility and is vulnerable to Satan."

items.title: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin | "The Lord's Side"
items.description: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The Lord has left no doubt in defining his side and where the Saints should be in their thoughts, words, actions, and practices.”

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | The Inexhaustible Gospel
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Quite understandably, given its very nature, God’s latter-day work will be regarded with much skepticism by many.”

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | Trust and Accountability
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, First Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Trust and accountability are two great words by which we must guide our lives if we are to live beyond ourselves."

items.title: Elder Marvin J. Ashton | "Know He Is There"
items.description: Elder Marvin J. Ashton of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Quietly we can pray for the patience to have our secret prayers answered.”

items.title: President Rex E. and Sister Janet G. Lee | Selective Attitudes and the Happy Life
items.description: Rex E. and Janet G. Lee, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Selective attitudes—particularly when combined with the truths of the restored gospel—affect the quality of life itself."

items.title: Elder Russell M. Nelson | Integrity of Heart
items.description: Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Your precious identity deserves your precious integrity! Guard it as the priceless prize that it is."

items.title: Elder Richard G. Scott | Acquiring Spiritual Knowledge
items.description: Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "There is only one arena of study where we may learn absolute truth—and that is centered in the gospel of Jesus Christ."

items.title: Janet G. Lee and Michael Lee | Visualizing Our Success
items.description: Janet G. Lee, wife of Rex E. Lee, President of Brigham Young University, and her son Michael S. Lee, ASBYU President. "The Lord wants us to learn from our mistakes because that is how we become strong. He does not expect us to be perfect."

items.title: Elder L. Tom Perry | "To Everything There Is a Season"
items.description: Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We must continually be thinking about our preparation for the time of the harvest."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson (2-15-94)
items.description: Presidents of the Church

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | "Called to Serve"
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Be assured that God is 'in the details' and in the subtleties of the defining moments and the preparatory moments.”

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Sins and Mistakes
items.description: Elder Dallin Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "In the treatment process we should not require repentance for mistakes, but we are commanded to preach the necessity of repentance for sins.”

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | Codes and Covenants
items.description: President Gordon Hinckley, First Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Codes and covenants are as old as mankind and as contemporary as marriage.”

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Adversity
items.description: Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Like the mortal life of which they are a part, adversities are temporary. What is permanent is what we become by the way we react to them."

items.title: President Rex E. Lee & Sister Janet G. Lee | Your Time on Earth: When Would You Have Chosen to Come? // The Lord Doesn't Grade on a Curve
items.description: President Rex E. and Sister Janet G. Lee, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Never will our eternal value be measured in comparison with another’s performance. The Lord doesn’t think in terms of quotas—only qualities.”

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | To a Man Who Has Done What This Church Expects of Each of Us
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "God is our Almighty Father. He is our anchor and our strength...We must look to Him. We must extend our thanks to Him and seek His direction.”

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | "Brim with Joy" (Alma 26:11)
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "One of the great blessings the gospel gives us is the lens through which we can see with proportion.”

items.title: Elder M. Russell Ballard | When Shall These Things Be?
items.description: Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "These are the [challenging] last days. Safety, peace, joy, and security are found only in the life and mission of Jesus Christ."

items.title: President Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | A Peculiar Treasure // The Best Gifts
items.description: President Merril J. Bateman and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "As covenant children of the Lord and as his peculiar treasure, we must strengthen continually our faith in him and in his atonement.”

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | Stand Up for Truth
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "In this world so filled with problems, so constantly threatened, you can and must rise above mediocrity, above indifference."

items.title: President Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | A Faith That Preserves and Strengthens // One's Personal Influence
items.description: President Merrill J. Bateman and Sister Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "We can trust him. He earned our trust in the Garden and on the cross."

items.title: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin | Being Righteous in Our Hearts
items.description: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "How glorious is integrity! Those who have it display a constancy of character. Their behavior is the same in private as in public.”

items.title: Elder L. Tom Perry | The Value of a Good Name
items.description: Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We cannot isolate ourselves from those around us. Our good name can be a special valued asset worth more than the riches of the world."

items.title: President Thomas S. Monson | In Search of Treasure
items.description: President Thomas S. Monson, First Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "There are keys in our past, present, and future that can help us find our eternal treasure—the kingdom of God."

items.title: President Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | One by One // "To Thine Own Self Be True"
items.description: President Merrill J. Bateman and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "May each of us accept the Savior’s invitation to approach him and to spiritually see and feel the wounds in his hands, feet, and side."

items.title: Elder Henry B. Eyring | A Child of God
items.description: Elder Henry B. Eyring of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You are a child of God. Our Heavenly Father lives. Jesus is the Christ, our Savior."

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | The BYU Experience
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You came because you wanted the BYU experience, although perhaps you could not define it. Having gained it, never lose it."

items.title: President James E. Faust | Learning for Eternity
items.description: President James E. Faust, Second Counselor of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You need to know the purpose for your being. Each of you needs to ask yourself, Why am I here on earth?”

items.title: President Merrill J. Bateman | The Eternal Family
items.description: Merrill J. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University. "Each one of us may be part of an eternal family if we are obedient to gospel principles. A fullness of joy is found only within the framework of an exalted family."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson (3-10-98)
items.description: Thomas S. Monson delivers an address entitled "Your Choice."

items.title: President Merrill J. & Marilyn S. Bateman | Children of the Covenant // Our Sacred Honor
items.description: President Merrill J. Bateman and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "It is one of the cornerstones of character. Integrity implies honesty, moral soundness, and a quality of being undivided."

items.title: Richard G. Scott (9-15-98)
items.description: Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Decisions Based upon Eternal Truth. That pattern of life will lead you to success, accomplishment, peace, happiness, and great joy."

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | The Quest for Excellence
items.description: Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Reach for the stars. If you touch them, great shall be your reward. If you stumble and fall while reaching upward, you will be happy knowing you have made the effort."

items.title: Merrill and Marilyn Bateman (1-5-1999)
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, Merrill J. Bateman, and his wife Marilyn S. Bateman. "May our testimonies motivate us to improve our lot in life."

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Weightier Matters
items.description: Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We know that the work of God cannot be done without unity and cooperative action.”

items.title: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland | "Cast Not Away Therefore Your Confidence"
items.description: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Perseverance saved Moses when he was surrounded by enemy forces, and it can save you too.”

items.title: President Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | Gathered in the Tops of the Mountains // Evolution of the Mind, the Heart, and the Soul
items.description: Merrill J. Bateman and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Read the scriptures daily, even if only for a few minutes. Accept Church assignments and fulfill them. Make daily prayer a pattern in your life.”

items.title: Elder James E. Faust | Our Search for Happiness
items.description: Elder James E. Faust of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The Savior of the world taught us to seek that inner peace which taps the innate happiness in our souls.”

items.title: President Gordon B. Hinckley | Keep the Chain Unbroken
items.description: President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Life is a great chain of generations that we in the Church believe must be linked together."

items.title: President Merrill and Marilyn Bateman (1-11-00)
items.description: President Merrill J. and Sister Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "If we continue earnestly with faith and hope in Christ to seek the gift of charity, it will be granted to us."

items.title: Elder M. Russell Ballard | The Lord Has a Work for You to Do
items.description: Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. " It is more important than what you do, even as vital as your work is and will be.”

items.title: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland | How Do I Love Thee?
items.description: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You want capability, safety, and security in dating and romance, in married life and eternity? Be a true disciple of Jesus."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson (9-12-00)
items.description: Thomas S. Monson delivers an address entitled "What God Expects."

items.title: President Merrill J. & Marilyn S. Bateman | Light, Visions, and Dreams // Tapestry of Life
items.description: President Merrill J. & Sister Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "If we make Christ the center of our lives, our tapestries will be rich in color and beautiful in design."

items.title: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin | "Live in Thanksgiving Daily"
items.description: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Gratitude is a mark of a noble soul and a refined character. They tend to be more humble, more joyful, more likable."

items.title: Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | Christ Is the Reason
items.description: Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Christ is the basis for all that we do. Without the Savior and His Atonement, there would be no good news to spread."

items.title: Elder Richard G. Scott | To Acquire Knowledge and the Strength to Use It Wisely
items.description: Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You can learn vitally important things by what you hear and see and, especially, by what you feel, as prompted by the Holy Ghost."

items.title: Elder M. Russell Ballard | "Here Am I, Send Me"
items.description: Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We cannot fulfill our mission as a Church without the inspired insight and support of women."

items.title: President Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | "Lay Hold upon Every Good Thing"
items.description: Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Family relationships are sacred. The bonds within families have spiritual roots. We know that we lived as brothers and sisters before coming to earth."

items.title: Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | How Knoweth This Man Letters
items.description: Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "Do you feel the beauty and power of the scriptures? Can you sense the blessings that await if you drink deeply of Christ's living water?"

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Timing
items.description: Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Accept the Lord's planning and the agency of others in matters that inevitably affect you. Take the long view- the timing of eternity."

items.title: President Merrill J. Bateman | Temples of Learning
items.description: Merrill J. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University. "Remember and honor those whose lives were lost in last year’s tragedy. May we live in a manner that will add to the Spirit in this temple of learning. May we be worthy of the Holy Ghost."

items.title: Russell M. Nelson | Christ the Savior is Born
items.description: Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "With a testimony of the Lord we have the privilege in faith to testify of His divine parentage and that Jesus is the Son of [God]."

items.title: Merrill J. and Marilyn S. Bateman | Mortality and Our Eternal Journey
items.description: Merril J. and Marilyn S. Bateman, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "We are the spirit offspring of an Eternal Being who has given us the opportunity to experience mortality-a brief but critical time in an eternal journey."

items.title: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin | Improving Our Prayers
items.description: Elder Joseph B Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "As we approach our Heavenly Father in the name of Christ, we open the windows of heaven."

items.title: President Cecil & Sharon Samuelson | Outward Expressions of the Inner Self // Be Thou an Example
items.description: President Cecil O. and Sister Sharon G. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University and his wife. "When we show that we really know who we are, we benefit not only ourselves but others."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson (1-20-04)
items.description: Thomas S. Monson delivers this address entitled "I Will Serve the Lord."

items.title: Elder Neal A. Maxwell | "Free to Choose"
items.description: Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The vital revelations about the agency of man…inevitably and simultaneously portray the perfect generosity and perfect justice of God.”

items.title: President Cecil O. & Sharon Samuelson | Integrity // A Good Name- A Priceless Possession
items.description: President Cecil O. Samuelson and Sister Sharon G. Samuelson, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. "May we honor our names and thus our forebears as we strive to live righteous lives."

items.title: Dallin H. Oaks (11-9-2004)
items.description: Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "What seem to be only small detours from the straight and narrow path can result in huge differences in position down the road of life."

items.title: Cecil O. & Sharon G. Samuelson (1-18-05)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University. "Each one of us here is writing the book of his or her life, and reading, learning, loving, serving, and worshipping are integral parts of the process."

items.title: James E. Faust (3-1-05)
items.description: James E. Faust of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints should be in our hearts, and when it is in our individual hearts, it will also be in our great in our buildings of worship."

items.title: David A. Bednar (5-10-05)
items.description: David A. Bednar of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Like baptism by water comes before the baptism by fire, so being quick to observe is a prerequisite to and a preparation for the gift of discernment."

items.title: Cecil O. & Sharon Samuelson (8-30-05)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University. “Our prophet’s voice and the message it shares can be trusted to teach and guide us."

items.title: Gordon B. Hinckley (9-20-05)
items.description: President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Gordon B. Hinckley. "President Joseph F. Smith had an understanding of the eternal nature of man that few others have ever possessed."

items.title: Robert D. Hales (11-15-05)
items.description: Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The temple is a sacred edifice, a holy place where essential saving ceremonies and ordinances are performed to prepare us for exaltation."

items.title: Cecil O. & Sharon G. Samuelson (1-10-06)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University. "Our eternal worth is given to us by God. We can lose sight of our self-worth if we do not keep the commandments and consequently disregard the divinity within us."

items.title: Cecil O. & Sharon G. Samuelson (9-12-06)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University. "The Honor Code is an outward manifestation of our inner appreciation for and understanding of the privilege of being at BYU."

items.title: Gordon B. Hinckley (10-31-06)
items.description: Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "[Experiences] have influenced my thinking and my behavior. They have affected my life in an unforgettable manner. You likewise will have significant experiences."

items.title: Thomas S. Monson (11-14-06)
items.description: Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The gate of history swings on small hinges, and so do people’s lives. You must pass through each gate to be successful in your journey through mortality."

items.title: Cecil and Sharon Samuelson (1-09-07)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of BYU. "The seeds of faith and light are planted, cultivated, nurtured, and grow bathed in the glow of His tender care."

items.title: Boyd K. Packer (1-16-07)
items.description: Boyd K. Packer, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "If you hold on to the rod, you can feel you way forward with the gift of the Holy Ghost."

items.title: Pres. Cecil Samuelson and Sharon Samuel (9-11-07)
items.description: Cecil O. Samuelson and his wife, Sharon G. Samuelson. "Do not neglect your private and personal prayers, your scripture study, or your appropriate acts of anonymous service as as the public manifestations you make of you devotion to God and country."

items.title: Gordon B. Hinckley (9-18-07)
items.description: President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Gordon B. Hinckley. "God is no respecter of persons. All are deserving of our consideration. Love and mercy must be the foundation principles of our relationships."

items.title: L. Tom Perry (10-30-07)
items.description: L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "In this first dispensation we learn that we are sons and daughters of an Eternal Father and have the right to communicate with Him."

items.title: President Thomas S. Monson (11-13-07)
items.description: First Counselor in the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Thomas S. Monson. "I testify to you today that turning away from God brings broken covenants, shattered dreams, and crushed hopes."

items.title: Cecil O. and Sharon Samuelson (1-8-06)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of BYU. "I do know that in this extraordinary community of students, staff, faculty, and administrators there are many who deserve our respect, admiration, and appreciation."

items.title: Pres. Henry B. Eyring (1-15-08)
items.description: Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Your experience in enduring well in the trials of life can bring you the assurance you need to find peace in this life and confidence for the next."

items.title: Richard G. Scott (3-18-08)
items.description: To Establish a Secure Foundation for Life

items.title: Cecil O. and Sharon Samuelson (9-9-08)
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of BYU. "We are really agents of God the Father in providing these little ones the very best mortal experiences possible."

items.title: President Cecil & Sister Sharon Samuelson (1-6-09)
items.description: President Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson of Brigham Young University. "Each of you has the light of Jesus Christ within you. How wonderful that is for you as you strive to discern what is truly of great worth in your life."

items.title: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland (1-13-09)
items.description: Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Faith builds on the past but never longs to stay there. Faith trusts that God has great things in store for each of us.'"

items.title: President Cecil & Sister Sharon Samuelson (9-8-09)
items.description: President Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson of Brigham Young University. "The things of greatest ultimate importance to us are largely in our control and are within the scope of our agency."

items.title: President Thomas S. Monson (9-15-09)
items.description: Thomas S. Monson, president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Remember whom you can follow- even the Lord Jesus Christ. Let us follow Him. He has sent Presidents of the Church, whom we can have as guides and whom we can follow."

items.title: Cecil O. & Sharon Samuelson (1-5-10)
items.description: Lessons Taughts by Two Prophets/Act Well Thy Part

items.title: Cecil O. & Sharon Samuelson (9-7-10)
items.description: Appropriate Zeal/Gratitude -- a Commandment of God

items.title: Elder Robert D. Hales (9-14-10)
items.description: Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles speaks to students on the subject "Our Essential Spiritual Agency."

items.title: Cecil O. and Sharon Samuelson (1-4-11)
items.description: Seven Suggestions/Remembering and Honoring Your Covenants

items.title: D. Todd Christofferson (10-19-1999)
