items.description: D. Todd Christofferson of the Presidency of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "May your reverence for these holy beings and your allegiance to them be the shining guide of your life forever."

items.title: Robert H. Daines (6-20-00)
items.description: Robert H. Daines, Driggs Professor of Strategy in the BYU Marriott School of Management. "Let us establish clearly our priorities in life. Let us go to the sacrament table repenting of our sins and renewing our covenants on a weekly basis."

items.title: LaVell Edwards | Take upon Yourself the Whole Armor of God
items.description: LaVell Edwards, Former Brigham Young University Head Football Coach. "As members of the Church, we must seek truth in all areas, be it spiritual, educational, scientific, or in the social and moral settings of society."

items.title: W. Gibb Dyer Jr. | Repentance: The Key to Eternal Progression
items.description: W. Gibb Dyer Jr, Professor of Organizational Behavior at Brigham Young University. "To recognize sin we must not rely on the world but rely on our living prophet, President Hinckley; the scriptures; and our ecclesiastical leaders to show us the way."

items.title: Lynn E. Garner | Learning in an Eternal Context
items.description: Lynn E. Garner, Chair of the Department of Mathematics at Brigham Young University. "The knowledge of most worth comes first as we learn to place all learning in the context of the gospel of Jesus Christ and seek the gifts of the Spirit as we learn."

items.title: Kristine Hansen | Lift Up Thine Eyes to the Mountains
items.description: Kristine Hansen, Associate Dean of General Education and Honors and Professor of English. "I propose that in striving to achieve the aims of a BYU education, you will simultaneously be advancing in your quest for perfection and eternal life."

items.title: Mary Williams | To Know and to Be Known of God
items.description: Mary Williams, Associate Dean in the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. "Sooner or later every person who has lived on this earth will be given knowledge regarding the divinity of Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Jeffrey D. Keith | Feeling the Atonement
items.description: Jeffrey D. Keith, professor of Geology at Brigham Young University. "If we are constantly seeking to know the breadth and depth of His atoning love and how very personal it really is, our seeking will not be in vain."

items.title: David A. Bednar | "In the Strength of the Lord"
items.description: David A. Bednar, President of Brigham Young University-Idaho. "As you and I come to understand and employ the enabling power of the Atonement in our personal lives, we will pray and seek for strength to change our circumstances."

items.title: Elder Cecil O. Samuelson | The Importance of Asking Questions
items.description: Elder Cecil O. Samuelson of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "One of the key ways that we learn—not only here at BYU but throughout life—is by asking questions."

items.title: John D. Lamb | Witnesses in Stars and Stones
items.description: John D. Lamb, professor and associate dean of General Education and Honors at BYU. "The Lord has sent you witnesses in stars and stones that He lives, that He loves you, and that He has set in place a plan. All He has created can be yours."

items.title: Elaine Michaelis | Anxiously Engaged
items.description: Elaine Michaelis, Director of Women's Athletics at Brigham Young University. "We cannot be slackers in our commitment to the Lord, in our effort to be an example of His teaching, or in our desire to share."

items.title: Bruce Chadwick (5-7-2002)
items.description: Bruce A. Chadwick, professor of sociology at Brigham Young University. "Today I want to share with those of you who are single some of the appropriate ways to establish an eternal relationship. A good marriage and family life is crafted, not found."

items.title: Alan Parkinson (5-14-02)
items.description: Alan Parkinson delivers a message entitled "The Savior's Example in Doing the Father's Will."

items.title: Elder Sheldon F. Child | Follow the Prophet
items.description: Elder Sheldon F. Child of the Seventy for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We sustain 15 men as prophets, seers, and revelators. [President Hinckley] holds the keys of the kingdom. He is the Lord's chief apostle on the earth today."

items.title: Dennis B. Neuenschwander (11-12-2002)
items.description: Dennis B. Neuenschwander of the Presidency of the Seventy for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Much trouble in life originates from forgetting what we should remember and remembering what we should forget."

items.title: Robert L. Marshall | Becoming
items.description: Robert L. Marshall, Chairman of the Department of Visual Arts at Brigham Young University. "We are being prepared to perform many great and marvelous things in our families, communities, and church.”

items.title: Keith J. Karren | Ultimate Health: God's Gift and Our Personal Responsibility
items.description: Keith J. Karren, professor of Health Sciences at Brigham Young University. "Our Father in Heaven desires us to be joyful and well, to nurture and care for the garden that is entrusted to each of us."

items.title: Bishop Keith B. McMullin | Make God and His Kingdom the Center of Your Life
items.description: Bishop Keith B. McMullin, 2nd Counselor of the Presiding Bishopric of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Position yourself firmly inside God's kingdom; allow it to encompass you."

items.title: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf (11-11-2003)
items.description: Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the Presidency of the Seventy. "The Holy Ghost will be the wind beneath your wings, placing in your hearts the firm conviction of the divinity of the Lord Jesus Christ and His place in the eternal plan."

items.title: Sheri L. Dew | You Were Born to Lead, You Were Born for Glory
items.description: Sheri L. Dew, President and CEO of Deseret Book Company. "You simply must understand this, because you were born to lead by virtue of who you are, the covenants you have made, and the fact that you are here now in the 11th hour."

items.title: John K. Carmack | Bless the Poor and Needy
items.description: John Carmack, managing director of the Perpetual Education Fund for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Let's do what we can, according to our circumstances, to lift those arms that hang down."

items.title: Lee Wakefield | Feel and Follow the Holy Spirit
items.description: Lee Wakefield, professor of dance at Brigham Young University. "Appreciate the wisdom of placing ourselves in situations where the Spirit of the Lord can be present. It makes a difference where we are, what we are doing, and when we are doing it."

items.title: Elder D. Todd Christofferson | Moral Agency
items.description: Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The beauty of the gospel of Jesus Christ is that it pours knowledge into our souls and shows things in their true light.”

items.title: President Cheryl C. Lant | God's Love
items.description: Cheryl C. Lant, Primary General President for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Pure love is a gift and is at the very foundation of His gospel. Our love for Him is constantly being redefined as we learn, grow, and experience."

items.title: Stephen Jones | "He Hath Made with Us an Everlasting Covenant, Ordered in All Things, and Sure"
items.description: Stephen Jones, dean of the College of Fine Arts and Communications at Brigham Young University. "Surely, returning to our loving Father is the final purpose of our attempts to order our lives in full and complete wholeness."

items.title: Thomas B. Griffith | "The Very Root of Christian Doctrine"
items.description: Thomas B. Griffith, Judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. "When we are speaking of what the Savior has done for us, we are at the core of the meaning of life, and we are connected to the root of Christian doctrine."

items.title: Robert C. Oaks (3-21-06)
items.description: Robert C. Oaks of the Presidency of the Seventy for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Here, you owe it to yourself to make an extra effort to discover who you really are—to discover your true and eternal potential in God’s plan."

items.title: Andrew C. Skinner | The Nature and Character of God
items.description: Andrew Skinner, Executive Director of the Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship at Brigham Young University. "We may rest assured that our Father knows all things and He does all that He does out of love."

items.title: Edward Blaser (5-9-06)
items.description: Edward Blaser delivers an address entitled "The World is Our Stage."

items.title: Elder Neil L. Andersen | Seeing Through the Generations
items.description: Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Seventy for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You will see more clearly who you are and what you must become. Your place in this vast, beautiful plan of happiness is no small place."

items.title: Joseph D. Parry | On Being a Christian Perfectly
items.description: Joseph D. Parry, associate professor in the Department of Humanities, Classics, and Comparative Literature at Brigham Young University. "I want to think with you about being a Christian perfectly, rather than doing Christianity perfectly."

items.title: Elder Donald L. Staheli | "Be Strong and of Good Courage"
items.description: Elder Donald L. Staheli of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "While you will be tried and tested, your faithful adherence to the Lord’s standards will be seen as a beacon in the night to those around you.”

items.title: Gerald R. Williams | Learning from Our Conflicts
items.description: Gerald R. Williams, professor of law at Brigham Young University. "When we remember our conflicts and reflect on them, they are like mirrors that can teach us things about ourselves that are otherwise difficult to discover."

items.title: Jo Ann C. Abegglen | The Power of One: Selfless Service
items.description: Jo Ann C. Abegglen, associate professor of Nursing at Brigham Young University. "It is easy to give away excess money, used equipment, and used clothing. It is more difficult to give of our time, to give of our personal presence to help others."

items.title: William H. Baker | Knowing, Doing, and Being
items.description: William H. Baker, professor of management communication at Brigham Young University. "In addition to increasing what we know and improving how we apply that knowledge, we must refine who we are deep down in our heart."

items.title: Scott D. Sommerfeldt | Exactness in Our Discipleship
items.description: Scott D. Sommerfeldt, department chair of physics and astronomy at Brigham Young University. "As we become more exact in our discipleship of the Savior, there is an impressive power that comes into our lives that aids us in our spiritual growth."

items.title: David A. Hunt | "Fresh Courage Take"
items.description: David A. Hunt, assistant administrative vice-president of Student Auxiliary Services at Brigham Young University. "The Lord has promised to give us His power and protection as we live righteous lives."

items.title: Douglas L. Callister (9-19-06)
items.description: Douglas L. Callister of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The nearer we get to God, the more easily our spirits are touched by refined and beautiful things. Refinement is a companion to developed spirituality."

items.title: Thomas A. Holmoe | Brotherly Love
items.description: Thomas A. Holmoe, athletic director of Brigham Young University. "In our present-day situations, we would all do well, as children of our Heavenly Father, to contemplate our answer to that same question: 'Am I my brother’s keeper?'"

items.title: Joseph Fielding McConkie | Finding Answers
items.description: Joseph Fielding McConkie, emeritus professor of ancient scripture at Brigham Young University. "It is not the design of heaven that we be rescued from all difficult situations. Rather, it is the system that we grow up and learn to handle them."

items.title: Peter M. Johnson | Faith, Family, and Friendship
items.description: Peter M. Johnson, Assistant Professor of Accounting at the Marriott School of Business at Brigham Young University. "We have been given much; therefore we must give of ourselves and incorporate and strengthen faith, family, and friendships."

items.title: President Bonnie D. Parkin | Personal Ministry: Sacred and Precious
items.description: President Bonnie D. Parkin, Relief Society General President in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "I believe we received our personal ministry in the premortal world. It was divinely given and lasts a lifetime."

items.title: Elder Quentin L. Cook | Be a Missionary All Your Life
items.description: Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Peace in this life does not come from merely pursuing worldly objectives. Eternal life… does not come from pursuing merely worldly objectives.”

items.title: Richard O. Cowan | Preparing for That Which Is to Come
items.description: Richard O. Cowan, Professor of Church History and Doctrine at Brigham Young University. "May we ponder our personal part in helping the Lord's kingdom roll forth."

items.title: Neil J. Anderson | Responding to the Savior's Invitation: "Come"
items.description: Neil J. Anderson, Professor of Linguistics and English Language at Brigham Young University. "As we desire to respond to the Savior's invitation to come, we will have to leave behind our weaknesses and our sins."

items.title: Elder Richard G. Hinckley | "Prophetic Priorities"
items.description: Elder Richard G. Hinckley of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Some of you struggle with certain doctrines or practices of the Church, past or present. That's okay. Be patient, but be persistent."

items.title: Gary K. Palmer | The Spokes of a Balanced Life
items.description: Gary K Palmer, Professor of Recreation Management and Youth Leadership at Brigham Young University. "We need to remember that all we take with us is who we have become through serving God.”

items.title: Earl C. Tingey | The Watchman on the Tower
items.description: Elder Earl C. Tingey of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We do not change all this because we have living prophets who ‘stand in holy places,’ and [are not] moved."

items.title: John Telford | "Gladly, Gladly We'll Walk in the Light"
items.description: John Telford, Professor of Visual Arts at Brigham Young University. "To be the best in the world, all of the attention is focused on the individual. To be the best for the world, the attention is focused on others."

items.title: Delora Bertelsen | The Care and Keeping of BYU's Human Resources
items.description: Delora Bertelsen, Managing Director of Employee Relations, Equal Opportunity, and Benefit Services at Brigham Young University. "As children of our Heavenly Father, we should know that how we treat each other is very important in His eyes.”

items.title: Tina Taylor Dyches | "Walk as Children of Light"
items.description: Tina Taylor Dyches, Associate Professor of Counseling Psychology and Special Education at Brigham Young University. "Let us shine the Light of Christ at home, at school, at play, at work, and in any other place where we may be found.”

items.title: Brian K. Evans | Your Contract with BYU
items.description: Brian K. Evans, Chief Financial Officer and Administrative Vice President at Brigham Young University. "Let our campus be an inclusive community, not an exclusive fraternity."

items.title: Ronard Brough | Balance in Life
items.description: Ronald Brough, Professor of Music at Brigham Young University. "Prayer is a tool to help us commune with our Father in Heaven. It is also the vehicle He can use to reveal His will to us.”

items.title: Elder Bruce C. Hafen | A Disciple's Journey
items.description: Elder Bruce C. Hafen of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Christ is so eager for our return that He comes to meet and strengthen us all along our way. No matter where we are on that path, we are never lost to Him."

items.title: Gregory Clark | Some Lessons on Faith and Fear
items.description: Gregory Clark, associate dean of the College of Humanities at Brigham Young University. "In faith, we are blessed with peace that comes in the form of confidence- confidence that in the midst of all the storms of this life, all is well."

items.title: David A. Thomas | A Law upon Which All Blessings Are Predicated
items.description: David A. Thomas, professor at J. Reuben Clark Law School at Brigham Young University. "One of the things we should think about each day is whether [the blessings received] seem to be coming to us in response to our obedience to… the Lord."

items.title: Mary Anne Prater | Using Spiritual Maps to Navigate Through Life
items.description: Mary Anne Prater, chair of the Department of Counseling Psychology and Special Education at Brigham Young University. "We have spiritual maps to help guide and direct us to our ultimate destination- back to our heavenly home."

items.title: E.J. Caffaro | Our Personal Game Plan
items.description: E.J. Caffaro, director of the Student Athletic Center at Brigham Young University. "Know what your personal game plan is for today and for your future. Incorporate these strategies into your lives and protect yourselves from the adversary."

items.title: Rae Jeanne Memmott | Learning Eternal Truths Through Our Relationships with Others
items.description: Rae Jeanne Memmott, associate professor of nursing at Brigham Young University. "I have come to realize that there isn’t much to do with the gospel that isn’t about relationships- either with Heavenly Father and the Savior or with our fellowmen."

items.title: Scott M. Ritter | "Come Ye, and Let Us Walk in the Light of the Lord"
items.description: Scott M. Ritter, chair of the Department of Geological Sciences at Brigham Young University. "Appreciate the blessings of this greater light and knowledge in our lives and understand the methods by which it has been, and continues to be, obtained."

items.title: Rodger Sorensen | Evidences of the Heart
items.description: Rodger Sorensen, Department Chair of Theatre and Media Arts at Brigham Young University. "We must learn the language of the Spirit for ourselves and find our own sacred places in which we personally come to know the things of God by [the Spirit]."

items.title: Craig H. Hart | Our Divine Nature and Life Decisions
items.description: Craig H. Hart, professor of human development in the School of Family Life at Brigham Young University. "There is an important spiritual dimension of our beings that cannot be probed by scientific means. Our [spirits] and biology are intertwined."

items.title: Fred E. Woods | The Soul of Kalaupapa
items.description: Fred E. Woods, professor of religious understanding at Brigham Young University. "In a world of religious varieties, the unconditional love and spirit of acceptance that exist on Kalaupapa stand as an example to us all."

items.title: Elder Robert R. Steuer | Just in Case Someone Asks, I Will Be Ready
items.description: Elder Robert R. Steuer of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Embracing key scriptures and doctrines can help us simplify and prepare for life’s important decisions.”

items.title: Bishop Richard C. Edgley | Faith, Hope, and You
items.description: Bishop Richard C. Edgley of the Presiding Bishopric of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "I would like to talk about how the powerful twin forces of faith and hope can affect your future. Hope [is] the result of exercising faith."

items.title: C. Terry Warner | An Education of the Whole Soul
items.description: C. Terry Warner, professor of philosophy at Brigham Young University. "God desires the flourishing of your whole soul for the glories He has in mind that is why He intends to bless you, if you will exert yourself, with a soul-stretching education."

items.title: Sarah Westerberg | Pastry, Chalk Circles, and Other Words to Live By: A Guide to Keeping Commitments
items.description: Sarah Westerberg, Associate Dean of Students at Brigham Young University. "As we ponder the wonder of His birth and life on earth, let us also review the commitments we have made and recommit to labor with greater zeal during the coming year."

items.title: Elder Bruce D. Porter | A Child Is Born
items.description: Elder Bruce Porter of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Whatever binds us, whatever sins, circumstances, or past events hold each of us captive, the Lord Jesus Christ, the great Immanuel, has come to set us free."

items.title: J. Matthew Shumway (1-20-09)
items.description: J. Matthew Shumway, professor of geography at Brigham Young University. "Our life's journey is intended to be difficult. Otherwise we would not be pure enough to return and live with our Father in Heaven and receive His eternal blessings."

items.title: Barbara Culatta (2-3-09)
items.description: Barbara Culatta, professor of education at Brigham Young University. "If we were to give others the benefit of the doubt by looking at their intentions, our lives would be much richer and we would be more tolerant."

items.title: Ronald A. Rasband (2-10-09)
items.description: Ronald A. Rasband of the Presidency of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Temples are houses of the Lord, where our Savior’s teachings are reaffirmed through sacred ordinances which unites families for all eternity."

items.title: Stephen J. Bahr (3-3-09)
items.description: Stephen J. Bahr, professor of sociology at Brigham Young University. "Our Savior wants us to succeed and will support us through our trials if we have the faith to follow Him and the counsel He has given through His prophets."

items.title: Jay E. Jensen (3-10-09)
items.description: Jay E. Jensen of the Presidency of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "I know that we will face both current and future storms successfully because of this rock which we build our lives, our faith, and our testimonies."

items.title: Carol Wilkinson (3-17-09)
items.description: Carol Wilkinson, professor of exercise sciences at Brigham Young University. "If trials haven't come into your life yet, rest assured that they will come to each of you at some point...another reason trials come is that they can help us develop."

items.title: David V. Dearden (3-31-09)
items.description: David V. Dearden, professor of chemistry and biochemistry at Brigham Young University. "It is fun to think about what science can teach us about the gospel in general and about agency in particular. For me, science is highly faith affirming."

items.title: Michael A. Jensen (5-5-09)
items.description: Michael A. Jensen, professor of electrical engineering at Brigham Young University. "We must identify those things currently keeping us from following the Savior as fully as we should and be willing to put those things on the altar of sacrifice."

items.title: Brett G. Scharffs (5-12-09)
items.description: Brett G. Scharffs, professor of law at Brigham Young University. "Faith, hope, and charity...are [foundational]. Each is a trait of character to be cultivated...a set of attitudes and beliefs to guide thought and action...a choice...a gift from God."

items.title: Steven C. Wheelwright (5-26-09)
items.description: Steven C. Wheelwright, President of Brigham Young University- Hawaii. "Following the Lord's process of decisions making results in consistently and powerfully righteous decisions. And that pattern of...decision making in turn develops our character."

items.title: Glenn L. Pace (1-11-05)
items.description: Glenn L. Pace delivers an address entitled "Your Work is Not Yet Finished."

items.title: Elder Gene R. Cook | The Love of God: Suffering Tribulation in the Redeemer's Name
items.description: Elder Gene R. Cook of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "[God] has blessed me with many wonderful days-more of those than of difficult days of suffering and despair."

items.title: Brad W. Farnsworth | Reflections of the BYU Experience
items.description: Brad W. Farnsworth, Administrative Vice President of Brigham Young University. "I didn't really appreciate what BYU offered until I had graduated and left the campus."

items.title: Thomas Sederberg (3-29-05)
items.description: Professor of Computer Science, Thomas W. Sederberg. "To ignore or violate the principle of faith will hamper our own progression and diminish our spiritual influence on others. The mastering of faith gives us joy."

items.title: Shirley R. Klein | Protect Our Homes, Renew Our Powers
items.description: Shirley R. Klein, Associate Professor of Family Life at Brigham Young University. "Our social fabric has been attacked around the edges, and now it is moving to the center—our homes! I'll use Moroni’s strategies of preparing places of security."

items.title: Van C. Gessel | The "Welding Link" of Culture
items.description: Van C. Gessel, Dean of the College of Humanities at Brigham Young University. "The more links you forge with your ancestors through their culture, the richer the legacy you will have to pass along to your own children and grandchildren."

items.title: Douglas M. Chabries | Talents
items.description: Douglas M. Chabries, professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Brigham Young University. "I would invite each of you to study and prepare your minds and then make a commitment to develop your talents."

items.title: Dana T. Griffen | Choices and Changes, Burdens and Blessings
items.description: Dana T. Griffen, Associate Dean of the College of Physical and Mathematical Sciences at Brigham Young University. "If we are to emulate the Savior, then our choices must repeatedly lead us to Christlike behavior.”

items.title: Hal B. Heaton | Truth
items.description: Hal B. Heaton, professor of Finance at Brigham Young University. "If you really understood that truth, you would sacrifice anything—everything—to achieve it. Understanding this truth is central to your purpose for being on the planet."

items.title: Lynn A. Mickelsen (6-28-05)
items.description: Lynn A. Mickelsen of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Growing up requires constant decision making. We must learn to be decisive, because indecision is no choice at all. If we fail to choose, we fail to act."

items.title: Arnold H. Green | Discernment for Journeying Through Babylon to Athens and Zion
items.description: Arnold H. Green, professor of History at Brigham Young University. "Discerning our journey through the world entails, first, choosing specific worthy destinations rather than just drifting somewhere."

items.title: Gordon B. Lindsay | "And Always Remember Him"
items.description: Gordon B. Lindsay, Associate Dean of the College of Health and Human Performance at Brigham Young University. "The Lord does not want some form of general, always-sort-of-in-the-back-of-the-mind kind of remembering."

items.title: Janielle Christensen (8-2-05)
items.description: Artistic Director of Brigham Young University Living Legends, Janielle Christensen. "Opportunities to serve are available to all of us if we will seek for them and have the faith and courage to accept them when they come."

items.title: R. J. Snow | "The Ends of the Earth Shall Inquire After Thy Name"
items.description: R. J. Snow, professor of Political Science at Brigham Young University. "The Lord’s firm assurance to the Prophet was laden with profound implications for the future of missionary work in the Church."

items.title: Timothy J. Powers (10-25-05)
items.description: Coach of the Brigham Young University's Men's Swim Team, Timothy J. Powers. "Constant effort yields perfection in a skill and a glimpse of the capacity our Heavenly Father has endowed us with. Trust and coachability are akin to faith and obedience."

items.title: K. Richard Young (11-1-05)
items.description: Dean of the David O. McKay School of Education, K. Richard Young. "Thus kindness is a test of the quality or genuineness of our character. Each act of kindness leaves a yellow or positive mark on our personal touchstone."

items.title: Carri P. Jenkins | A Solemn Obligation
items.description: Carri P. Jenkins, Assistant to the President for University Communications at Brigham Young University. "Each one of us has the ability and the obligation to testify and defend the work of the Lord.”

items.title: Heidi S. Swinton | Joseph Smith: Love of the Cause of Christ
items.description: Heidi S. Swinton, award-winning author, screenwriter and member of the Relief Society General Board. "Joseph’s life was one of pure integrity to the cause of Christ, who he loved. He loved what the Lord loved. He lived the Lord’s way. It wasn't easy

items.title: Daniel E. Johnson | The Cycle of Becoming
items.description: Daniel E. Johnson, assistant dean in the College of Physical and Mathematical Science at Brigham Young University. "This cycle...is literally going on in some micro or miniature form every day of our lives. That's how we've become who we are today."

items.title: David Day | Lessons of Pride and Glory from the Doctrine and Covenants
items.description: David Day, music and dance librarian for the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University. "Pride is Satan's great counterfeit for glory."

items.title: C. Raymond Smith | Depending on the Lord: Gospel Insights from a Musician
items.description: C. Raymond Smith, professor of Music at Brigham Young University. "If we consecrate our preparations unto the Lord and leave the outcome in His hands, the outcome will always be a blessing to us. He can control the outcome much better than we can."

items.title: Lynette B. Erickson | Flags, Faith, and Finishing the Race
items.description: Lynette B. Erickson, associate professor of Teacher Education at Brigham Young University. "An important part of the race of life is that the Creator of the plan knows who we are and has given us the necessary...tools for [successful completion]."

items.title: Richard D. Draper | Light, Truth, and Grace: Three Interrelated Principles Necessary for Exaltation
items.description: Richard D. Draper, professor of Ancient Scripture at Brigham Young University. "When they accept grace by accepting the light, they are capacitated to receive truth. As they continue by giving grace...they are eventually glorified in truth."

items.title: Jeffry H. Larson | What Do You Expect?: A Key to Personal Happiness
items.description: Jeffry H. Larson, professor of Marriage and Family Therapy at Brigham Young University. "By being more aware and...realistic in our expectations and thoughts about life..., we can become happier than...by expecting life or others to change for us."

items.title: Curtis D. Lebaron | Face-to-Face Leadership: "As a Man Speaketh unto a Friend"
items.description: Curtis D. Lebaron, associate professor of organizational leadership and strategy in the Marriott School at Brigham Young University. "I want to talk about today...the private conversations whereby leaders change people and transform organizations."

items.title: Erin D. Maughn | Be Still, and Know God
items.description: Erin D. Maughan, assistant professor of Nursing at Brigham Young University. "Instead of stressing over [disappointments] or blaming others, sometimes it is best for 'be still,' become humble, and put your trust in God that all is well."

items.title: President Kim B. Clark | "Are Ye Stripped of Pride?"
items.description: Kim B. Clark, President of Brigham Young University- Idaho. "The message is clear: whether in prosperity or in adversity, if we are not diligent and faithful, even the elect of God...can fall prey to the Great Lie and become hard-hearted."

items.title: Susan Sessions Rugh | Our Journey into the Wilderness
items.description: Susan Sessions Rugh, associate dean of the College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences at Brigham Young University. "After our life's journey, we will be reunited with Him and our loved ones, and we can say: 'I am back. I am safe. I love you.'"

items.title: Elder Walter F. Gonzalez | A Brave Generation
items.description: Elder Walter F. Gonzalez of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "You may draw courage to defend the principles of righteousness from your faith in God and also from your love toward God and your fellow man."

items.title: Elder Jon M. Huntsman Sr. | God Did Not Put Us Here to Fail
items.description: Elder Jon M. Huntsman Sr., Area Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Our Heavenly Father expects the best from each of us. We must believe in ourselves. Don't give in when the going gets rough."

items.title: Bishop H. David Burton | These Are the Times
items.description: Bishop H. David Burton, Presiding Bishop of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "It is an awesome and exciting time to be alive because the fullness of the gospel of Jesus Christ has again been restored to the earth in our day."

items.title: Rollin H. Hotchkiss | God Loves You
items.description: Rollin H. Hotchkins, associate chair of the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Brigham Young University. "If Heavenly Father loves me and knows of me- since He is no respecter of persons- He loves you as well."

items.title: President Cheryl C. Lant | Hold Tight to the Iron Rod
items.description: President Cheryl C. Lant, General Primary President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Be true to everything that you are and everything you can become It is so worth it... It will bring you full circle back to Him."

items.title: Richard B. Miller | Repentance and Forgiveness in Marriage
items.description: Richard B. Miller, professor in the School of Family Life at Brigham Young University. "Repentance includes striving to forsake our shortcomings and weaknesses... We endeavor to become better listeners and less judgmental."

items.title: Rosemary Thackeray | Strengthened by the Hand of the Lord
items.description: Rosemary Thackeray, associate professor in the Department of Health Science at Brigham Young University. "As we wait upon the Lord and prepare ourselves to be strengthened by the hand of the Lord, we will become the person [He] desires us to become."

items.title: Elder Spencer J. Condie | A Disposition to Do Good Continually
items.description: Elder Spencer J. Condie of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Your righteous thoughts and deeds will overcome any susceptible disposition to do evil...the Holy Spirit will be your constant companion."

items.title: Barbara A. Heise | Grow Toward Christ
items.description: Barbara A. Heise, professor in the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. "We don't have to be perfect- after all we can do, the Savior does the rest... we choose to be changed, to be spiritually stronger, and to come closer to the Savior."

items.title: Elder Glenn L. Pace | The Divine Nature and Destiny of Women
items.description: Elder Glenn L. Pace of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "My associations... with the righteous women in my life have created a metamorphosis of my spirit and have been purifying and sanctifying."

items.title: C. Jeffrey Belliston | Gospel Gifts
items.description: C. Jeffrey Belliston, assistant university librarian for the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University. "The giving and receiving of gospel gifts are two separate actions...the true receipt of a gospel gift is manifested by keeping the gift."

items.title: Ross Spencer | Scholarship and Faith
items.description: Ross Spencer, chair of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Brigham Young University. "The priesthood and science both help us live better in this complex world."

items.title: Steven C. Baugh | The Parable of the Cherry Tree: How to Enjoy the Constant Companionship of the Holy Ghost
items.description: Steven C. Baugh, professor of education at Brigham Young University. "Branches separated from their roots wither and die, but when they are connected, they receive nourishment, which brings abundant life."

items.title: W. Vincent Wilding | Tenacious Faith and Selfless Service
items.description: W. Vincent Wilding, professor of chemical engineering at Brigham Young University. "If we show tenacious faith and are prepared to lose ourselves in service, our Father in Heaven will prepare the way for us to accomplish all that He asks of us."

items.title: Jeffrey F. Ringer | Finding Sanctuary
items.description: Jeffrey F. Ringer, director of the Kennedy Center for International Studies at Brigham Young University. "We can find sanctuary...in the open, loving arms of a Father in Heaven and a Savior who love us both for who we are and who we may become."

items.title: Jeffery A. Thompson | What Is Your Calling in Life?
items.description: Jeffery A. Thompson, associate professor in the Romney Institute of Public Management at Brigham Young University. "The grace of Christ...is what will guide us to our callings and enable us to excel in them."

items.title: Marilyn W. Berrett | Earnest Prayer
items.description: "Marilyn W. Berrett, professor of dance at Brigham Young University. ""I know that God hears and answers our prayers, and I testify that the act of praying changes us... This gesture of humility and reverence does so much for the one kneeling.""

items.title: Steven L. Taylor | The Sure Foundation
items.description: Steven L. Taylor, assistant dean of the College of Life Sciences at Brigham Young University. "Our true desires, priorities, and aspirations guide our lives now and will determine our future possibilities...[Christ] is the sure foundation."

items.title: Richard E. Bennett | Martin Harris and Three Wise Men
items.description: Richard E. Bennett, professor in the Department of Church History and Doctrine at Brigham Young University. "I... have chosen to see the hand of the Lord not only in our history but also in... new understandings of His handiwork in the Restoration."

items.title: Paul B. Farnsworth | Avoiding Spiritual Drift
items.description: Paul B. Farnsworth, professor in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at Brigham Young University. "The admonitions that we receive... can be viewed as reminders to regularly correct our courses by reference to divine standards."

items.title: David B. Paxman | Zoram and I: Getting Our Stories Straight
items.description: David B. Paxman, professor in the Department of English at Brigham Young University. "Zoram's life story is like all of ours. He could see God's providence or man's manipulation... his choice would influence his posterity far into the future."

items.title: Randal Day | The Sacred Matters
items.description: Randal Day, professor in the School of Family Life at Brigham Young University. “As we negotiate the challenging and dangerous paths of this life, we can draw on the power of the sacred, holy, divine, awe-inspiring, sanctified, and hallowed.”

items.title: Alton L. Thygerson | Saving Lives
items.description: Alton L. Thygerson, professor of health science at Brigham Young University. "Only Jesus can save us... To be saved by Jesus Christ means to be saved by the Atonement."

items.title: Russell C. Taylor | The Gardener of Gethsemane
items.description: Russell C. Taylor, department chair of the L. Tom Perry Special Collections. “If we are looking, we will see the caring hands of the Gardener of Gethsemane shaping our lives in ways we cannot now imagine.”

items.title: Claudio R. M. Costa (11-2-10)
items.description: Claudio R. M. Costa of the First Quorum of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I promise you that if you have faith in God, you will have the lighthouse of the gospel to help you and to bless your life.”

items.title: Cecilia M. Peek | “Yea, They May Forget, Yet Will I Not Forget Thee”
items.description: Cecilia M. Peek, associate professor of classics and ancient history in the Department of Humanities, Classics, and Comparative Literature at Brigham Young University. “I testify to you that you are His most important work.”

items.title: Elder Donald L. Hallstrom | The Heart and a Willing Mind
items.description: Elder Donald L. Hallstrom of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Both the heart and the mind must be fully engaged in this holy process.”

items.title: Elder Yoshihiko Kikuchi | How Do You Open Your Heart to Heaven?
items.description: Elder Yoshihiko Kikuchi of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “When you hold a personal morning devotional every day, I promise you again that your life will be changed.”

items.title: Andrew S. Gibbons | The Skills of a Saint
items.description: Andrew S. Gibbons, graduate research assistant at Brigham Young University. “Skilled performance is a very important manifestation of human knowledge. It is a kind of knowledge that improves with use.”

items.title: Len B. Novilla | Journey of the Soul, Anchors of the Heart
items.description: Len B. Novilla, associate professor in the department of health science at Brigham Young University. “Throughout the uncertainties of life, only Christ and His love are constant. There is no more perfect example of love than the Atonement itself.”

items.title: Elder Christoffel Golden Jr. | To Know Thee, the Only True God
items.description: Elder Christoffel Golden Jr. of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Because of the Restoration and… a true and fuller understanding of mankind’s origin and destiny, we know that we are not predestined to anything.”

items.title: James C. Brau | Spiritual Thoughts in the Classroom
items.description: James C. Brau, professor of finance at Brigham Young University. "I have made it a point to share a spiritual thought in each section I teach every day I am in the classroom.”

items.title: President Russell T. Osguthorpe | What If Love Were Our Only Motive?Russell T. Osguthorpe | What If Love Were Our Only Motive?
items.description: President Russell T. Osguthorpe, Sunday School general president of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “It’s important to remember that we should not try to judge another’s motives.”

items.title: James P. Porter | Receiving and Recognizing the Holy Ghost
items.description: James P. Porter, associate dean of the College of Life Sciences at Brigham Young University. “One of the most important skills we must learn in this life is to receive and recognize the quiet whisperings of the Spirit.”

items.title: Derek A. Marquis | “To Every Nation, Kindred, Tongue, and People”
items.description: Derek A. Marquis, managing director of BYU Broadcasting. “May we recognize a loving Heavenly Father’s hand in the miracles of the technologies around us and remember that He gave them to us to bless us and our families and to advance His purposes.”

items.title: Cory W. Leonard | By Persuasion, Longsuffering, Meekness, and Love
items.description: Cory W. Leonard, assistant director at the David M. Kennedy Center for International Studies at Brigham Young University. “Perhaps it is fear that limits much of our ability to listen, learn, persuade—and be persuaded—by others and by the Spirit.”

items.title: Ed Adams (5-10-11)
items.description: Ed Adams, dean of the College of Fine Arts and Communications. “My life was forever changed and set on a different trajectory, one other than where it could have headed.”

items.title: Parris K. Egbert | Confess the Lord’s Hand in All Things
items.description: Parris K. Egbert, chair of the computer science department at Brigham Young University. “As wonderful as modern technology is, it still pales in comparison to God’s power and ability. We get to view the wonders of the universe; He [creates] them.”

items.title: Larry L. Howell | Faith: An Essential Principle of the Gospel
items.description: Larry L. Howell, professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. “Eventually I will stand before the judgment bar of God. No one there is going to ask me what I did for a living… those things are going to be totally irrelevant.”

items.title: Val Jo Anderson | “Into the Burn!”
items.description: Val Jo Anderson, professor of plant and wildlife sciences at Brigham Young University. “Regardless of the trial or the setting, it is important to know in advance whom you trust and whom you will follow, even if it seems counterintuitive to you.”

items.title: Kent P. Jackson | Receiving
items.description: Kent P. Jackson, American scholar and professor of ancient scripture at Brigham Young University. “He stands at the door and knocks—sometimes in person and sometimes through the service of others.”

items.title: Brad Wilcox | His Grace Is Sufficient
items.description: Brad Wilcox of the Sunday School General Board of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Grace is not achieved somewhere down the road. It is received right here and right now. It is not a finishing touch; it is the Finisher’s touch.”

items.title: Douglas F. Prawitt | Line upon Line: Finding Joy in Progress
items.description: Douglas F. Prawitt, Professor of Accountancy. “May we openly and honestly acknowledge to ourselves and to God where we are in our own personal path of progress, wherever that may be.”

items.title: Janet B. Bradford | Carry On!
items.description: Janet B. Bradford, senior librarian at Brigham Young University’s Harold B. Lee Library. “No one else can do what you can do. Please do not compare yourselves to others. Rather, bloom where you’re planted!”

items.title: Elder Jay E. Jensen | Building upon the Rock
items.description: Elder Jay E. Jensen of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "I know that we will face both current and future storms successfully because of this rock which we build our lives, our faith, and our testimonies."

items.title: Ramona O. Hopkins | A Miracle in the Making: Finding the Meaning in Adversity
items.description: Ramona O. Hopkins, professor of psychology at Brigham Young University. “All of us will experience difficult challenges in life. How you deal with and overcome adversity is what is important.”

items.title: Gregory F. Burton | Lessons from Life’s Laboratory
items.description: Gregory F. Burton, chair of the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at Brigham Young University. “The experiences of my life… logically teach me of a loving Heavenly Father and Savior who are vitally interested in us.”

items.title: William G. Eggington | “Therefore Ye Are No More Strangers and Foreigners"
items.description: William G. Eggington, professor and chair of the Linguistics and English Language Department at Brigham Young University “...let me suggest that going into the world means righteously interacting closely and lovingly with all of God’s children.

items.title: Damon L. Bahr | The Unique Opportunities of Living at This Time in This Dispensation
items.description: Damon L. Bahr, associate professor of Religious Education. “We must stand with our arms open, ready to catch them, accepting the Lord’s invitation to ‘come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers [or catchers] of men.’”

items.title: Elder Tad R. Callister | Becoming Men and Women of Integrity
items.description: Elder Tad R. Callister of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “When all the scaffolding is removed, it is our integrity that both defines us and identifies us.”

items.title: President Cecil O. & Sharon Samuelson | "Be Ye Therefore Perfect" // Building Your Bridges
items.description: President Cecil O. and Sister Sharon G. Samuelson, President of Brigham Young University and his wife. “One can be fully worthy in a gospel sense and yet still be growing while dealing with personal imperfections.”

items.title: Elder Neil L. Andersen | Honesty—The Heart of Spirituality
items.description: Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “For a disciple of Christ, honesty is at the very heart of spirituality.”

items.title: President Thomas S. Monson | Be a Light to the World
items.description: President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “As you keep the flame of testimony burning brightly, you will become a beacon of righteousness—even a light—for all to see.”

items.title: President Cecil O. & Sister Sharon G. Samuelson | Why We Appreciate BYU
items.description: President Cecil O. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Sister Sharon G. Samuelson. “We love the Spirit of the Y. We know this means different things to different people.”

items.title: President Julie B. Beck | Why We Are Organized into Quorums and Relief Societies
items.description: President Julie B. Beck, General Relief Society President. “There is much work a quorum must do as a quorum and much a Relief Society is to do as a circle of sisters, and there is much that is to be coordinated between them.”

items.title: Michael L. Dunn | The Miracle of Forgiveness
items.description: Michael L. Dunn, chair of the Department of Nutrition, Dietetics, and Food Science at Brigham Young University. “There is no superhuman feat or great thing that we must do to receive God’s forgiveness.”

items.title: Tom Fletcher (2-7-12)
items.description: Thomas H. Fletcher, director of the Advanced Combustion Engineering Research Center (ACERC). “It is my prayer that we can all strive to be great at what we do but good at who we are.”

items.title: Elder Patrick Kearon | Messages of Love
items.description: Elder Patrick Kearon of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “His messages are often quiet, and we all know that we can miss them if we are not ready to receive.”

items.title: Dallan R. Moody | What Happens When Life Gets One Degree Colder?
items.description: Dallan R. Moody, associate athletic director of athletics at Brigham Young University. “Through our faith, courage, hope, and trust, God will bless us—no matter how cold our lives may feel. I know that God loves us.”

items.title: Elder Stanley G. Ellis | The Courage to Choose Wisely
items.description: Elder Stanley G. Ellis of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Choosing wisely is a critical part of His plan of happiness and an integral part of the test of our earth life.”

items.title: Amy Petersen Jensen | Some Hopeful Words on Media and Agency
items.description: Amy Petersen Jensen, associate dean in the College of Fine Arts and Communications at Brigham Young University. “The tools of technology that surround us are easily tasked to our benefit and refinement when they facilitate conversations.”

items.title: Thomas H. Morris | Time: A Precious Commodity; a Finite Resource
items.description: Thomas H. Morris, author and geologist. “I have found that on occasion it is healthy for me to step back and contemplate what I really want to gain from this life and the precious time that I have.”

items.title: John P. Hoffman | Prophet, Priest, and King
items.description: John P. Hoffman, professor in the Department of Sociology at Brigham Young University. “It is my desire that all of us may get to know the Savior better, including his roles as the perfect Prophet, Priest, and King.”

items.title: J. Michael Hunter | Small Things
items.description: J. Michael Hunter, chair of the Department of Religion and Family History at the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University. “There’s nothing negligible about the simple acts of kindness and assistance that you and I offer to those around us.”

items.title: Melissa Heath | Becoming More Teachable
items.description: Melissa Heath, associate professor of Counseling Psychology and Special Education at Brigham Young University. “When we are teachable, the Holy Ghost bears witness of truth and we increase in knowledge and wisdom.”

items.title: Stanley A. Johnson | The Simpleness of the Way
items.description: Stanley A. Johnson, teaching professor of Ancient Scripture at Brigham Young University. “If a prophet of God tells us we can look upon the brazen serpent and be healed, then we can look upon the brazen serpent and be healed.”

items.title: Douglas R. McKinlay | The Approachable Master
items.description: Douglas R. McKinlay, associate professor of Advertising in the Department of Communications at Brigham Young University. “I testify that as we boldly approach Him, our own personal performance becomes our own personal legacy.”

items.title: D. Gordon Smith | What’s in a Name?
items.description: D. Gordon Smith, associate dean at BYU’s J. Reuben Clark Law School. “I have sometimes thought of the experience of changing my name in relation to my baptism—an ordinance in which I took upon myself the name of Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Patricia Ravert | Persistence, Patience, and Posies
items.description: Patricia Ravert, dean of the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. “I urge you to be persistent and persevere and exercise patience to find your plan and reach your goals.”

items.title: Donald W. Parry | Angels, Chariots, and the Lord of Hosts
items.description: Donald W. Parry, member of the International Team of Translators of the Dead Sea Scrolls. “Angels can move about the earth conducting the Lord’s divine work, and they serve, minister, and mingle among mortals, usually without our awareness.”

items.title: Elder Tad R. Callister | Our Identity and Our Destiny
items.description: Elder Tad R. Callister of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I testify there are no ordinary people, no ciphers, no zeros—only potential gods and goddesses in our midst.”

items.title: Cecil O. Samuelson | Character/ Sharon G. Samuelson | Beware the Dragons
items.description: President Cecil O. & Sister Sharon G. Samuelson of Brigham Young University. "Hold on to the iron rod...it is your only way to have sure footings as you make your way on the roadways of life."

items.title: Elder Steven E. Snow | Stepping-Stones and Stumbling Blocks
items.description: Elder Steven E. Snow of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “You will avoid many stumbling blocks by living wise, obedient lives and by paying attention to the stepping-stones that will build your faith.”

items.title: T. Jeffrey Wilks | Optimism and Joy in the Gospel of Jesus Christ
items.description: T. Jeffrey Wilks, former director of the School of Accountancy at Brigham Young University. “Never give up. Do all things cheerfully that lie in your power, and then stand still with the assurance that God will help you.”

items.title: Ray L. Huntington | A Grateful Heart
items.description: Ray L. Huntington, professor of Ancient Scripture at Brigham Young University. “May we have hearts that can feel, ears that can hear, and eyes that can see our blessings and live in continual gratitude toward God and those around us.”

items.title: James R. Rasband | Faith to Forgive Grievous Harms: Accepting the Atonement as Restitution
items.description: James R. Rasband, dean of the J. Reuben Clark Law School at Brigham Young University. “...to have saving power—our faith in Christ and His Atonement must include both His power to pay for our sins and His power to pay for the sins of others.”

items.title: Paul V. Johnson | Free to Choose Liberty or Captivity
items.description: Paul V. Johnson, commissioner of the Church Educational System of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Individually we can be free from any power the adversary would like to have over us by living righteously.”

items.title: Nancy Wentworth | Our Eternal Education
items.description: Nancy Wentworth, Chair of the Department of Teacher Education at Brigham Young University. “Our eternal education begins with an understanding of where we have come from, why we are here, and where we are going after this life.”

items.title: Elder Bruce D. Porter | "Did You Think to Pray?"
items.description: Elder Bruce D. Porter of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I am deeply thankful for the gift of prayer, which is surely among the greatest of gifts given by our Father in Heaven to His children on earth.”

items.title: President Cecil O. & Sharon G. Samuelson | The Lord’s Hand in Our Lives
items.description: President Cecil O. Samuelson and Sharon G. Samuelson, president and his wife of Brigham Young University. "We know that God lives and loves us and will guide, correct, and direct us if we are willing to have Him do so."

items.title: President Elaine S. Dalton | Prophetic Priorities and Dedicated Disciples
items.description: President Elaine S. Dalton, Young Women general president of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “You have been reserved to be here now on account of your exceeding faith in the premortal existence in our Heavenly Father’s plan.”

items.title: David Rolph Seely | Created in the “Image and Likeness of God”: Apprentices in the Master’s Workshop
items.description: David Rolph Seely, religion professor of Brigham Young University's Jerusalem Center. “As we help the Master with His masterpieces, we are engaged in His work and His glory: ‘the immortality and eternal life of man.’”

items.title: Janie Penfield | Live Your Life with Purpose
items.description: Janie Penfield, associate athletic director and senior woman administrator at Brigham Young University. “We can live our life with purpose—the purpose to gain eternal life and be counted as a disciple of Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Elder Donald L. Hallstrom | Living a Reverent Life
items.description: Elder Donald L. Hallstrom of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “My aspiration is for each of us to want to live a more reverent life—a life reflective of our love for God the Eternal Father and Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Gordon E. Limb | Recognizing and Responding to the Promptings of the Spirit
items.description: Gordon E. Limb, director of the School of Social Work in the College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences at Brigham Young University. “As we learn to better recognize and respond to the promptings of the Spirit, we will find answers to our prayers”

items.title: President Rosemary M. Wixom | The Covenant Path
items.description: President Rosemary M. Wixom, Primary General President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We are a making-and-keeping-covenants people, and nothing better shapes us than the sacred covenants we make to the Lord.”

items.title: James D. Gordon III | The Joy of Education and Lifelong Learning
items.description: James D. Gordon III, professor of Law at the J. Reuben Clark Law School. “If we do our best and seek Heavenly Father’s help, He will strengthen us beyond our natural abilities and help us to learn.”

items.title: Michelle Marchant | “My Life Is a Gift; My Life Has a Plan”
items.description: Michelle Marchant, associate professor in the Department of Counseling Psychology and Special Education at Brigham Young University. “The Lord knows you by name. He is so eager to share His infinite love with you.”

items.title: Ryan Holmes | The Truth of All Things
items.description: Ryan Holmes, director of digital media for BYU Broadcasting. “I am worried that the companionship we have with our smartphones is competing with the companionship of the Holy Ghost.”

items.title: Gary E. Arnoldson | The M&M’s of Missionary-Minded Members
items.description: Gary E. Arnoldson, controller for the McKay School of Education at Brigham Young University. “Missionary work is exactly what it is: hard, scary, consuming, exciting, fulfilling, and many other words.”

items.title: Larry Tucker | The Human Body: A Gift and a Responsibility
items.description: Larry Tucker, professor of health science at Brigham Young University. “Our bodies are sacred temples, worthy of special care and respect. Sacrifice is required to keep our temples in good condition. Do not give up.”

items.title: Kelly D. Patterson | Wandering and Wondering
items.description: Kelly D. Patterson, professor in the Department of Political Science at Brigham Young University. “We can creatively use the examples of wandering and wondering to blaze a reliable and exhilarating path back into the presence of our Heavenly Father.”

items.title: Brian Santiago | Safely on the Lord’s Side
items.description: Brian Santiago, senior associate athletic director at Brigham Young University. “Each one of us has the opportunity to join a winning team by being full of integrity, following the promptings of the Holy Ghost, and persevering.”

items.title: D. Kelly Ogden | The Miracle of Repentance
items.description: D. Kelly Ogden, professor emeritus of ancient scripture at Brigham Young University. “Whatever your past has been, your future is spotless, so tie yourself to your potential, not to your past.”

items.title: Tyler J. Jarvis | “That’s How the Light Gets In”
items.description: Tyler J. Jarvis, professor of mathematics at Brigham Young University. “The realities of living in our limited, imperfect world mean that we have no choice but to make do with an approximation—to admit and accept imperfection.”

items.title: Gary C. Barton | The Light Through the Dark Glass
items.description: Gary C. Barton, associate dean in the College of Fine Arts and Communications at Brigham Young University. “As we repent, are faithful…the path that leads us to the presence of our Heavenly Father will be illuminated.”

items.title: Curt Holman | Raising Your Ebenezer: A Monument to Remember
items.description: Curt Holman, associate professor in the Department of Dance at Brigham Young University. “We will raise our own Ebenezers—our own stones of remembrance—that will enable us to see God’s hand in our past.”

items.title: Kristin L. Matthews | The Worth of Souls Is Great
items.description: Kristin L. Matthews, associate professor of English and coordinator of the American Studies Program at Brigham Young University. “I hope you know that you are above and beyond those false measures of worth that we humans have created.”

items.title: Elder M. Russell Ballard | “Let Us Think Straight”
items.description: Elder M. Russell Ballard Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Sisters, your sphere of influence is a unique sphere—one that cannot be duplicated by men.”

items.title: President Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson | Failure and Success // Shall I Laugh or Shall I Cry?
items.description: President Cecil O. Samuelson of Brigham Young University and wife Sharon G. Samuelson. “Personal growth comes from being stretched, and you will likely find yourselves challenged in ways you have never previously experienced or expected.”

items.title: Elder Lynn G. Robbins | “Avoid It”
items.description: Elder Lynn G. Robbins of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “...one of life’s most helpful guiding principles: It is easier to avoid temptation than it is to resist temptation.”

items.title: Neal L. Cox | “And They Did Fellowship One with Another”
items.description: Neal L. Cox, associate dean of students at Brigham Young University. “I testify that this is true and rejoice in the many students who have discovered this emancipating principle of the gospel of Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Peggy H. Anderson | The Lord Desires Your Success
items.description: Peggy H. Anderson, professor in the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. “He desires your success in all aspects of your life—in your profession, in your education, in your family, in your relationships. The Lord desires your success.”

items.title: Elder Ulisses Soares | Becoming a Work of Art
items.description: Elder Ulisses Soares of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “It is possible to reject the temptations in our lives and develop the attributes of Christ—if and only if we hold onto the iron rod.”

items.title: C. Shane Reese | On the Measurements We Make in Life
items.description: C. Shane Reese, professor of statistics at Brigham Young University. “I pray that we will all be a little more fair in our measurements of ourselves and a little more patient in our measurements of others.”

items.title: Bishop Gérald Caussé | “For When I Am Weak, Then Am I Strong"
items.description: Bishop Gérald Caussé, Presiding Bishop of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “You will have the ability to meet the challenges you will face in your life. With Paul you will be able to say, ‘For when I am weak, then am I strong.’”

items.title: Scott E. Ferrin | Christmas and Christ’s Invitation to Become as a Little Child: What Manner of Child Ought We to Be?
items.description: Scott E. Ferrin, professor and graduate coordinator in the Department of Educational Leader­ship and Foundations at Brigham Young University. “May we trust our Father and develop the childlike attributes Christ and our prophet exemplify.”

items.title: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson | “Why We Do Some of the Things We Do
items.description: Cecil O. and Sharon G. Samuelson, president of Brigham Young University and his wife. “BYU is a great institution established by the Lord’s prophets to fulfill sacred purposes. It is prospered under the hand of heaven.”

items.title: Bishop Gary E. Stevenson | “Lean Not unto Thine Own Understanding”
items.description: Bishop Gary E. Stevenson, Presiding Bishop of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I have great expectations for each of you, as does the Lord.”

items.title: Jonathan G. Sandberg | Healing = Courage + Action + Grace
items.description: Jonathan G. Sandberg, professor in the School of Family Life at Brigham Young University. “Healing is much more than ‘getting better’ or ‘having our problems go away.’ Healing is growth, development, and maturation. In a word, healing is change.”

items.title: Elder Anthony D. Perkins | “Nevertheless I Went Forth”
items.description: Elder Anthony D. Perkins of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Be confident that the Savior will fulfill His promise to lead you along to an abundant life, even when the immediate path sometimes seems uncertain.”

items.title: Suzanne Julian | Led by the Spirit
items.description: Suzanne Julian, Instructio Coordinator for the Harold B. Lee Library of Brigham Young University. “Our faith and His love will help us succeed when the hard things we are asked to do seem impossible.”

items.title: Jane H. Lassetter | “Lead Me, Guide Me, Walk Beside Me”: Life Lessons with the Holy Ghost
items.description: Jane H. Lassetter, associate professor of nursing at Brigham Young University. “Live your life in a way that invites His presence and helps you sense His tender whispers.”

items.title: Elder Larry M. Gibson | Following Heavenly Father’s Plan
items.description: Elder Larry M. Gibson, 1st Counselor in the Young Men's General Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Heavenly Father believes in plans. He has a plan for the salvation of His children—a specific plan just for you.”

items.title: Chad W. Lewis (3-25-14)
items.description: Chad Lewis, associate athletic director of development. “People will love to hear your stories. Don’t be afraid to reach out and share them. Your stories did not just happen for you; they are meant to be shared.”

items.title: Lawrence C. Walters | Citizenship
items.description: Lawrence C. Walters, professor of public management at Brigham Young University. “Active engagement in the functioning of government and in addressing community concerns is an inherent responsibility of our citizenship and demands our best efforts.”

items.title: Steven M. Glover | “The Assurance of Things Hoped For”
items.description: Steven M. Glover, professor and associate dean of the BYU Marriott School of Management. “It is said that when we wish to communicate with God, we do so through prayer, and when God wishes to communicate with us, it is often through the scriptures.”

items.title: Trenton L. Hickman | Weaknesses Into Strength in Our Search for Knowledge
items.description: Trenton L. Hickman, associate professor of English at Brigham Young University. “The Spirit can also give me the knowledge and language that I need in unexpected, even extemporaneous, moments when I need to be wise beyond my own previous capacity.”

items.title: Brent E. Nelson | “I Know That He Loveth His Children . . .”
items.description: Brent E. Nelson, member in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Brigham Young University. “The Lord has provided me some specific tender mercies over the years to give me comfort and at least partial answers to these questions.”

items.title: Alexander L. Baugh | Joseph Smith: Seer, Translator, Revelator, and Prophet
items.description: Alexander L. Baugh, professor of Church history and doctrine at Brigham Young University. “Joseph Smith’s life exemplified the role of what a prophet was, is, and should be.”

items.title: James L. Slaughter | The Blessings of Choice
items.description: James L. Slaughter, Chaplain of Brigham Young University. “I hope we can all be happy with who we are and who we are becoming. I like ‘me,’ and I hope to like myself even better as I become a better version of me.”

items.title: R. Bruce Money | The Lord’s Country and Kingdom—Your Passport
items.description: R. Bruce Money, professor of Marketing and International Business at Brigham Young University. “Do not ever let your passport to the Lord’s country and kingdom lapse. If you do, you will find yourself outside its borders.”

items.title: Sherri Patten Palmer | Convenient Service
items.description: Sherri Patten Palmer, associate teaching professor in the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. “Even though there are material inequalities in the world, we all can have the righteous desire to serve.”

items.title: William B. Lund | For God So Loved You
items.description: William B. Lund, Associate University Librarian for Information Technology at Brigham Young University. “We aren’t specks in the universal expanse of God’s creations but individuals loved and cherished by God.”

items.title: Elder David A. Bednar (8-19-14)
items.description: David A. Bednar addresses BYU students with a speech titled "To Sweep the Earth as with a Flood."

items.title: Elder Dale G. Renlund | Constructing Spiritual Stability
items.description: Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The commandments are not intended to restrict us. Rather, obedience leads to increased spiritual stability and long-term happiness.”

items.title: Dan Clark | The Four Steps on the Stairway to Heaven
items.description: Dan Clark, CEO of Clark Success Systems. “So the question isn’t ‘are you going to crash and burn every once in a while?’ Of course you are—you are human!.. The question is, ‘what are you going to do about it?’”

items.title: Mark Alden Callister | Lost and Found
items.description: Mark Alden Callister, Professor in the Department of Communications at Brigham Young University. “I believe that if you will reflect for just a moment on the loving service you receive from others, you will see the workings of the Lord.”

items.title: Elder David F. Evans | Tenacity
items.description: Elder David F. Evans, General Authority Seventy for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “There is nothing more invigorating than knowing what you should do and then getting about doing it.”

items.title: Scott Swofford | Both Feet Forward
items.description: Scott Swofford, Television Series (Granite Flats) and Movie Executive Producer. “Clearly, weakness and the recognition of it, the humility that follows, and the application of faith in Christ are essential to our eternal progression.”

items.title: Elder Erich W. Kopischke | What Do You Envision in Life?
items.description: Elder Erich W. Kopischke of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I pray the blessings of heaven on you as you ponder these questions and strive to obtain sacred and eternal blessings.”

items.title: Lloyd D. Newell | Fear Not
items.description: Lloyd D. Newell, host of Music & the Spoken Word. “The Lord’s message to you today is the same message He sent through His angels so long ago: ‘Fear not.’ He can say that because He knows more than we do.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | Successfully Failing: Pursuing Our Quest for Perfection / Peggy S. Worthen | An Unexpected Path
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen. "Because of the Atonement, all failures are changeable and temporary, except the one that occurs when we give up. So whatever you do, don't you dare give up."

items.title: Elder Don R. Clarke | Pure Religion
items.description: Elder Don R. Clarke of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “If you want to be happy, feel the Holy Ghost, and grow closer to the Savior, then practice pure religion.”

items.title: Todd B. Parker | “True Doctrine, Understood, Changes Attitudes and Behavior”
items.description: Todd B. Parker, professor in the Department of Ancient Scripture at Brigham Young University. “My challenge to you is to study the scriptures daily, draw upon the word daily, let the words of Christ tell you all things that you should do.”

items.title: Sister Cheryl A. Esplin | The Abundant Life
items.description: Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, Second Counselor in the General Primary Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Everything the Savior did and said was for the benefit of humankind.”

items.title: David W. Hart | Be Excellent: Becoming Who You Are in Today’s World
items.description: David W. Hart, Associate Professor at the Marriott School of Management. “Spend your time here at BYU learning about who you really are and preparing yourselves to have an impact on the world. Then go and do. Be excellent and make a difference.”

items.title: Jennifer B. Nielson | Experiment and Experience
items.description: Jennifer B. Nielson, Chemistry Professor at Brigham Young University. “If we are not afraid, our life experiments can be tools to learn truth and to make changes.”

items.title: Kent F. Richards | Lessons from the Savior’s Young Adult Life
items.description: Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Do your very best, and the Lord will honor your efforts.”

items.title: "Carl Hernandez III | Devoted Discipleship "
items.description: Carl Hernandez III, professor of Law at the J. Reuben Clark Law School at Brigham Young University. “The first step on the pathway to devoted discipleship is to exercise faith in the Savior’s power to lift us to higher ground.”

items.title: Michael D. Brown | “The Lord Looketh on the Heart”
items.description: Michael D. Brown, professor of Cell Biology at Brigham Young University. “Just as a reliable physical heart is needed to provide nourishment to our physical bodies, a reliable spiritual heart is needed to provide nourishment to our spirits.”

items.title: Casey C. Peterson | Dally Up: Finding Our Anchor in Turbulent Times
items.description: Casey C. Peterson, Associate Dean of Students at Brigham Young University. “I am grateful to work with students who are striving to dally up to the power of service, involvement, and commitments during turbulent times in their lives.”

items.title: Kerry M. Muhlestein | Why We Must Be Wholeheartedly Holy
items.description: Kerry M. Muhlestein, Director of Research in the Department of Ancient Scripture at Brigham Young University. “With His help, eventually we will become the kinds of beings who are capable of thinking and feeling just as He does.”

items.title: Michael Middleton | Adding Stars to Your Life’s Sky
items.description: Michael Middleton, Assistant Athletic Director of Athletics at Brigham Young University. “Individually and collectively our destiny lies in the ability to connect the points of light in our lives so that we can see the broad patterns of eternity.”

items.title: Diane Strong-Krause | Be Anchored in Order to Soar
items.description: Diane Strong-Krause, associate professor and Chair of the Department of Linguistics and English Language at Brigham Young University. “Understanding your true self allows you to see others as spiritual beings of great worth.”

items.title: E. Jeffrey Hill | Money Matters: Living Joyfully Within Your Means
items.description: E. Jeffrey Hill, professor of Family Life at Brigham Young University. "Will we choose to waste our resources upon transitory pleasures, or will we choose to serve others and build up the kingdom of God?"

items.title: Sondra Heaston | Keeping Your Fingers on the PULSE of Service
items.description: Sondra Heaston, associate professor in the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. “When we serve our family, friends, and neighbors, we help those who are in need. As we emulate the Savior, we become more like Him.”

items.title: Mark B. Colton | Never Give Up on Your Testimony of the Gospel
items.description: Mark B. Colton, professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Brigham Young University. “Can you imagine what your testimony would be like if you fought for it with the same tenacity with which you fight for other things in life?”

items.title: Jennifer Paustenbaugh | When Your Bow Breaks
items.description: Jennifer Paustenbaugh, University Librarian at the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University. “We can trust in Heavenly Father that the growth we experience at the points at which our bows break will bring the miracle of blessings.”

items.title: Barry Willardson | Strangers and Pilgrims on the Earth
items.description: Barry Willardson, professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry at Brigham Young University. “Sometimes small flaws can put our lives out of focus and we cannot see our divine origins.”

items.title: Claudine Bigelow | Creativity
items.description: Claudine Bigelow, Member of the Deseret String Quartet and Professor of Viola at the Brigham Young University School of Music. “Inviting creativity into your professional and private lives is worth searching and striving for; don’t ever give up.”

items.title: Elder Neil L. Andersen | A Compensatory Spiritual Power for the Righteous
items.description: Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “If we unexpectedly face jagged rocks and uneven cliffs, each needs his or her own lantern to light the path.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | Building Character / Peggy S. Worthen | Which Way Are You Swimming?
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen. "It is important to keep a proper focus even when things are not going as planned...it is important to continue to progress toward our goals."

items.title: Elder Ronald A. Rasband | Religious Freedom and Fairness for All
