items.description: Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Your example of respect and fairness will open doors and create meaningful friendships that you will cherish throughout your life.”

items.title: Edward Eyestone | Following Worthy Mentors
items.description: Ed Eyestone, Director of Track and Field at Brigham Young University. “May we not just take direction but may we take direction well, without taking offense.”

items.title: Sterling C. Hilton | His Burden Is Light
items.description: Sterling C. Hilton, Chair of the Depart­ment of Educational Leadership and Foundations at Brigham Young University. “Like a powerful spotlight that shines more brightly in complete darkness, our suffering reveals Christ to us.”

items.title: Dean M. Davies | God Will Use You, God Will Bless You
items.description: Elder Dean M. Davies of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “He needs you to incline your hearts to Him and seek to honor Him by serving Him and reaching out in compassion to those around you.”

items.title: "Leslee Thorne-Murphy | “Peace I Leave with You” "
items.description: Leslee Thorne-Murphy, Associate Professor and Associate Chair of the Department of English at Brigham Young University. “Christ’s peace resides in one’s heart. It is a spiritual peace that quells fear and anxiety.”

items.title: Larry Y. Wilson | The Return of the King
items.description: Elder Larry Y. Wilson of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Make your choice… to use your time in the cause that matters most—the one that leads to the millennial reign of Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Bonnie Brinton Anderson | Cybersecurity and Spiritual Safety
items.description: Bonnie Brinton Anderson, director of Master of Information Systems Management at Brigham Young University. “The same way that keeping your software current helps keep you safe… keeping your temple recommend current helps keep you spiritually safe.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | “It Is Not Good That . . . Man Should Be Alone” / Peggy S. Worthen | The Allegory of the Wedding Cake
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen. “Sometimes the result will not be what we have expected, but the process itself is important.”

items.title: Elder Allan F. Packer | Finding Your Way
items.description: Elder Allan F. Packer of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We can safely travel life’s journey by relying on the maps of the scriptures, the words of the living prophets, and the compass of the Holy Ghost.”

items.title: Scott C. Esplin | “Daddy, Is Jesus Real?” Overcoming Fear through Faith in Christ
items.description: Scott C. Esplin, Associate Professor in the Department of Church History and Doctrine at Brigham Young University. “Part of becoming like and returning to our Heavenly Father… includes believing in Him both as we repent and after.”

items.title: Marcus B. Nash | Guided Safely Home
items.description: Elder Marcus B. Nash of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The Savior reminded him that belief, or faith, was key. Said He, ‘If thou canst believe, all things are ­possible to him that believeth.’”

items.title: Rickelle Richards | Beauties of the Earth
items.description: Rickelle Richards, associate professor of Dietetics at Brigham Young University. “God’s beauties of the earth are all around us and He wants us to find them and feel gratitude for them.”

items.title: Larry R. Lawrence | Choose Happiness
items.description: Elder Larry R. Lawrence of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “There are going to be both smooth days and rough days throughout our lives, but the Lord has commanded us repeatedly to ‘be of good cheer.’”

items.title: Jennifer Rockwood | Drawn to the Light
items.description: Jennifer Rockwood, Head Coach of the Women’s Soccer Team at Brigham Young University. “Are you lighting the way for others? Are you an example of the Savior in your words, thoughts, and actions?”

items.title: Jeffery N. Bunker | Of Starfish and Destinies
items.description: Jeffery N. Bunker, Associate Executive Director of Student Academic and Advisement Services at Brigham Young University. “Having pure, positive, and appropriate thoughts will affect all aspects of your life.”

items.title: Stephen W. Liddle | “Without Compulsory Means”
items.description: Stephen W. Liddle, professor of information systems at the Marriott School of Management at Brigham Young University. “I pray that each one of us will be able to find joy in learning ‘without compulsory means.’”

items.title: Rebecca Schroeder | Being in Tune: Minimizing Interference Beats
items.description: Rebecca Schroeder, Acquisitions Librarian and Department Chair of the Material Acquisitions Department at Brigham Young University. “To be in tune with our Heavenly Father, we have to find a way to see the truth we share and work toward peace.”

items.title: Blake E. Peterson | Do We Really Believe?
items.description: Blake E. Peterson, professor in the Department of Mathematics Education at Brigham Young University. “While you are waiting for your answers to come, live the gospel in a way that allows those around you to know what you really believe.”

items.title: Sarah M. Coyne | The Fantasy and the Reality of Your Royal Identity
items.description: Sarah M. Coyne, associate professor of Human Development at Brigham Young University. “We have the potential to have greater power and reach than the most powerful superhero portrayed in the media today.”

items.title: Alan R. Harker | Hope As an Anchor of Our Souls
items.description: Alan R. Harker, associate Academic Vice President for Research and Graduate Studies at Brigham Young University. “Just as hope is not the same as wishing, neither are anchors dead weight meant to slow us down or impede our progress.”

items.title: Michelle Stott James | Empty Centers and the Fire of the Lord
items.description: Michelle Stott James, professor of German and Russian at Brigham Young University. “Our service to God’s children is a visible sign of our love for Him. As we willingly serve others, we become a conduit through which His love flows.”

items.title: Timothy W. McLain | Navigating Our Way Through Life
items.description: Timothy W. McLain, professor of mechanical engineering at Brigham Young University. “It is my belief that we can obtain… celestial glory as we seek and follow the divine feedback that comes through the still, small voice of the Holy Ghost.”

items.title: Michael A. Goodman | Become a Seeker: The Way, the Truth, and the Life
items.description: Michael A. Goodman, associate professor of Church history and doctrine at Brigham Young University. “Do not fear to ask questions and to be a seeker. Do not fear that God or His gospel cannot stand up to scrutiny.”

items.title: Wade J. Hollingshaus | “On Earth”
items.description: Wade J. Hollingshaus, Chair of the Department of Theatre and Media Arts at Brigham Young University. “It is essential to the exaltation of each and every one of us that we pass through this fallen condition.”

items.title: David H. Moore | Watchmen on the Tower
items.description: David H. Moore, Associate Dean and Professor of J. Reuben Clark Law School. “Our responsibility to watch involves more than merely registering the signs that precede the Savior’s coming. It includes preparing ­ourselves for that coming.”

items.title: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland | Religion: Bound by Loving Ties
items.description: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The link between the highest in us and our highest hopes for others. That is why religion ­matters.”

items.title: Kevin J and Peggy S Worthen | A Graduate Program of Real Consequence: The Role of the Law School at BYU // Choose to Be a Leader
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, President Kevin J Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen. “Lifelong learning, an attribute law school helps us develop, is—in my view—a celestial attribute."

items.title: Elder Dallin H. Oaks | Elections, Hope, and Freedom
items.description: Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We must strive for mutual understanding and treat all with goodwill…We must, above all, trust in God and His promises.”

items.title: David C. Dollahite | Receiving the Eternal
items.description: David C. Dollahite, Professor of Family Life at Brigham Young University. “My friends, wherever you find yourself spiritually, I say to you in love and humility: I know that God lives and will answer your sincere prayers.”

items.title: David M. Whitchurch | Orson Hyde, the Holy Land, and Brigham Young University
items.description: David M. Whitchurch, Associate Professor of Ancient Scripture at Brigham Young University. “In the garden is a sign that reads, ‘Pray for the peace of Jerusalem’—a quote from Psalm 122:6. And so we must. We must hope for and pray for peace.”

items.title: Matthew O. Richardson | Stand Up Straight, Smile, and Remember Who You Are
items.description: Matthew O. Richardson, Advancement Vice President of Brigham Young University. “I testify that if you seek help and invite others into your life, then your life will be fuller, your success will be more meaningful, and you will find peace.”

items.title: Jodi Maxfield | Listen, Lift, Rescue
items.description: Jodi Maxfield, Artistic Director of the BYU Cougarettes. “Our Savior gave us the perfect example of love, compassion, respite, and rescue. He has beckoned us to come unto Him, to be His hands, and to love one another.”

items.title: President Bonnie L. Oscarson | Lessons from Joseph Smith
items.description: President Bonnie L. Oscarson, Young Women General President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I testify that from Joseph’s life we can learn many important gospel lessons to inspire and guide our lives.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | The Pursuit of All Truth / Peggy S. Worthen | A Safe Place
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife Peggy S. Worthen. “He is a careful and empathetic listener. Our communications with Him are safe. And He can help us develop the skills we need to communicate effectively.”

items.title: Elder Douglas D. Holmes | The Doctrine of Christ: Our Daily Walk
items.description: Elder Douglas D. Holmes of the Young Men General Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I invite you to be serious about your study of God and your pursuit to truly know Him.”

items.title: Craig Manning | The Power of Your Words
items.description: Craig Manning, Performance Psychology Consultant for BYU Athletics. “I have since learned that dwelling obsessively on what we do wrong is one of the greatest sources of interference to maximizing our potential. Self-doubt is dangerous.”

items.title: Elder Quentin L. Cook | A Banquet of Consequences: The Cumulative Result of All Choices
items.description: Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “As Latter-day Saints, we must be at the forefront of changing hearts and minds on the importance of children.”

items.title: Cassy Budd | On Failing and Finishing
items.description: Cassy Budd, Professor of the School of Accountancy. “Making mistakes is simply part of the human condition and can be one of your most productive learning tools.”

items.title: Elder Weatherford T. Clayton | The Rock of Our Redeemer
items.description: Elder Weatherford T. Clayton of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “If we have true faith in our Redeemer, we do something about it, because we have real intent.”

items.title: Keith Vorkink | Real Causes and Real Effects
items.description: Keith Vorkink, Professor in the BYU Marriott School of Management. “There is no information unobserved by or omitted from the Lord, and His love for us is not dependent on how perfect we appear on Instagram.”

items.title: Erin Kramer Holmes | Waiting upon the Lord: The Antidote to Uncertainty
items.description: Erin Kramer Holmes, BYU Professor in the School of Family Life. “In essence, uncertainty is a reflection of the gap between our desire for the ideal and our experience of reality.”

items.title: Eric Gillett | Testimony and Other “Wicked” Problems
items.description: Eric Gillett, BYU Professor of Graphic Design. “Embrace doubt and uncertainty as essential elements in problem solving. Let them motivate you to seek greater understanding.”

items.title: McKay Christensen | “Lay Hold upon the Word”: The Power of Wholehearted Living
items.description: McKay Christensen, Managing Director of Alumni and External Relations. “When you leave here today, look for ways you can lay hold upon the word. By doing so you will lay hold upon every good gift that our Heavenly Father has prepared for you.”

items.title: Keith J. Wilson | B-Y-You Matter to Him
items.description: Keith J. Wilson, Professor of Ancient Scripture. “President Monson spoke undeniable truth when he said, ‘One day, when we look back at seeming coincidences of our lives, we will realize that perhaps they weren’t so coincidental after all.’”

items.title: Diane Thueson Reich | On Change and Becoming: Thoughts from a Reluctant Grower
items.description: Diane Thueson Reich, Associate Professor from the School of Music. “I cannot fully take advantage of the Atonement of Jesus Christ when I fear or when I am unwilling, because then I am doubting our Savior and the power of His Atonement.”

items.title: Ray T. Clifford | Language Learning: A Truly Educational Experience
items.description: Ray T. Clifford, Director of the BYU Center for Language Studies. “In my experience, for an activity to build character it must be inherently good, it must require concerted effort, and it must demand perseverance over an extended period of time.”

items.title: Eva Witesman | Women and Education: “A Future Only God Could See for You”
items.description: Eva Witesman, Associate Professor of the BYU Marriott School of Business. “Women’s stories are powerful, and they haven’t always been told. So I am going to tell you a little bit of mine.”

items.title: Paul Caldarella | The Call of the Lord
items.description: Paul Caldarella, Associate Professor of the McKay School of Education. “Often the Lord calls us to do difficult things that we may not be sure we want to do but that will bring great blessings.”

items.title: Kirt R. Saville | Living a Life of Service and Love: What Goes Around Comes Around
items.description: Kirt R. Saville, Director of the BYU School of Music. “Christ most often blessed others when He was on His way to do something else.”

items.title: Gayla M. Sorenson | “To Me He Doth Not Stink”: Advocacy and Love
items.description: Gayla M. Sorenson, Dean of Admissions in the J. Reuben Clark Law School. “God will guide us as we develop our advocacy skills, and He will provide us with opportunities to be advocates for His children.”

items.title: Elder Lynn G. Robbins | Be 100 Percent Responsible
items.description: Elder Lynn G. Robins of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Agency and responsibility are inseparably connected. You cannot avoid responsibility without also diminishing agency.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | Fear Not / Peggy S. Worthen | Facing the Algebras of Life
items.description: Kevin J Worthen, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen. “You are more capable, more talented, and more faith-filled than you realize. More important, you are more loved by God than you realize.”

items.title: Elder Richard J. Maynes | Shape Your Life Through Service to Others
items.description: Elder Richard J. Maynes of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “When we speak of shaping our lives through service to others, we are really speaking of living a charitable, Christlike life.”

items.title: Elder Carl B. Cook | Putting Off the Natural Man and Becoming Saints
items.description: Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “It is humbling ourselves and putting God’s will above our own, seeking what He wants instead of what we want and aligning our will with His.”

items.title: Carolyn Billings | Are You All the Way In?
items.description: Carolyn Billings, Director of Sports Medicine at Brigham Young University. “If you will make sure that you are all the way in by trusting in the Lord, taking His yoke upon you, and following Him, then He will make you a conqueror.”

items.title: Elder Wilford W. Andersen | The Pride Cycle
items.description: Elder Wilford W. Andersen of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Recognize that all good things come from God. He is the source of every blessing you receive. Fill your heart with gratitude for His merciful kindness.”

items.title: Elder M. Russell Ballard | Questions and Answers
items.description: Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “He has given us His eternal plan, so ‘stay in the boat and hold on!’ We love you and we need you now and in the years to come.”

items.title: Elder Brian K. Ashton | Happiness, Deceit, and Small Things
items.description: Elder Brian K. Ashton, Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency. “True happiness comes from having the Spirit in our lives and cultivating an eternal perspective, and thus happiness is not dependent upon our circumstances.”

items.title: Elder D. Todd Christofferson | A Message at Christmas
items.description: Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “He opens the door to immortality and eternal life. It would be impossible to plumb the depths of His love.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | The Plan of Salvation: The Gospel Paradigm / Peggy S. Worthen | Lessons from Roses: Trust Yourself and Trust God
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, president of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen. “Once we understand the overall plan, it is easier to understand and obey the commandments.”

items.title: Elder LeGrand R. Curtis Jr. | Humbly Combining Heart and Mind
items.description: Elder LeGrand R. Curtis Jr. of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The fact that man does not comprehend all that God can comprehend should make us deeply humble before Him and willing to follow His counsel.”

items.title: Benjamin M. Ogles | Agency, Accountability, and the Atonement of Jesus Christ: Application to Sexual Assault
items.description: Benjamin M. Ogles, Dean of the College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences. “Only by uniting our voices and actions to assist victims and to promote respect for others can we help to end sexual violence.”

items.title: Elder S. Gifford Nielsen | Rise and Shout and Shine Forth!
items.description: Elder S. Gifford Nielsen of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I invite each of us to be a powerful influence for good. We have value. We have purpose. May we be the kind of living epistles our new prophet describes.”

items.title: Julie Crockett | Discovering Your Divine Individuality
items.description: Julie Crockett, Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. “We are supposed to be different! We were created as such for our individual growth and the growth of our friends and neighbors.”

items.title: Elder Ronald A. Rasband | Integrity of Heart
items.description: Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Integrity in business and in spiritual and family matters all draw from the same well of strength—our love for the Lord Jesus Christ.”

items.title: Elder Kim B. Clark | Embrace the Plan
items.description: Elder Kim B. Clark of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “My dear brothers and sisters, with all my heart I invite you to follow Jesus Christ and embrace Heavenly Father’s great plan of salvation.”

items.title: Michael J. Dorff | Seeing Things Differently
items.description: Michael J. Dorff, Department Chair of Mathematics. “Our Savior Jesus Christ sees us differently—not as we currently are but as we may become.”

items.title: Elder Neil L. Anderson | A Holier Approach to Ministering
items.description: Elder Neil L. Anderson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Caring for others, physically and emotionally, requires an unselfish and sensitive heart. It is an important part of the gospel.”

items.title: Robert T. Barrett | Illuminated Stories
items.description: Robert T. Barrett, Professor of Illustration in the BYU Department of Design. “Stories are a way to preserve our history and culture, passing it along to the next generation in a form that is easy for others to remember.”

items.title: Brianna M. Magnusson | Revealing Questions
items.description: Brianna M. Magnusson, Associate Professor in the College of Life Sciences at BYU. “We dislike the feeling of not knowing because we feel vulnerable. Yet this vulnerability can actually be a sacred space.”

items.title: Michael R. Orme | Recognizing and Understanding the Spirit at BYU
items.description: Michael R. Orme, BYU General Counsel. “Understanding the nuances of how we communicate with God through the Holy Ghost is a lifetime challenge.”

items.title: Beth Luthy | The Faith to Do His Will
items.description: Beth Luthy, Professor of Nursing. Though it is not always easy, God expects us to trust in Him. Beth Luthy shares how having the faith to do His will caused miracles to happen in her life.

items.title: Steven L. Shumway | Keeping the Spiritual Lifeblood Flowing
items.description: Steven L. Shumway, Professor in the Technology and Engineering Studies Program. “Like walking when your legs are frozen, sometimes what we least want to do is the very thing we need to keep our spiritual lifeblood flowing.”

items.title: Denise Stephens | Finding Your Place in the Universe
items.description: Denise Stephens, Professor of Astronomy. “Never forget to look up. He is there, and He is waiting for you, and He will help you find your place in this universe.”

items.title: Jeffrey S. McClellan | "Thy Troubles to Bless"
items.description: Jeffrey S. McClellan, Director of BYU Publications and Graphics. “As the song says, we lean for repose on Jesus, who will not desert us to our foes, though all hell may shake around us.”

items.title: Lori L. Wadsworth | Seeing the Divinity in Others
items.description: Lori L. Wadsworth, MPA Director, Professor of Public Management. “If we are honestly striving to love others, we must also pray for them, even if they are our ­enemies—maybe especially if they are our ­enemies.”

items.title: Eric D. Huntsman | Hard Sayings and Safe Spaces: Making Room for Struggle as Well as Faith
items.description: Eric D. Huntsman, Professor of Ancient Near Eastern Studies. “I love the wonderful diversity of the mosaic that is the body of Christ, each beautiful piece reflecting the glorious light of God’s love.”

items.title: President Joy D. Jones | "Look Unto Him in Every Thought"
items.description: President Joy D. Jones, Primary General President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Obviously we cannot completely control the events that come at us daily, but we can indeed control the worthwhileness of those events.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | Recieving Revelation / Peggy S. Worthen | That We Might Have Joy
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife Peggy S. Worthen. “Hopefully we will choose to follow the counsel of President Thomas S. Monson: ‘Let us relish life as we live it [and] find joy in the journey.’”

items.title: D. Carolina Núñez | Loving Our Neighbors
items.description: D. Carolina Núñez, Associate Dean and Professor of Law, BYU Law School. She uses the story of the good Samaritan to teach why loving our neighbors—the ones who are in proximity—should be a primary focus in our lives.

items.title: J. Scott Miller | Humble Uncertainty
items.description: J. Scott Miller, Dean of the BYU College of Humanities. “It is when we combine humility about the limits of our knowledge with honest questions about life’s perplexities that we demonstrate the kind of humble uncertainty that will expand our souls.”

items.title: Elder Gerrit W. Gong | “We Seek After These Things”
items.description: Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “For me, looking backward from the future is a remembrance of things to come.”

items.title: President Stephen W. Owen | Strength and Safety Through Gathering
items.description: President Stephen W. Owen, Young Men General President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Come unto Him and renew your commitment to serve Him and be part of His people."

items.title: Elder José A. Teixeira | How to Have Joy and Fulfillment
items.description: Elder José A. Teixeira of the Presidency of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Your priorities of today will be your joy and fulfillment of tomorrow."

items.title: Elder Shayne M. Bowen | “I Can Sleep When the Wind Blows”
items.description: Elder Shayne M. Bowen of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. In all of your dealings with others, decide today to do the right thing for the right reason.

items.title: Elder David A. Bednar | “That They Might Have Joy”
items.description: Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He reminds us that if we turn to the teachings of Jesus Christ, we can find peace. They were given "that we might have joy."

items.title: Sister Michelle D. Craig | "This Is My Day of Opportunity"
items.description: Michelle D. Craig, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency. "Earth life is so short in the eternal scheme, but it determines so much. It is our 'day of opportunity.' Use it well and you will have opportunities you never dreamed of."

items.title: Kevin J. and Peggy S. Worthen | Knowing Who You Are/ Spiritual Gifts
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, president of Brigham Young University, and wife Peggy. “Understanding that we are children of Heavenly Parents—sharing Their divine nature and possessing the potential to be like Them—can bring great power into our lives.”

items.title: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf | Can You Hear the Music?
items.description: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We sometimes get so caught up in the grind of everyday life that we fail to recognize the sublime voice of the Spirit."

items.title: Elder Lawrence E. Corbridge | Stand Forever
items.description: Elder Lawrence E. Corbridge of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Knowledge is crucial to avoid deception, to discern between truth and error, and to see clearly and chart a course through the hazards of our day.”

items.title: Elder Ulisses Soares | “Always Remember Him”
items.description: Elder Ulisses Soares of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Please consider some of the things we can do to always remember Jesus Christ every single day.”

items.title: Carrie Roberts | If You Don’t Like It, Change It
items.description: Carrie Roberts, women’s golf coach at Brigham Young University. “In order to get what you want in life, you have to first know what you want. It is hard to think and act for yourself when you don’t know what to think and act upon.”

items.title: Elder Carlos A. Godoy | Enter to Learn; Go Forth to Fight!
items.description: Elder Carlos A. Godoy of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “You are part of the Lord’s army. You don’t need to be set apart for that. The call to stand up for the truth is not a Church calling. It is a life calling.”

items.title: Elder Randall K. Bennett | Prophetic Invitations and Promised Blessings
items.description: Elder Randall K. Bennett of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I promise that your contribution to this world will be profound if you will always be found ­following God’s prophets.”

items.title: Jason S. Carroll | “As I Have Loved You”: Agency-Based Love in Dating and Marriage
items.description: Jason S. Carroll, professor of Marriage and Family Studies at Brigham Young University. “Improper understandings of love… are responsible for many of the struggles some individuals and couples have in dating, courtship, and marriage.”

items.title: Elder M. Joseph Brough | The Modern Mighty Women of Israel
items.description: M. Joseph Brough, Second Counselor in the Young Men General Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “For all of you, as you listen, please remember that bringing honor to the mighty women of Israel in your life will bring joy.”

items.title: J.B. Haws | Wrestling with Comparisons
items.description: J.B. Haws, associate professor of Church History and Doctrine at Brigham Young University. “We can trust that the Lord’s grace is sufficient to ultimately right every injustice, to make up for every loss, and to make weak things become strong.”

items.title: Julianne H. Grose | Finding Your Purpose
items.description: Julianne H. Grose, associate professor of Microbiology and Molecular Biology at Brigham Young University. “Believe that you have a divine purpose. Believe that you have unique talents that are unmatched in the world. Work hard and pray.”

items.title: Phillip D. Rash | Looking to the Margins: Creating Belonging
items.description: Phillip D. Rash, Psychologist and Clinical Professor at Brigham Young University. "I believe it is also critical for us to remember that Christ Himself lived on the margins and that… was intentional and foretold by the ancient prophets.”

items.title: Ellie L. Young | The Transformative Power of Covenants
items.description: Ellie L. Young, associate professor of Clinical Psychology and Special Education at Brigham Young University. “As we journey on the covenant path, the Lord’s long suffering is evidence of his patience and desire to walk the path with us.”

items.title: Michalyn Steele | Choose to Trust the Lord
items.description: Michalyn Steele, associate professor of Law at the J. Reuben Clark Law School at Brigham Young University. “I have worked to develop trust and love for the Lord that is not transactional, but is relational.”

items.title: Christopher E. Crowe | “The Undiscover’d Country”: Navigating Toward the Future
items.description: Christopher E. Crowe, professor of English and English Education at Brigham Young University. "The light of the gospel and the guidance of the Holy Ghost are the constants that you can rely on to help you make the right decisions."

items.title: Amy Tanner | The Gift of Uncertainty
items.description: Amy Tanner, associate professor of Mathematics Education at Brigham Young University. "In this life we know only in part, the more I see that I do not know… in our uncertainty we can accept God’s love for us as certain and constant."

items.title: J. Spencer Fluhman | The University and the Kingdom of God
items.description: J. Spencer Fluhman, Executive Director of Neal A. Maxwell Institute at Brigham Young University. "Gather your strength today. Rest up today, because tomorrow we ride for Zion. And it is not quite Zion if you are not there."

items.title: Pam Musil | The Path to Transformative Change
items.description: Pam Musil, Associate Chair of the Department of Dance at Brigham Young University. "All of us can find ways to be more open and receptive to the transformative change that the Lord requires of us."

items.title: Elder Gary E. Stevenson | The Ongoing Restoration
items.description: Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The Book of Mormon is the engine that powers conversion and a change of heart, leading us closer to Jesus Christ."

items.title: Kevin J. and Peggy S. Worthen | Gathering: Education in a Compact Society / Your Show Must Go On
items.description: Kevin J. Worthen, president of Brigham Young University, and wife Peggy S. Worthen: “Remember… why you came to earth. Do your utmost. Do the best you can. And then act as if there is no alternative but to succeed.”

items.title: President Russell M. Nelson | The Love and Laws of God
items.description: Russell M. Nelson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Because the Father and the Son love us with infinite, perfect love… They have given us laws that will guide and protect us.”

items.title: Michael A. Dunn | Why Mountains?
items.description: Michael A. Dunn, Managing Director of BYU Broadcasting. “Learning how to deal with and overcome things that we perceive as hard betters and improves us.”

items.title: Brigitte C. Madrian | Harry Potter and the Five Gospel Truths
items.description: Brigitte C. Madrian, Dean of the Marriott School of Business of Brigham Young University. “I invite you to prayerfully ask the Lord to help you identify your weaknesses, that through His grace your weak things may become strong.”

items.title: President Mark L. Pace | Faith Still Precedes the Miracle
items.description: Mark L. Pace, Sunday School General President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I commend you for the goodness of your lives and your devotion to the Savior and His gospel. How noble you are and how valuable is your contribution.”

items.title: Bishop W. Christopher Waddell | Are You Ready?
items.description: W. Christopher Waddell, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We all understand that the Lord answers prayers and provides inspiration in a variety of venues.”

items.title: Elder Dale G. and Sister Ruth L. Renlund | Experience God’s Love; The Power to Change
items.description: Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and wife Ruth L. Renlund. “Addressing our dysfunctional receptors for God’s love restores power, stability, and direction in our lives.”

items.title: Sister Jean B. Bingham | How to Be Happy Now—and Forever
items.description: Sister Jean B. Bingham, Relief Society General President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. With the eternal perspective of the gospel as our guide in this life, we can learn how to be truly happy now—and forever.

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | Enduring Joy / Peggy S. Worthen | Learning from the Best Stories
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, President Kevin J Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen.

items.title: Elder Michael T. Ringwood | Everything We Need
items.description: Elder Michael T. Ringwood of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The foundational gift, then—the gift that is given to all—is the Light of Christ.”

items.title: Elder Ronald A. Rasband | Free to Choose
items.description: Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “How are you exercising your agency to further the work of the Lord?”

items.title: Sister Bonnie H. Cordon | Ask of God: Our Solace, Guide, and Stay
items.description: Bonnie H. Cordon, Young Women General President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “He will guide us! He wants to help us achieve the divine and eternal potential He knows is ours.”

items.title: Elder Terence M. Vinson | Meekly Placing Our Total Trust in God
items.description: Elder Terence M. Vinson of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We can sometimes feel like we are careening out of control…But God has been there and done this before.”

items.title: Elder M. Russell Ballard | Children of Heavenly Father
items.description: Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I plead with each of you to please keep your divine identity at the center of everything you do.”

items.title: Steven M. Sandberg | The Light of Forgiving
items.description: Steven M. Sandberg, assistant to the president of Brigham Young University. “When Christ asks us to act with compassion unto ‘the least of these,’ that includes you and how you treat yourself.”

items.title: Elder Jack N. Gerard | “Could We Have Supposed?”
items.description: Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Each of us will have moments when the pressures of this life seem to cloud our ability to see clearly.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | The Process and Power of Hope / Peggy S. Worthen | Faith and Courage to Move Forward
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, President Kevin J Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen.

items.title: Elder James B. Martino | “Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve”
items.description: Elder James B. Martino of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Remember that there is one thing Christ and Satan have in common: they both want us to become like them.”

items.title: Estela Marquez | Enduring and Trusting to the End
items.description: Estela Marquez, Multicultural Student Services Advisor at Brigham Young University. “It is possible to reach your goals if you work hard, keep the right perspective, and use your challenges as opportunities to grow and develop.”

items.title: Candace Berrett | "Angels to Beckon Me"
items.description: "Candace Berrett, associate professor in the Department of Statistics at Brigham Young University. “We are not meant to accomplish this life alone. While we are waiting, we have angels ascending and descending all around us.”

items.title: Bishop Gérald Caussé | Harmony of Body and Spirit: A Key to Happiness
items.description: Gérald Caussé, Presiding Bishop of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “To glorify God in our bodies is to put our external appearance and behavior in tune with our highest spiritual desires."

items.title: President Dallin H. Oaks | Racism and Other Challenges
items.description: President Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Only the gospel of Jesus Christ can unite and bring peace to people of all races and nationalities."

items.title: Jamie L. Jensen | Faith and Science: Symbiotic Pathways to Truth
items.description: Jamie L. Jensen, associate professor of biology at Brigham Young University. “If learning scientific theories puts your faith in jeopardy, choose your faith! Choose your faith until you can better understand the science.”

items.title: Elder Quentin L. Cook | Great Expectations
items.description: Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I am confident we can have the joy and happiness that we desire here and now and that God wants for us.”

items.title: Matthew Wickman | Thriving Spiritually
items.description: Matthew Wickman, professor of English and founding director of the Humanities Center at Brigham Young University. “What does spiritual thriving mean to me? Very simply, it means seeking, recognizing, and enjoying experiences with the Spirit of God.”

items.title: Scott D. Whiting | Deepening Discipleship
items.description: Elder Scott D. Whiting of the Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Your efforts to love your fellow men and women will be the hallmark of your efforts to deepen your discipleship.”

items.title: Kevin J. Worthen | Persevere in Unity / Peggy S. Worthen | Gratitude Amid Chaos
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, President Kevin J Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen.

items.title: Elder David A. Bednar | “As Long as the World Shall Stand”
items.description: Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We are blessed to live and serve in a most remarkable season of the dispensation of the fulness of times.”

items.title: Elder L. Todd Budge | “Broke” Hearts and Contrite Spirits
items.description: L. Todd Budge, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “As we enter into a covenant relationship with [God], we will experience the joy and exhilaration of becoming one with Him.”

items.title: Elder José A. Teixeira | “To Be Spiritually Minded Is Life and Peace”
items.description: Elder José A. Teixeira of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “I invite you to hold on and keep pedaling to become spiritually minded by setting goals in your life for spiritual things.”

items.title: Elder Gary E. Stevenson | Divinely Appointed Responsibilities, Heavenly Blessings
items.description: Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “We have the divinely appointed responsibility as members of the Church of Jesus Christ of caring for those in need.”

items.title: Janalee Emmer | The Transformative Power of Faith and Art
items.description: Janalee Emmer, associate director at the Museum of Art at Brigham Young University. “We all have unique gifts and skills. Your time at the university is an incredible opportunity to investigate, experiment with, and develop those gifts.”

items.title: President Mark L. Pace | His Sheep Still Hear His Voice
items.description: Mark L. Pace, Sunday School General President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The need for us to hear the voice of the true Shepherd has never been greater. His sheep still hear His voice.”

items.title: Elder Kyle S. McKay | There Must Needs Be a Christ
items.description: Elder Kyle S. McKay of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “The Spirit will help you remember that our potential is beyond our present capacity.”

items.title: Ryan Gabriel | Healing Racism Through Jesus Christ
items.description: Ryan Gabriel, assistant professor of sociology at Brigham Young University. "As representatives of Christ, we can work hard to heal the painful legacies of racism that we have inherited, legacies that manifest in new and pernicious ways."

items.title: Niwako Yamawaki | An Immigrant’s Journey Toward God
items.description: Niwako Yamawaki, professor of psychology at Brigham Young University. “As the Lord Himself told us, it is in the service of others and in taking up our own crosses of suﬀering that we will find our own selves.”

items.title: Rick Jellen | Quinoa and Olive Trees: Strengthening the Lord’s Vineyard
items.description: Rick Jellen, associate dean of the College of Life Sciences at Brigham Young University. "I believe that our Father in Heaven expects us to develop this unity and cultivate our diverse talents and abilities.”

items.title: Liz Darger | To Receive, to Covenant, and to Minister
items.description: Liz Darger, senior associate athletic director at Brigham Young University. “This is a one-on-one, personal, individual ministry, and we need everyone!”

items.title: Steven C. Harper | How I Became a Seeker
items.description: Steven C. Harper. professor of Church history and doctrine at Brigham Young University. “The plan is for us to seek our way from simplicity through complexity, by study and by faith, until we arrive at the simplicity on the other side of complexity.”

items.title: Tracianne B. Neilsen | The Messy Middle of Revelation
items.description: Tracianne B. Neilsen, associate professor of physics at Brigham Young University. “The Holy Spirit is the conduit through which you can feel how much your Father in Heaven loves you.”

items.title: Steven A. Smith | Being Christ’s Compassionate Hands
items.description: Steven A. Smith, director of Student Development Services at Brigham Young University. “A humbling duty we have as disciples of Christ is to be His hands in helping make this happen.”

items.title: Melissa F. Lewis-Western | Vaulting to Greater Heights: Replacing Fear with Lasting Peace
items.description: Melissa F. Western, faculty fellow in the Marriott School of Business at Brigham Young University. “I pray that we keep our gaze elevated so that we can see our trials through the lens of their purpose…"

items.title: Lisa Valentine Clark | “Yes, and . . .”: The Creative Art of Living
items.description: Lisa Valentine Clark, Comedian, actor, and host of “The Lisa Show.” “Guided by personal revelation, the creative art of living and becoming requires our full attention and intention to ‘Yes, and . . .’ because that is magic…”

items.title: John B. Bingham | In Awe: The Astonishing Goodness of God
items.description: John B. Bingham, associate dean at the Marriott School of Business at Brigham Young University. “His sacrifice is 'sufficient . . . to redeem, and to justify' all of humanity, and at the same time He succors you and me personally.”

items.title: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf | Five Messages That All of God’s Children Need to Hear
items.description: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "No matter our shortcomings, no matter our flaws, God can heal, inspire, and cleanse us. For He is the God of new beginnings."

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | Heart Knit Together in Love / Peggy S. Worthen | Preparing for Life’s Unexpected Storms
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, President Kevin J Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen.

items.title: Elder Dale G. Renlund | Lifelong Conversion
items.description: Elder Dale G. Renlund, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Enduring to the end is actively and intentionally repeating the steps in the doctrine of Christ.”

items.title: Elder Paul B. Pieper | BYU: Building a Community of Trust and Respect
items.description: Elder Paul B. Pieper of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “BYU is a unique institution in all the world—a community of saint scholars…that could only be possible as a result of the Restoration.”

items.title: Bishop W. Christopher Waddell | Stay Connected: Making it Safely Home
items.description: W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We choose the King of the kingdom when we choose to follow the counsel of those He has chosen: the living prophets.”

items.title: Sister Rebecca L. Craven | The Dignity and Demeanor of Discipleship
items.description: Rebecca L. Craven, Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency. “Dignity and demeanor in our discipleship begin with understanding who we are.”

items.title: Julie L. Valentine | A Noble Responsibility for Good
items.description: Julie L. Valentine, associate dean of Undergraduate Studies and Research in the College of Nursing at Brigham Young University. "You have a noble responsibility to use your strength and influence for good."

items.title: Gilbert W. Fellingham | Six Rules of Success
items.description: Gilbert W. Fellingham, professor of statistics at Brigham Young University. "There are certain rules on this earth that are critically important not only to our temporal journey but to our eternal journey as well."

items.title: Elder W. Mark Bassett | Take Heed and Go Forth
items.description: Elder W. Mark Bassett of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Take advantage of every resource and do your best to keep your spirit, your body, and your mind strong."

items.title: Elder Neil L. Andersen | Time for the Savior at Christmas
items.description: Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The desire to continue good habits beyond Christmas will stay with you, and your progress as one of the Savior’s disciples will grow."

items.title: Kevin J. Worthen | Choose to Be Humble / Peggy S. Worthen | Of Cookies and Judgements
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, President Kevin J. Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen.

items.title: Camille N. Johnson | Bound Securely to the Savior
items.description: Sister Camille N. Johnson, Primary General President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The Savior is steady, sure, and rock solid. He is an anchor that is never displaced. He is a mooring buoy that doesn’t dislodge."

items.title: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland | A Saint Through the Atonement of Christ the Lord / Patricia T. Holland | Thoughts of Peace in Times of Need
items.description: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and his wife, Patricia T. Holland.

items.title: Justin Collings | A Certain Idea of BYU
items.description: Justin Collings, Associate Dean of the J. Reuben Clark Law School at Brigham Young University. "Seek holiness, seek revelation...seek Christlike exemplars, and, above all, 'seek this Jesus of whom the prophets and apostles have written.'”

items.title: Clark G. Gilbert | Christ's Peace in Perilous Times
items.description: Elder Clark G. Gilbert of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "What Christ knew is that despite the tumult we feel all around us, God will prevail in the end."

items.title: Vern P. Stanfill | "Blessed Are the Peacemakers"
items.description: Elder Vern P. Stanfill of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Use every talent...you have to change the world, but while you are doing that, I invite you to make a difference in the world by being true peacemakers.”

items.title: Megan Sanborn Jones | "Won't You Be My Neighbor?"
items.description: Megan Sanborn Jones, Chair of the Department of Theatre and Media Arts at Brigham Young University. “To be a good neighbor is to wonder how your words and actions will impact others rather than to wonder how you will be impacted."

items.title: Elder Kelly R. Johnson | Conquering Life's Daily Distractions
items.description: Elder Kelly R. Johnson of the General Authority Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Think about the things [you] want...then begin doing [things] consistent with that desire every day and you will achieve the desired result."

items.title: Elder D. Todd Christofferson | The First Commandment First
items.description: Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Thus, beginning from our primal state as intelligences, our Heavenly Father has centered Himself and His work in us.”

items.title: Anthony Sweat | We Need an Endowment
items.description: Anthony Sweat, professor of Church history and doctrine at Brigham Young University. “The endowment is a divine power, and the presentation of the endowment is an authorized religious ceremony to facilitate that power.”

items.title: Neill F. Marriott | Pointing Our Souls to Christ
items.description: Neill F. Marriott, former Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Spiritual wisdom, real peace, healing, and godly discernment come to us from Jesus Christ through the Holy Ghost.”

items.title: Tracy Flinders | Of Disciples and Higher Education
items.description: Tracy Flinders, Vice President of Information Technology of Brigham Young University. “Who are we? What is our true identity? In today’s polarized world of divisive identity politics, we need to know the answers to these foundational questions.”

items.title: Adam T. Woolley | Scholarship and Faith: Insights from My BYU Experience
items.description: Adam T. Woolley, Dean of Graduate Studies of Brigham Young University. “I think all of us have experience in attempting to do something many times and failing but slowly getting closer to the goal and then eventually succeeding.”

items.title: Richard Osguthorpe | "To Believe on Their Words"
items.description: Richard Osguthorpe, Dean of the David O. McKay School of Education at Brigham Young University. “There is great value and importance in developing the spiritual gift of believing on the words of others.”

items.title: Tiffany Turley Bowcut | Faith in the Lord, Faith in Ourselves
items.description: Tiffany Turley Bowcut, Title IX coordinator at Brigham Young University. "In order for us to have faith in the Lord, we have to get to know Him."

items.title: Rachel Wadham | Cultivating Godliness in Mortality
items.description: Rachel Wadham, senior librarian for the education and juvenile collection at the Harold B. Lee Library at Brigham Young University. "Cultivating wisdom allows us to enrich and broaden our understanding of so many topics from biology to religion."

items.title: Stacey Shaw | Your Path of Discipleship
items.description: Stacey Shaw, associate professor of social work at Brigham Young University. "Your path to discipleship must include knowing and valuing who you are, seeing and loving others, and choosing to serve throughout your life."

items.title: Christopher Mattson | Six Ways to Be a Better Boat Builder
items.description: Christopher Mattson, professor of mechanical engineering at Brigham Young University. “The boat we take on life’s journey matters, since it will largely determine how we experience the storms.”

items.title: Janis Nuckolls | Finding Wonder in Remote Places
items.description: Janis Nuckolls, professor in the Department of Linguistics at Brigham Young University. “We have unlimited access to wisdom, truth, and blessings from our scriptures, our ordinances, and our covenants.”

items.title: Elder Quentin L. Cook | Give Heed to the Words of the Prophets
items.description: Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “In the doctrines of the Church, faith and the quest for knowledge are not inconsistent; they are compatible and complementary.”

items.title: Kevin J Worthen | We Get to Choose Our Destiny / Peggy S. Worthen | Taking Charge of Our Own Testimony
items.description: President of Brigham Young University, Kevin J Worthen, and his wife, Peggy S. Worthen.

items.title: President Dallin H. Oaks | Going Forward in the Second Century
items.description: President Dallin H. Oaks, First Counselor of the First Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “God’s incomprehensible love for His children does not excuse us from accountability when we break His commandments.”

items.title: Steven J. Lund | Flashes of Light
items.description: Steven J. Lund, Young Men General President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Heavenly Father purposefully designed and ordered our world to require us to walk in faith.”

items.title: Kendra M. Hall-Kenyon | Finding Strength in the Lord
items.description: Kendra M. Hall-Kenyon, Interim Dean of the McKay School of Education at Brigham Young University. “‘You can have a no-problem day, but you can’t have a no-problem life!’”

items.title: Michael S. Drake | Deliverance
items.description: Michael S. Drake, professor of accounting in the School of Accountancy at the Marriott School of Business at Brigham Young University. “I think that we love films of deliverance because we are living in the ultimate deliverance story here on earth.”

items.title: Elder Kevin W. Pearson | The Abundant Life
items.description: Elder Kevin W. Pearson, General Authority Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “An abundant life is a spiritual life. Spiritual, because we are dual beings--literal spirit sons or daughters of God, in physical bodies.”

items.title: Susan H. Porter | Receiving the Gifts of God
items.description: Susan H. Porter, Primary General President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Receiving the gifts of God is a catalyst for change! A change of heart, a change of countenance, a change of desires, a new birth.”

items.title: Jenet Erickson | Designed for Covenant Relationships
items.description: Jenet Erickson, associate professor in Religious Education at Brigham Young University. “We are deeply relational beings, designed not for independence, but for radical dependence and connection.”

items.title: Peter M. Johnson | Christ’s Atonement, Invitations to Act, and Promised Blessings
items.description: Elder Peter M. Johnson of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Christ knows there are people on this campus who feel alone, marginalized, mistreated, and who feel their voices and their concerns are not being heard.”

items.title: Elder Ulisses Soares | Light and Truth
items.description: Elder Ulisses Soares of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “As we continue on this path of walking in Jesus’s holy light, we learn, grow, and gain even more light.”

items.title: BYU President Kevin J Worthen and Sister Peggy Worthen | The Power of Prophetic Promises
items.description: BYU President Kevin J Worthen and Sister Peggy Worthen. "God has promised us powerful blessings that can help us through challenges and trials—if we obey the voice of his prophet."

items.title: Elder Neil L. Andersen | Allowing Your Faith in Jesus Christ to Guide Your Life
items.description: Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Your faith in Jesus Christ will bring you assurance in the choices you are making."

items.title: Elder Kevin S. Hamilton | Why a Church?
items.description: Kevin S. Hamilton, General Authority Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We need a church and this church is literally His Church. The Savior Jesus Christ and the Church of Jesus Christ are inseparably joined together."

items.title: Elder Mark A. Bragg | A Master Class in Leadership: One Day with the Savior
items.description: Mark A. Bragg, General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, "The Book of Mormon details the master class on leadership that Jesus Christ taught during His first day among the Nephites."

items.title: Sister Tracy Y. Browning | Preserving Our Relationship with Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ
items.description: Sister Tracy Y. Browning, Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, "God is always trying to talk to you — He’s trying to tell you He loves you and that you are His priority."

items.title: Andra J. Duke | Spiritual Creation
items.description: Andra J. Duke, Director of Content at BYU Broadcasting. "You have a unique story that you are shaping every day through your experiences and choices."

items.title: Elder Paul V. Johnson | Beautiful Babies Blessing the World
items.description: Paul V. Johnson, Presidency of the Seventy for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, "The greatest impact comes as we move forward with faith."

items.title: Loreen Allphin | Spiritual Lessons from the Natural World
items.description: Loreen Allphin, Associate Dean of the BYU College of Life Sciences, "Because I have benefitted so greatly from the divine Creation, I truly want to be a good steward over it."

items.title: Elder Gerrit W. Gong | Our Own Best Story
items.description: Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, "We can create our best story by focusing on spiritual identity and relationships instead of focusing on our external environments."

items.title: Brooke A. Robertson | “Here’s My Heart, O Take and Seal It”
items.description: Brooke Robertson, policy manager and analyst for BYU’s Integrity and Compliance Office, "Jesus Christ’s covenantal fetters paradoxically give us ultimate freedom if we will wholeheartedly commit ourselves to keep our covenants."

items.title: Melissa P. Larson | Christlike Transformation
items.description: Melissa Larson, professor of accountancy at the BYU Marriott School of Business, "By relying on the strength and comfort Christ offers us, we can move through our transformational journeys with greater peace and confidence."

items.title: W. Justin Dyer | Choosing Christ’s Light Burden
items.description: W. Justin Dyer, professor of religious education, "All choices bring burdens. Aligning our choices with Christ, with His Church, and with His Apostles is the light burden."

items.title: Gus Hart | Six Things I Believe
items.description: Gus Hart, professor of physics and astronomy, "There are six important things we can believe to help us develop our divine potential and complete our unique missions."

items.title: Chip Oscarson | Let Your Education Change You
items.description: Chip Oscarson, associate dean in Undergraduate Education at Brigham Young University, "[Christ] desires to transform us all.... He knows how to make you into more than you could ever possibly make of yourself."

items.title: Barbara Morgan Gardner | Endowed with His Power, You Are Ready to Lead
items.description: Barbara Morgan Gardner, associate professor of Church history and doctrine, "It is [Jesus Christ] who... selflessly transforms us to become like Him, if we will allow Him to do so."

items.title: Pamela Brubaker | Jesus Christ, the Greatest Influencer in Your Life
items.description: Pamela Brubaker, associate professor of public relations in the School of Communications, "Jesus Christ is the most important influencer to have ever lived. He is the most important influencer you can subscribe to."

items.title: Kevin W. Utt | Gathering in Divine Communities
items.description: Kevin W. Utt, director of the Honor Code Office, "We are not on a solo sojourn. Since our first day on this earth, God has organized us into communities, where we learn more about Him and become more like Him."

items.title: Reid L. Neilson | Counting the Known (and Unknown) Costs of Discipleship
items.description: Reid L. Neilson, assistant academic vice president of BYU, Despite the escalating costs of Christian discipleship, the blessings that come from complete and total consecration are worth it.

items.title: Dale G. Renlund | Observation, Reason, Faith, and Revelation
items.description: Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Observation, reason, and faith facilitate revelation and enable the Holy Ghost to be a reliable, trustworthy, and beloved companion."

items.title: Shane and Wendy Reese | No Coincidences // Comfort in Christ
items.description: C. Shane Reese, President of Brigham Young University, and his wife, Wendy Reese. "Understanding God’s divine design for our lives demands deeper discipleship and a fuller acknowledgment of His overarching will."

items.title: Abigail M. Allen | How Will You Carry His Name?
items.description: Abigail M. Allen, assistant professor of accounting in the Marriott School of Business at Brigham Young University. "You are His ambassadors, and through your actions His light can be reflected."

items.title: Allen D. Haynie | Meeting Jesus in the House of the Lord
items.description: Elder Allen D. Haynie of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Gratefully, even though we are imperfect, we are invited as His guests into His House. He extends this invitation to us again and again."

items.title: Kristin M. Yee | Our Covenant Relationship with God: A Wellspring of Relief
items.description: Sister Kristin M. Yee, 2nd Counselor in the General Relief Society Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "We don’t need to navigate this life alone...choose to find relief in partnering with the Lord through our covenants."

items.title: Gary B. Sabin | Fear Not and Return with Honor
items.description: Elder Gary B. Sabin of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "The revealed formula for a successful life and an honorable graduation from life is to follow the Savior."

items.title: Matthew L. Carpenter | We Believe in Being Honest
items.description: Elder Matthew L. Carpenter of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "As you are honest in all you do...You will feel more full of light. You will feel more confident and more comfortable in your relationships with others."

items.title: Campus Christmas Devotional (12-12-23)
items.description: Join students, faculty, performing groups and a host of others as they testify of the gift that came to the world when the Savior was born at Bethlehem.

items.title: President C. Shane Reese and Sister Wendy W. Reese | Eyes to See // Being Doers of the Word
items.description: President C. Shane Reese of Brigham Young University and wife Sister Wendy W. Reese. "To truly become 'doers of the word'... We must move beyond the mere accumulation of knowledge and internalize and apply the teachings of the restored gospel."

items.title: Elder K. Brett Nattress | “Choose You This Day”—“Think Celestial”
items.description: Elder K. Brett Nattress of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Knowing that no one is perfect and that we all make mistakes, we will find peace and safety as we choose to 'Think Celestial.'"

items.title: Elder David A. Bednar | "Consider the Wondrous Works of God" (Job 37:14)
items.description: Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "This marvelous work and a wonder of the latter days is spreading...and enables you and me individually to become the works of God’s work."

items.title: Brother Jan E. Newman | Magnifying Our Precious Gift of Time
items.description: Brother Jan E. Newman, Second Counselor in the Sunday School Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "As you effectively manage your allotted time here on earth, [you will] play a powerful role in [building His kingdom]."

items.title: Elder Evan A. Schmutz | Can You Imagine?
items.description: Elder Evan A. Schmutz of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "When the promised rewards of the next life become so real that they motivate our every action in this life, we are drawing near to our eternal home." Elder Evan

items.title: Elder Dale G. Renlund | Stronger and Closer Connection to God through Multiple Covenants
items.description: Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "[Why?] It is because the multiple covenants are not only sequential but also additive—and even synergistic—in our relationship with God."

items.title: Steven J. Hafen | Our Path to Lasting Personal Peace
items.description: Steven J. Hafen, Administrative Vice President of Brigham Young University. "Through our Savior's Atonement, we can experience the promise that He will never leave us comfortless! What an amazing blessing this is!"

items.title: Brian K. Taylor | Rise to Your Divine Identity, Purpose, and Destiny
items.description: Elder Brian K. Taylor of the Seventy of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. “Understanding God's and our divine identities is the vital foundation for happiness and success as well as for avoiding the identity and purpose crises we see.”

items.title: Rick Anderson | The Tree, the Fruit, and the Building
items.description: Rick Anderson, University Librarian at Brigham Young University. “I testify that as we put both our minds and our hearts to work in studying and applying the truths of eternity, miracles will happen for us and, through us, for others.”

items.title: Mary Davis | Finding Direction in Uncertainty
items.description: Dr. Mary Davis, professor of microbiology and molecular biology at Brigham Young University. “God wants you to be involved in your path. If you are pointed towards Him, He can walk with you no matter what career or life choices you make."

items.title: Grant Jensen | Choosing God's Best Blessings: Family
items.description: Grant Jensen, Dean of the College of Computational, Mathematical, and Physical Sciences at Brigham Young University. "Love is earned through service, and that’s why it is so strong within families."

items.title: Michelle H. Bennett | Eternal Belonging and Becoming
items.description: Michelle H. Bennett, assistant vice president of information technology at Brigham Young University. "We may ask the question 'do I belong' in the [Church]? Let’s change the question and ponder 'why would I not belong?'"

items.title: Ali Crandall | The Entire Church Shall Take Hold of Christ
items.description: Ali Crandall, Associate Professor of Public Health at Brigham Young University. "Whatever storms we face, if we shift our perspective to take hold of Christ, He will help us to weather those storms and we can go forward in confidence."

items.title: Brad P. Owens | Let Us Run with Patience the Race That Is Set Before Us
items.description: Brad P. Owens, Business Ethics professor, Marriot School of Business at Brigham Young University. "In a very real way, our lives are like an ultra-marathon that tests the limits of our spiritual endurance."

items.title: Kimberly O. Jenkins | Bring Healing Light into Your Life
items.description: Kimberly O. Jenkins, Communications Director, BYU College of Computational, Mathematical, and Physical Sciences. "It’s not always an instantaneous process to let light into our lives. It’s more of a process requiring effort and action."

items.title: Ellen S. Knell | Look for the Light
items.description: Ellen Knell, Associate Director at the Center for Language Studies at Brigham Young University. "We don’t always know where our experiences... will take us. Over time, we will detect a pattern and we will see God’s hand in our life."

items.title: Richard A. Gill | The Covenantal Journey of Disciple-Scholarship
items.description: Richard A. Gill, Dean of Undergraduate Education at Brigham Young University. "Being covenantal creates a unique type of acceptance and wonder along the voyage of discovery, inviting us to discover who God intends us to become."

items.title: Tonya H. Fischio | Illuminating Your Place in God's Masterpiece
items.description: Tonya H. Fischio, Assistant Dean of Communications at Brigham Young University. "If you invite the Spirit into all your life’s endeavors and seek to follow... the Holy Ghost, you will be right where you need to be right when you need to be."

items.title: Darron M. Billeter | Learn of Christ
items.description: Darron M. Billeter, associate professor of Marketing at Brigham Young University. "The gate that leads to His strength, His healing, and His guidance is wide open to us if we choose to learn of Him."

items.title: Elder Neil L. Andersen | Educating Our Righteous Desires
items.description: Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. "As we educate our desires, we shape our lives in a way that will allow our desires to be realized."

items.title: President C. Shane Reese and Sister Wendy W. Reese | An Invitation to Become: Vision, Work, and Covenants | The Power of Positivity
items.description: President C. Shane Reese of Brigham Young University and Sister Wendy Reese. "We won’t know how to become if we don’t first know what we want to become... who we may become. Having eyes to see ourselves as something more... is a gift worth seeking."

items.title: Elder Patrick Kearon | "Flecks of Gold"
items.description: Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. "As you look out, and as you look up, you become flecks of gold to an often troubled world. You rejoice in becoming flecks of gold. You build yourselves while you’re here."

items.title: Shima Baughman | Giving All Our Heart to Christ
items.description: Shima Baughman, Professor at the Brigham Young University Law School. "Whatever shame Satan is putting in your heart, remember that Jesus has conquered it."

items.title: Elder Takashi Wada | Journey to a Land of Promise—Obtaining Charity
items.description: Elder Takashi Wada, General Authority Seventy. "The blessings associated with the trials in our lives are to become closer to the Lord and to develop the characteristics of charity, even the pure love of Christ."

items.title: Elder Jörg Klebingat | The Atonement of Jesus Christ, Judgment Day, and You
items.description: Elder Jörg Klebingat, General Authority Seventy. "The Savior’s Atonement must not be cheap, instead, it should mean everything to us."

items.title: Sister Amy A. Wright | The Divine Pattern of Deliverance
items.description: Sister Amy A. Wright, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency. "Instead of 'wishing for the day'—wishing and waiting and hoping for calmer waters—we would be wise to strengthen and fortify our anchors."

items.title: J. Ty Hopkins | Lessons on Endurance
items.description: J. Ty Hopkins, professor at Brigham Young University. "There will be rough terrain, blisters, and crashes; but there will also be a meadow of flowers... The process, not the product, will allow us to find joy on our way to the finish."

items.title: Elder Anthony D. Perkins | Becoming God's Peculiar Treasure
items.description: Elder Anthony D. Perkins, General Authority Seventy. "If we are not ashamed of Jesus Christ, then He will not be ashamed of us."

items.title: Sister J. Anette Dennis | Finding Peace Amidst Uncertainty
items.description: Sister J. Anette Dennis, First Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency. "We have the Lord, the Spirit, and angels around us to bear us up. That includes you! There really is no limit to the Savior’s capacity to help you!"

items.title: President C. Shane Reese and Sister Wendy Reese | God Loves Underdogs // Connections
items.description: President C. Shane Reese of Brigham Young University and his wife Sister Wendy Reese. "God’s grace goes beyond improbable victories—God wins impossible victories."

items.title: Elder Gary E. Stevenson | Banners for Discipleship
items.description: Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. "Strive to make a meaningful contribution as you engage in new countries, communities, neighborhoods, and wards—wherever you may be."

items.title: Elder Kevin R. Duncan | Jesus Christ Is the Answer
items.description: Elder Kevin R. Duncan, General Authority Seventy. "Christ’s grace isn’t about us being perfect. It’s about trusting in and relying on Him when we’re at our lowest and letting His strength carry us through."

items.title: Elder Ricardo P. Giménez | My "Why" Is My Love for the Savior
items.description: Elder Ricardo P. Giménez, General Authority Seventy. "Seek to understand the reason 'why' you do what you do. Seek to find the connection between what you do to worship the Savior and your love for Him."

items.title: Elder Michael A. Dunn | These Foolish Things
items.description: Elder Michael A. Dunn, General Authority Seventy. "The very highest and Christlike ideals within us... are well worth clinging to and standing up for, even despite the ridicule and biting scorn of a very naysaying world."

items.title: Kalani Sitake | Discovering God's Plan for You
items.description: Kalani Sitake, head football coach at Brigham Young University. "Struggles in school mean you’re learning new skills. Being low on funds means you’re learning how to budget and will be thankful... God will provide. And good times are ahead."

items.title: Gabriel W. Reid | Go to Work and Build
items.description: Brother Gabriel W. Reid, Second Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "When you go to work and build, God builds you."

items.title: Teresa Bell | The Hand of God in Your Life
items.description: Teresa Bell, Faculty Member at Brigham Young University. "Every time you wonder what you should do with your life, study your patriarchal blessing. Every time you want to feel God’s love, read your patriarchal blessing."

items.title: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf | Joyfully Receive the Unexpected Messiah
items.description: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. "If you wait for sorrow to end before you experience joy, you might miss joy completely."

items.title: Hal Boyd | A Bonfire of Faith
items.description: Hal Boyd Chief of Staff at Brigham Young University. "Christ calls to us to continue to hold fast to our spiritual mission, our sacred light."

items.title: Salani Lesā Pita | The Most Desirable Above All Things
items.description: Salani Lesā Pita, analyst in the Brigham Young University budget office. "Every time I act in faith on a prompting from the Lord, His purposes are accomplished."

items.title: Sarah Clark | Jesus Christ, The Master Teacher
items.description: Dean Sarah Clark from the Mckay school of education. "By picking up these stories again and again, we allow the Savior to help us rewrite them in ways that can make us whole."

items.title: Richard Houseman | BYU: A Place we can Go to Light, Be Filled with Light, and Share Light
items.description: Richard Houseman, Dean of Continuing Education. "Have the faith to go to Jesus Christ! His light is the most joyous influence in our lives when we make Him the most desirable influence in our lives."

items.title: William Clayton | Answering the Dual Calls for Academic Excellence and Discipleship
items.description: William Clayton, professor and associate dean at BYU law school. "When you are willing to work hard and your motivations are righteous, God can help you do more than you think you’re capable of."

items.title: Dawan Coombs | Working Through Wobble
items.description: Dawan Coombs, Associate Professor of English. "The Saviors Atonement fills the gaps in our path of where we are versus where we think we need to be."

items.title: Brennan Platt | We Chose This! Agency, Atonement, and Joy
items.description: Brennan Platt, a professor in the college of Home & Family Sciences. "We chose this. We shouted for joy! We knew it was right."

items.title: Sherami Jara | Fear Not, Little Flock
items.description: Sherami Jara, Assistant Dean of Humanities. "Faith is not the absence of sorrow, sadness, struggle or pain. They often coexist."

items.title: Amy Jex | Doin’ the Plan: Trusting in God’s Love and Help
items.description: Amy Jex, an associate professor in the Department of Dance. “In trusting in His plan, we can also grow to trust ourselves and our ability to choose wisely.”

items.title: Elder Gerrit W. Gong | An Ear to Wisdom, a Heart to Understanding
items.description: Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. "Instead of our being held captive to old pasts, His Atonement can free us to new futures. Jesus Christ atones. He redeems. He restores not only what was, but what can be."

items.title: BYU Sesquicentennial Kickoff | Celebrating Gifts of Light
