items.description: The Bain and Tan families prove the in-laws are not always outlaws; famous football players, Matt Bushman and Chad Lewis get personal about being in-laws. Author Greg McKeown on finding more joy in daily work; the Sorensen’s raise hard working kids.

items.title: The Happy Empty Nest & The Big Beautiful Family
items.description: Dr. Jennifer Finlayson-Fife addresses the unique challenges of empty-nest couples; the Cramers tell their experience. Family researcher Heather Johnson on the changing nature of the American family; the Bairds manage a modern family of ten.

items.title: Calling on the Village & The Blended Family
items.description: The Ashbys build a support system and never feel alone; Sister Aburto from the LDS Church points to the Savior’s example for Christians and community. The Kights have a successful blended family; Tony Overbay shares four pillars of communication.

items.title: Honoring Roots & The Mother-Son Bond
items.description: Former BYU basketball player Yoeli Childs and Kara Childs get personal about their mother-son bond; Lindsey Wells makes efforts as a "boy mom". The Lotulelei family honors roots; Dr. Matt Townsend offers three questions to define your family legacy.

items.title: Raising Kids with Grit & The Engaged Dad
items.description: Surfer Bethany Hamilton reveals more of her story and how to live with grit, grace and faith; the Phipps raise with grit with the “farm approach”. One ritual helps Fernando Seminario be an engaged dad; Anthony Sweat offers insights on fatherhood.

items.title: Strong Sibling Bonds & The Nature Connection
items.description: The Anderson family offers ways for siblings to get along better; a brother bond makes musicians Ben and Chad Truman successful. Getting outside everyday makes the Sutherland family happier; Dr. Patti Freeman declares that recreation is God-given.

items.title: Fiddler on the Roof
items.description: In pre-revolutionary Russia, a poor Jewish villager struggles to provide for his daughters while preserving his cherished traditions.

items.title: Yearning for the Word
items.description: William Tyndale, Martin Luther, and other Christian reformers endeavor to provide the Bible in common vernaculars. Their hopes for the support religious and political leaders are met with rejection, punishment, and turmoil.

items.title: Martyrs for a Book
items.description: Charges of heresy lead to imprisonment, excommunication, and martyrdoms as reformations of Christianity continue across Europe. King Henry VIII assumes more political and religious power as he strives to issue a male heir.

items.title: The King James Bible
items.description: William Tyndale’s work inspired further reformation even after his martyrdom. Much of his translation is found in the King James version of the Bible. Phrases and words created by Tyndale are part of today’s vernacular because of the Bible.

items.title: Flood of Memories: Remembering the 1976 Teton Dam Disaster & Recovery
items.description: "In 1976, the Teton Dam failed, releasing 80B gallons in Idaho. 50 years later, historians Fred Woods and Christian Mawlam document the disaster's impact in 'Flood of Memories.'"

items.description: Legendary head coach LaVell Edwards inspired and influenced the coaching careers of many directly.

items.description: Cougars in the NFL features Fred Warner, Jamaal Williams, Bronson Kaufusi, and John Denney discussing life in the NFL, BYU football, preparation, leadership, and professional success.

items.description: BYU Football Media Day 2021 features Kalani Sitake, Tom Holmoe, coaches, and players discussing the post-11-win season, quarterback competition, returning fans, player development, and expectations for a challenging schedule.

items.title: BYU Football - A History of Offensive Innovation
items.description: A look at the cutting edge creativity on offense that has made BYU Football successful.

items.title: Web Chats 2021
items.description: BYU Football Media Day 2021 Web Chats features players and coaches discussing team culture, quarterback competition, family, special teams, personal stories, and preparations for an exciting season ahead.

items.title: State of the Program
items.description: Dave McCann hosts, with many different coaches and players on the BYU Football team discuss the state of the program and their plans for the final season in independence, and preparing for the Big 12.

items.title: BYU: A History of Independence
items.description: A look at BYU’s time as an Independent and how it prepared them for the move to the BIG 12.

items.title: Web Chats
items.description: In preparation for BYU football, BYUtv will host its annual Media Day with many interview sessions throughout the day.

items.title: Start with Why with Simon Sinek
items.description: Author and rogue anthropologist, Simon Sinek discusses his philosophy of starting with a why or learning how to live everything with a purpose with our host Rebecca Cressman.

items.title: Families on the Home Front
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses families on the home front with individuals who are a part of the military community.

items.title: Bullying
items.description: Dr. Dorothy Espelage and Rebecca Cressman discuss bullying in schools through the stories of Jeff Johnston and Falcon Ridge Elementary.

items.title: Charitable Organizations
items.description: Rebecca Cressman and Jennifer Borget discuss charitable organizations and how individuals can make a difference in the world around them.

items.title: Helping Public Schools
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses how parents can help the children in public schools with the National PTA President, Chuck Saylors.

items.title: Mommy Blogging
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses mommy blogging with individuals who have experienced it firsthand.

items.title: The Jets
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses the rise of The Jets, an 80’s pop group, with the Wolfgramm family.

items.title: Inspiring Stories 2
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses inspiring stories of hope with Kevin Bardsley, Ginger Johnson, and Kelle Hampton.

items.title: Pornography--Start a Conversation
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses opening conversations about pornography with clinical psychologist Dr. Kirk Dougher and women who have experienced the effects of pornography in their lives.

items.title: Movie Night
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses new ideas on how to enjoy movie nights.

items.title: Collaborative Consumption
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses collaborative consumption with author and expert, Rachel Botsman.

items.title: 5 Love Languages
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses the five love languages with marriage and family therapist, Dr. Gary Chapman.

items.title: Slow Food Feast
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses slow food feasting with specialists in the food community and the slow food movement.

items.title: Inner Amazing-Breast Cancer
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses the inner amazing about breast cancer survival with personal style consultant, Darcy Howard.

items.title: Biz Kids
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses Biz Kids with producers and founders Jim Mckenna and Jeanine Glista.

items.title: Dare to Dream
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses daring to dream with Whitney Johnson from the Dare To Dream Blog.

items.title: Men Preventing Violence
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses men preventing violence with co-founder of A Call To Men, Ted Bunch.

items.title: Inspiring Stories 1
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses the inspiring stories of hope from Cami Walker, Kate Fletcher,Jason and Rachel Levitt, and Becky Douglas.

items.title: Momnificent
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses how to be momnificent with life coach Lori Radum.

items.title: The Life Story
items.description: Rebecca Cressman and Dan McAdams discuss the life story and how individuals use narratives to find their identities.

items.title: Food Awareness
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses food awareness with author Blake Spalding and mother Jen Kilstrom.

items.title: Edible Schoolyard with Alice Waters
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses the edible schoolyard with chef and food advocate, Alice Waters.

items.title: Chocolate
items.description: Rebecca Cressman and members of the Fresh Take staff explore fine chocolate with chocolate importer Nick Fapier.

items.title: True Men True Strength
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses true men and true strength with Curt Doussett. Together they recognize men who exemplify the ideals of this organization.

items.title: Inner Amazing-Self Esteem
items.description: Rebecca Cressman discusses the inner amazing of self-esteem with personal style consultant Darcy Howard.

items.title: Following Jesus
items.description: Join children around the world to learn about following Jesus. Joined by Sisters Susan H. Porter, Amy A. Wright, and Tracy Y. Browning of the Primary General Presidency, and President Dallin H. Oaks and his wife Sister Kristen Oaks.

items.title: Sharing the Love of Jesus with Others
items.description: Watch and listen to stories from children all around the world about how they share the love of Jesus. Joined by Sisters Susan H. Porter, Amy A. Wright, and Tracy Y. Browning of the Primary General Presidency, and Elder Jeffrey R. Holland.

items.title: Sharing Jesus's Love Through Service with Elder Bednar
items.description: Fun, engaging content made just for kids — with music, stories from children around the world, inspirational messages and a visit from Louie the Toucan.

items.title: Sharing Jesus's Love Through Service with Elder Kearon
items.description: Join Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, Sister Jennifer Kearon, and the Primary General Presidency to learn about sharing the love of Jesus through serving others.

items.title: Prophets Guide Us to Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ
items.description: Special messages for children by Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, Sister Susan Gong, and the Primary General Presidency.

items.title: The Family Is of God
items.description: The Family Is of God invites children and their families into warm, personal conversations about God's love, our divine worth, and the bonds that connect us. Through stories and real families, kids learn they belong to God's family.

items.title: From the Rough
items.description: Based on a true story, Catana Starks becomes the first woman to coach a collegiate men’s golf team. Her team of misfits face challenges, but eventually she leads them to an all-time-record championship season.

items.title: Lumina
items.description: Raised mostly by a surrogate family, Boston artist Lumina Gershfield is compelled to find out all that she can about her biological family.

items.title: Durrell
items.description: As an African American with a southern heritage, Durrell assumed his great-grandfather was a farmhand, but an old photo reveals a different story.

items.title: Katie
items.description: Katie’s great grandmother is said to have died of leukemia. After having her own share of health problems, Katie wants to know if her great grandmother's health problems are genetic or not.

items.title: Maile
items.description: Maile wants to learn more about her ancestor that was sent to an island off of Hawaii, Kalaupapa, because she was diagnosed as a leper. Maile wants to learn what life was like for her, isolated from her children and family.

items.title: John
items.description: John wants to learn where he got his name from and the type of person his great grandpa was. He visits Andersonville Prison, Palmetto Agricultural Museum, and Palmetto’s Yellow Fever Cemetery.

items.title: Deanna
items.description: Deanna’s great grandparents died in a house fire. Deanna wants to learn the truth about what happened and what her great grandparents' lives were like immigrating from Italy to St. Louis.

items.title: Danielle
items.description: Danielle learns that her great-grandfather was an inventor, so she looks into more of her ancestry.

items.title: James
items.description: Gown designer James Walker investigates the truth behind the family legend of an Indian princess ancestor who immigrated to Utah in the early 1900s.

items.title: Andrea
items.description: Andrea is looking for the motivation to live a healthier life and looks to her great-grandmother who immigrated to the United States. She learns what her life was like and what drove her great grandmother to leave her home in Ireland.

items.title: Gloria
items.description: Gloria sets out to uncover any positive attributes for which her ancestor can be remembered.

items.title: Boyd
items.description: Boyd wants to discover if his lineage traces back to Hawaiian royalty. He visits Iao Valley and Kauai Historical Society to find his answers.

items.title: Vicki
items.description: Vicki Biss believes she is part American Indian and travels to Shiloh, Tennessee, to discover the surprising truth behind the legend.

items.title: Lakia
items.description: After spending her childhood in foster care, Lakia Holmes looks to make a connection with her family through her great-grandmother.

items.title: Xander & Carrie
items.description: After their twins contract a genetic disease, Xander and Carrie search their history for traces of HLH and want to learn about the blood donor that saved their children’s lives.

items.title: Kerry
items.description: Kerry learns about his father's relationship with his own parents and wonders if history is repeating with Kerry and his son.

items.title: Emily
items.description: Emily goes on a journey to trust the feelings and impressions she has about her ancestors. She visits Marysburg Cemetery and Cambridge, Massachusetts to kindle a connection to her ancestors.

items.title: Do Your Own Generations Project
items.description: Learn how to do your own generations project by connecting with your ancestors in a way that makes a difference in your life right now.

items.title: Pj & Heidi
items.description: PJ seeks to rekindle a relationship with her sister Heidi after they grew through finding the good stories in their family history. They visit Germantown, New York and Canada.

items.title: Tara
items.description: After going through the trauma of contracting meningitis, Tara is looking for strength by learning about her Muslim ancestors and their life during the Indo-Pakistani War.

items.title: Will
items.description: Will wants to learn if he should pursue his love for acting or settle down and have a family. He looks to his great-grandfather who lived his life as one of the first forest rangers in St George, Utah.

items.title: Nick
items.description: Nick wants to discover why his French Canadian grandmother turned against her heritage and followed the Greek tradition. Along the way, he learns about French Canadian cuisine.

items.title: Rachel
items.description: Rachel looks to her ancestors to find a purpose and learn about the truth to botany rumors in history. She learns about the Salem Witch Trials and Tulip Mania.

items.title: Ty
items.description: Ty wants to learn about his German heritage and knows he will have to come to terms with some tough history.

items.title: Sam
items.description: An undertaker learns about his African-American ancestors by investigating their deaths.

items.title: Sean
items.description: Sean learns about his great-grandfather's life during World War I to see if following the call is worth all the heartache. He visits Plymouth Plantation and Boston.

items.title: Ed
items.description: Ed was adopted, but always believed he had a connection to the Native American culture. He goes in search for a possible Native American heritage and to understand some of his other cultural roots.

items.title: Matthew
items.description: Matthew seeks closure after his brother's death by walking in the shoes of his ancestors who fought in wars and grieved the loss of loved ones.

items.title: Where Are They Now?
items.description: Emily, Tara, Rachel, and Sean share how the Generations Project has changed their lives after a year has passed.

items.title: Graham
items.description: Olympic snowboarder Graham Watanabe wants to learn what it takes to make sacrifices and learns about his Asian ancestry.

items.title: Rachel
items.description: Rachel has always sought validation from outside sources ever since her dad died. She looks to her ancestry to find the strength to be true to who she is and learns that her great-grandma sang in the first women’s quartet in Las Vegas.

items.title: Roi
items.description: Roi hopes that by exploring his family history, he will be able to deal with racial persecution. He visits Surrey County Historical Society and helps heal the lives hurt by the 2011 Joplin Tornado.

items.title: Amber
items.description: Amber helps her daughter, Deseree, discover her African American heritage and self-acceptance. They visit Washington D.C. and Orange, Virginia.

items.title: Raquel
items.description: Raquel needs her ancestors’ advice on how to choose between a family and career. She visits Madrid, Spain and learns about her biological ancestors who lived during the Spanish Civil War.

items.title: Nancy
items.description: Nancy is a full-time caregiver for her husband and wants to be self-empowered and follow her own dreams. She learns about her grandparents and visits New York.

items.title: David
items.description: David says his family has this innate desire to succeed at all costs and wants to learn if his immigrant grandfather really did leave a child behind in Jamaica and lied about his race to succeed.

items.title: Jill
items.description: Jill wants to learn to let go of the resentment she had for her negligent father by learning about his life and why he might have made the choice he did.

items.title: Eli
items.description: Eli is an Iraq veteran who founded Turtle Women Rising. She wants to find peace and learn about her Yaqui history.

items.title: Natalie
items.description: After the tragedy of losing her youngest son, Natalie wants to learn about her heritage and find strength to be the mother her other three children need.

items.title: Go Tell it on the Mountain by BYU Singers
items.description: BYU Singers performs Go Tell It on the Mountain, a joyful Christmas spiritual celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ. Expressive choral harmonies bring the familiar melody and its message of hope, faith, and praise to life for the holiday season anew.

items.title: God Bless the Broken Road
items.description: The widow of a war veteran and her 9-year-old daughter develop a close bond with an up-and-coming race car driver.

items.title: Grace Divine by BYU Men’s Chorus Featuring BYU Celtic Ensemble & BYU Irish Dance Club
items.description: Enjoy Grace Divine by the BYU Men's Chorus, featuring the BYU Celtic Ensemble and BYU Irish Dance Club. Choral harmonies, Celtic music, and Irish dance come together in an uplifting performance celebrating music, movement, and shared artistry.

items.title: Francesca Battistelli / Sidewalk Prophets
items.description: Billboard music award nominees Sidewalk Prophets perform "Come to the Table" and "I Believe It Now." Grammy award and Dove winner Francesca Battistelli performs "Holy Spirit" and "God is Good."

items.title: Jonathan McReynolds / Marie Osmond
items.description: #1 Billboard artist and Grammy Nominee Jonathan McReynolds performs "Best Thing" and "Lover of My Soul." Marie Osmond performs "The Only One" and "I Need Thee Every Hour."

items.title: Christmas Special
items.description: Amy Grant, CeCe Winans, Kirk Franklin, Michael W. Smith, Lecrae, Michelle Williams, Ben Rector and more celebrate Christmas with musical performances.

items.title: Cece Winans / Jordan Smith
items.description: Season 9 winner of The Voice Jordan Smith performs "Be Still and Know" and "Don't Quit." Cece Winans, the most awarded female Gospel artist of all time, performs "Believe For It" and "Great Is Thy Faithfulness."

items.title: Zach Williams / Naomi Raine
items.description: Grammy Award–winner and contemporary gospel singer Naomi Raine sings "Find My Peace" and "Promises." Grammy and GMA Dove Award–winner and southern rock artist Zach Williams performs his hit songs "Heaven Help Me" and "Chainbreaker."

items.title: Brandon Lake / Tasha Layton
items.description: Worship singer and Billboard Music Award winner Brandon Lake performs his songs "Grave Into Gardens" and "Gratitude." Christian artist and Christian Airplay chart-topper Tasha Layton performs her songs "Look What You've Done" and "Into The Sea."

items.title: Evan Craft / DOE
items.description: Contemporary gospel music singer/songwriter and Grammy nominee DOE performs her songs "So Good" and "Brighter." Worship singer and Dove Award nominee Evan Craft performs his songs "Be Alright" and "All I Ever Need."

items.title: Phil Wickham / MŌRIAH
items.description: Contemporary Christian musician and GMA Dove Award winner Phil Wickham performs his songs "Hymn of Heaven" and "Battle Belongs." Entertainer MŌRIAH performs her songs "Brave" and "Known, Seen, Loved."

items.title: Kevin Olusola / Elle Limebear
items.description: Pentatonix beatboxer Kevin Olusola performs "Turn Your Eyes Upon Jesus" and "Because He Lives." Singer Elle Limebear performs her original songs "Angels" and "Call On Your Name."

items.title: We Are Messengers / Elaine Bradley
items.description: Billboard Top Christian Albums chart-topper Darren Mulligan of Irish band We Are Messengers performs “Come What May,” and “Maybe It’s Okay.” Singer, songwriter, drummer, and Billboard Music Award–winner Elaine Bradley sings “Show Me,” and “What If.”

items.title: Matt Maher / Anna Golden
items.description: Singer and songwriter Anna Golden performs “Take It To Jesus,” and “Amazing Grace.” Five-time GMA Dove Award winner Matt Maher performs “Leaning” and “Run to the Father.”

items.title: Rhett Walker / Matt Sallee
items.description: Grammy winner Matt Sallee of Pentatonix performs "Yes and Amen" and "Word of God Speak." Grammy nominated country and Christian singer Rhett Walker sings his songs "Believer" and "Gospel Song."

items.title: Rend Collective / Mali Music
items.description: Grammy Award–winner Mali Music performs "Way For You" and "Miracle." GMA Dove Award nominees Gareth Gilkeson and Chris Llewellyn from Rend Collective perform "Your Name is Power" and "Counting Every Blessing."

items.title: Cory Asbury / Dante Bowe
items.description: Grammy Award–nominated singer and songwriter Dante Bowe performs "Champion" and "Voice of God." GMA Dove Award–winner Cory Asbury sings "Reckless Love" and "Egypt."

items.title: A Grace Notes Christmas: Vol. 3
items.description: Zach Williams, Brandon Lake, Naomi Raine, Tasha Layton, DOE, Kevin Olusola, Matt Sallee, Phil Wickham and more celebrate Christmas on the Grace Notes studio.

items.title: Tye Tribbett / Evvie McKinney
items.description: Evvie McKinney performs "Look Not Further" and "Just Like God." Grammy-nominated Tye Tribbett performs "I Need You" and "Anyhow."

items.title: Granite Flats Trailer
items.description: Watch the trailer for Granite Flats.

items.title: Pilot
items.description: Arthur Milligan and his mother move to Granite Flats, Colorado where they hope to find peace and quiet in the midst of the Cold War. An explosion rocks the town as well as the local army base.

items.title: Empty Box
items.description: Granite Flats is in a panic in the aftermath of the explosion. Arthur and his new friends won't be left out of the action; a covert meeting and a few far-fetched theories have the trio embarking on an investigative journey.

items.title: A Secret to the Heart Nearest
items.description: Two investigations into the mysterious happenings in Granite Flats ensue—one by Chief Sanders and the military police and the other by Arthur and his cohorts—and each has varying degrees of success.

items.title: Talking
items.description: Beth tries to connect with her son, Arthur, who has built a metal detector with his friends to help them investigate the mysteries in Granite Flats. A big city reporter begins asking questions around town.

items.title: Bonds
items.description: Friendships are tested after a failed class project; Beth investigates Frank's strange behavior and John struggles to balance his family life with his duties as police chief.

items.title: Reassembly
items.description: Madeline, Arthur, and Timmy seek out new mysteries to solve and Chief Sanders uncovers something huge with the help of some mysterious newcomers.

items.title: The Wrong Man
items.description: Frank asks for Beth's help to prove his sanity, Hershel receives visitors while incarcerated, and Arthur and his friends try to salvage their science fair project.

items.title: Something Dangerous
items.description: Chief Sanders calls in a favor as he attempts to prove Hershel's innocence and have him released from jail. After the science fair, Arthur, Timmy, and Madeline solve yet another mystery in Granite Flats.

items.title: The Making of Granite Flats
items.description: Catch a behind-the-scenes glimpse of BYUtv's first scripted drama.

items.title: Children of Darkness, Children of Light
items.description: Chief Sanders and Agent Scott investigate citizens whose loyalties are questionable. The young detectives are still curious about the coded message they found. At the hospital, experiments reveal a patient's past.

items.title: Boundaries
items.description: The three sleuths argue about getting involved with the FBI's investigation. Beth is concerned about Frank and the experiments at the hospital. Wallace is caught in the middle when Regina and Hershel argue about what's best for the boy.

items.title: From Whose Bourn No Traveler Returns
items.description: Timmy, Arthur, and Madeline make a dangerous and significant discovery, right under the nose of the FBI. While they investigate, Granite Flats is in an uproar—chaos breaks out at the hospital and Chief Sanders pursues Slim.

items.title: Also Be the Consolation
items.description: The town is in mourning the loss of a friend. Regina is grieving and reliving her memories, John can't seem to live with himself, and even Hershel struggles to deal with the tragedy.

items.title: Put Away Childish Things
items.description: The kids' new English teacher (Christopher Lloyd) has a way of making Hamlet applicable to life in Granite Flats. Some citizens are unsettled when a CIA agent arrives (Cary Elwes). Arthur takes his detective work to a new level.

items.title: The Stories We Tell....
items.description: Mr. Hugh Ashmeade (Cary Elwes) stirs up confusion and danger when he meddles in the Andrews’ personal and professional lives and Chief Sanders recruits a new deputy with somewhat surprising results.

items.title: Cor Unum, Corambis
items.description: Arthur continues his investigation alone because Tim and Madeline seem distracted. Professor Hargraves (Christopher Lloyd) counsels Timmy on romance. Hershel becomes the bait in a dangerous trap.

items.title: Project Madman
items.description: Beth, Whittison, and the Andrews turn the tables on Ashmeade and get to the bottom of what he’s been planning. Timmy and Madeline find what everyone has been pursuing, leading Madeline to question her adoption story.

items.title: Behind the Scenes of Granite Flats
items.description: Get a behind-the-scenes look at how Granite Flats is produced.

items.title: Our Rendezvous Is Fitly Appointed
items.description: Granite Flats is rocked after the death of one of the town's most beloved citizens. Two new faces show up in town: Arthur's Aunt Alice (Parker Posey) and Madeline's Uncle Scottie (George Newbern). A new mystery needs to be solved.

items.title: The Converging Objects of the Universe Perpetually Flow
items.description: Ezekiel gets one step closer to discovering the identity of The Plumber. Alice settles into Granite Flats. Trust issues arise between the Andrews. Scottie takes a new case from an unlikely client.

items.title: Mortised in Granite
items.description: Lieutenant Frank Quincy disappears from the hospital. Chief Sanders and Hershel take matters into their own hands. Aunt Alice has a prophetic dream.

items.title: Form and Union and Plan
items.description: The Andrews try to get answers from Frank Quincy. John enlists his wife's help in the investigation and she discovers a major piece to the puzzle. Frank enlists the help of the kid detectives.

items.title: The Threads That Were Spun Are Gathered
items.description: The Andrews have Professor Hargraves over for dinner, but with an ulterior motive. The kid detectives are back together for a common cause. Agent Ezekiel Scott’s interrogation does not go quite as planned.

items.title: Some Intricate Purpose
items.description: Chief Sanders and Agent Scott disagree about the identity of The Plumber. Wallace’s mother comes to town and shakes things up. Susan desperately clings to Madeline after hearing her true feelings.

items.title: The Terrible Doubt of Appearances
items.description: Agent Scott questions Professor Hargraves for his suspicious behavior and refuses to believe his story. The kids suspect that something is up when Professor Hargraves fails to come to class. They team up with Mrs. Andrews to solve Frank’s case.

items.title: All Truths Wait in All Things
items.description: Doctor Andrews unlocks Lieutenant Quincy’s memories, including the truth about Beth’s fate. Regina and Hershel come to an agreement. The kid sleuths dig up secrets and Whittison must face his troubling past.

items.title: On Set with the Cast of Granite Flats
items.description: As Season 3 begins, meet some of the cast members of Granite Flats, and find out how they develop their characters and relate to one another.

items.title: Handel’s Messiah with The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square performs George Frederic Handel’s Messiah with soloists Amanda Woodbury, Tamara Mumford, Tyler Nelson, and Tyler Simpson.

items.title: Heart of the Country
items.description: Faith’s husband, Luke, is jailed for fraud. Heartbroken, she leaves her life behind in New York to return home to rural Carolina and be near her father and sister.

items.title: Coming Home
items.description: Animal-loving Amy discovers a horse named Spartan being abused at Mallen's farm and convinces her mother to rescue him. But when a storm on the way home sends their truck and trailer off the road, Amy wakes up in the hospital at the center of tragedy

items.title: After the Storm
items.description: Lou sends home Mrs. Roach's horse, despite the fact that his fear of vehicles has yet to be cured. Val Stanton begins spreading rumors about Heartland and their skills without Marion. Ty's probation officer comes to the ranch while he is off showing

items.title: Breaking Free
items.description: Heartland has its first open house, and Lou invites their dad. Amy works with Lisa's horse Promise, and at the open house Val accuses Amy of giving Promise drugs. Meanwhile, Pegasus is depressed.

items.title: Taking Chances
items.description: A new guy, Ben, is staying at Heartland and wreaks havoc on Amy and Ty's relationship.

items.title: The Best Laid Plans
items.description: Lou drives friends and family to distraction as she arranges to have a video made to promote Heartland.

items.title: One Trick Pony
items.description: Lou's New York boyfriend Carl comes for a visit, but he has to adjust to the ranch's lifestyle.

items.title: Come What May
items.description: Heartland takes in a pregnant mare, Mallory gives Ty riding lessons, and Ben competes in a horse show.

items.title: Out of the Darkness
items.description: Amy tries to help a champion stallion and his trainer, who were injured. Mallory gives advice.

items.title: Ghost From the Past
items.description: After elderly Mrs. Bell has a heart attack, Amy takes in her pony, Sugarfoot, to whom Lou grows surprisingly attached. Ty's old girlfriend from the juvenile group home shows up looking for him, having taken a job at Briar Ridge.

items.title: Born to Run
items.description: Mallory discovers a crooked ranch-hand who plans to sell a herd of wild mustangs to a slaughterhouse.

items.title: Thicker Than Water
items.description: When Amy invites Tim up to the ranch, Lou tries to impress their estranged father, not wanting to admit to him her fear of horses. Jack escapes from the family reunion by going on a fishing trip with Lisa while Ty practices his cattle skills.

items.title: Rising From the Ashes
items.description: A sudden barn fire puts Heartland in financial straits, just as Lou was preparing to return to her old life in New York. Looking to expand neighboring ranch Briar Ridge, Val makes an offer to buy some of Jack's land.

items.title: Coming Together
items.description: Ashley Stanton reluctantly seeks Amy's aid with her horse Apollo when Ashley's domineering mother threatens to sell him. Meanwhile, Ty tries to share a pressing secret.

items.title: Ghost Horse
items.description: Amy's birthday party isn't the only surprise when she discovers that Ty has returned to Heartland.

items.title: Letting Go
items.description: A wild mustang forces Amy and Ty to examine their own issues.

items.title: Gift Horse
items.description: Amy is having a hard time keeping up with school, her chores, and her competitions on the show jumper Storm.

items.title: Dancing in the Dark
items.description: The simmering rivalry between Ty and Caleb for Amy's affections erupts and triggers a stampede.

items.title: Corporate Cowgirls
items.description: Lou pairs up with Tim to lead a group of young career women on an overnight trail ride.

items.title: Holding Fast
items.description: Amy devotes herself to working with a police horse that has been traumatized by an accident.

items.title: Sweetheart of the Rodeo
items.description: Amy backs Soraya in becoming the rodeo queen while helping to pull Ashley out of a downward spiral.

items.title: The Long Road Home
items.description: Scott and Tim join forces with the Flemmings to deal with a truckload of sick horses.

items.title: Cattle Call
items.description: Jack is upset when Tim hires Ty and Caleb to watch over his cattle.

items.title: True Enough
items.description: When Amy's teacher, Ms. Adams, brings a horse names Boxer to Heartland, Amy learns a lesson.

items.title: Starstruck
items.description: When Hollywood comes to Heartland, Amy is so starstruck she loses track of what's really important.

items.title: The Divorce Horse
items.description: Lisa meddles into Lou's business and personal life with disastrous results.

items.title: Seismic Shifts
items.description: Lou goes head to head with big Bedford Oil when seismic surveyors force their way onto Heartland.

items.title: Do or Die
items.description: Clint brings two tough kids on probation to Heartland, forcing Ty to deal with a part of his past.

items.title: Dark Horse
items.description: Lou resurrects the Hudson Derby, stirring up an age-old grudge between Jack and Tim.

items.title: The Ties that Bind
items.description: Once discovering that Spartan has been taken, Amy and Ty will stop at nothing to get him back.

items.title: Full Circle
items.description: Amy heads into the mountains to visit a horse healer and leaves with a new understanding.

items.title: Step by Step
items.description: Ty and Amy are finally forced to deal with their feelings for each other after being stranded.

items.title: Miracle
items.description: Amy is thrust into the limelight when she performs a “miracle” and a video of the event is posted.

items.title: Little Secrets
items.description: Amy is caught in the middle of a family crisis when she tries to help a girl after an accident.

items.title: Man's Best Friend
items.description: Jack's truck is getting old, forcing him to find the courage to say goodbye to part of his past.

items.title: The Haunting of Hanley Barn
items.description: Amy and Ty spend the night in the "haunted" Hanley barn, trying to get to the bottom of a mystery.

items.title: Glory Days
items.description: While shadowing Scott on a vet visit, Ty is thrown into an awkward situation with Kit and her pregnant mare. Tim and Jack relive their glory days.

items.title: Growing Pains
items.description: When Amy and Ty become parents of an orphaned foal, the strength of their relationship is tested.

items.title: The Starting Gate
items.description: Tim buys a racehorse from Lisa and puts everything on the line, including Amy, to win big.

items.title: The Fix
items.description: Ty protects his mother Lily from his abusive stepfather, who shows up at Heartland to win her back.

items.title: Broken Arrow
items.description: Amy is upset when Ty flies with Scott to a vet call on his last day before leaving for vet school.

items.title: Eye of the Wolf
items.description: Amy leads a search to find Ty and Scott, whose plane has gone missing in a forested mountain area.

items.title: Catch and Release
items.description: While the boys head off on a fishing trip, the girls are left back at Heartland to deal with problems.
