items.description: The Collinsville mural needs volunteers, but Holly’s jealousy of Piper’s friendship with Amy gets in the way. Robby and Lyla consider the future of their relationship and make plans.

items.title: The Crushing Criminal
items.description: Piper’s family is at risk of moving out of Collinsville; Holly takes matters in her own hands. Heather thinks her parents’ marriage is on edge and tries to reignite their love.

items.title: A Whole New Holly
items.description: Holly auditions for the town musical but needs to prove herself as a performer. Robby makes a mistake that changes his relationship with Lyla forever, but he has a plan to fix it.

items.title: The Thwarted Thespian
items.description: Holly struggles to balance school and her role in the musical, and hits a breaking point. Heather is perplexed by a mysterious girl at school, but giving her a chance leads to an unexpected friendship.

items.title: The Salty Songstress
items.description: Holly confronts Savannah for spreading lies about her and losing her spot in the musical. Heather asks her dad about a mysterious grandpa.

items.title: The Cranky Camper
items.description: The Hobbies go camping to get away from devices and and each of the kids’ personal drama. Piper works with her mom’s yard work business but she runs into an unexpected employer.

items.title: The Puzzled Peacemaker
items.description: Lyla makes a tweet that sparks controversy and Piper has a heart to heart with her about cultural appropriation. Robbie is inducted into the Association of Batting Cages and celebrates his masculinity.

items.title: The Night-Crawling Newbie
items.description: Holly, Piper, and Amy get invited to a party past curfew so they enlist the help of Robbie. Heather has a sleepover and gets convinced that ghosts are real.

items.title: The Perplexed Pioneer
items.description: Piper’s mom gets a new job that means the Parishs are moving. Robbie is chosen as team captain of the football team but he might need to give up immature pranks to be a leader.

items.title: The Dauntless Daughter
items.description: Holly isn’t allowed to have boys in her room and she struggles to make sense of it with her parents. Amy stands up against inequality she finds in the science fair.

items.title: The Hesitant Heroine
items.description: Holly and Oscar score a gig opening for a big musician named Gwen Taylor, but Holly gets in her head. Amy teams up with Robbie to present for the science fair. Her anxiety and feelings of incompetency set her back from having faith in her project.

items.title: The Selfless Starlet
items.description: Oscar and Holly need to work with a company that has unjust labor practices but Holly is conflicted about representing a company she doesn’t believe in. Heather tracks down her long-lost grandfather and tries out beekeeping to meet him.

items.title: The Jam Jam
items.description: The father of the Hobbie family, Robert, gets injured in a car accident and his recovery will be an expensive process. Holly hosts an open mic night to raise donations and Robbie and Heather are unexpectedly roped into the world of jam making.

items.title: The Shortsighted Scholar
items.description: Holly falls behind in her schoolwork because of the drama happening in her family; she must either read Little Women in one day or attend summer school. Heather panics over her baseball career and tries her hand at wrestling instead.

items.title: The Posing Performer
items.description: Piper helps Holly to put more effort into Holly’s social media platforms, but ends up sacrificing authenticity for maintaining the perfect image. Robbie’s new job isn’t what he expected, and his first paycheck is even worse.

items.title: The Grandpa Grenade
items.description: Holly wrestles with the internal struggle of whether or not she should accept her estranged grandfather. Heather loses her brand new baseball mitt and tries to earn money to replace it by selling candy at school.

items.title: The Bumbling Bossgirl
items.description: Holly listens to too many opinions for her music video and loses her say in the project. Robbie has troubles writing for the newspaper and discovers that the problem is deeper than he thought and he may have dysgraphia.

items.title: The Slimy Sensation
items.description: Holly tries to grow her social media following with the help of Piper. Holly gets caught up in the influencer lifestyle and starts to lose time to do what she loves most. Amy conducts an experiment to see if gum improves memory.

items.title: The Horrible Hero
items.description: Heather is determined to discover the role of women in the history of Collinsville for a group project. Piper is commissioned by Holly to help with a pie fundraiser, but Piper still resents Holly.

items.title: The Fairweather Friend
items.description: Amy scrambles to find a date to the dance, but a huge storm derails her plans. Heather suspects that Robbie may be doing drugs, so she teams up with Lyla to investigate.

items.title: The Careening Counselor
items.description: Piper chooses between being a camp counselor with her friends and going to Paris with her mom. Robbie has a big job opportunity, but Heather comes up with a plan to make him stay home for the summer.

items.title: The Difficult Decision
items.description: Holly learns of a songwriting opportunity in Nashville. Grandma Hobbie plans to get married in a hasty town hall ceremony but the Hobbies decide to throw her a bigger celebration. Heather is trusted with a crucial part of wedding planning.

items.title: The Struggling Songwriter
items.description: Holly and Amy are disappointed to be separated during summer vacation. Holly starts a songwriting camp in Nashville. Amy works as a camp counselor and learns teamwork.

items.title: The Song Circle Surprise
items.description: Holly meets a big pop star. Robbie struggles with his food truck without the help of his mom.

items.title: The Bestie Bonfire
items.description: Amy struggles to keep a secret from Savannah. Heather gets roped into dance auditions, but then realizes she has some talent.

items.title: The Aspiring Ally
items.description: Justin opens Holly’s eyes to how others see him. Robbie recreates his first date with Lyla to put off an important conversation.

items.title: The Reticent Rulemaker
items.description: Oscar gets jealous when Holly starts writing songs with Justin. Heather hides her new dance hobby from her dad.

items.title: The Anxious Achiever
items.description: Justin helps Amy come to terms with her anxiety diagnosis. Heather learns to compromise when her field trip gets canceled.

items.title: The Collinsville Conspiracist
items.description: Holly grows suspicious of Justin. Robby makes a big decision about his relationship with Lyla.

items.title: The Defiant Dancer
items.description: Holly learns about Amy and Justin’s secret. Heather is uncomfortable with aspects of her dance competition and learns to stand up for what she believes in.

items.title: The Cowering Confidant
items.description: Robert is hesitant to open his barbeque restaurant and needs a confidence boost. Justin plans a spontaneous trip with Amy.

items.title: The Friendship Fiasco
items.description: Holly and Amy’s friendship is tested when Justin leaves unexpectedly. Heather gets to the bottom of a rumor that could be devastating to her friends.

items.title: The Accidental Activist
items.description: Heather is dress coded for wearing a tank top and speaks up about the injustice on the internet. Lyla and Robbie argue over weighty real estate decisions, and Robbie makes a hasty purchase.

items.title: The Defensive Driver
items.description: Holly feels a new sense of independence when she gets her driver’s license, but learns that with more independence comes even more responsibility. Heather finds herself excluded when she joins the boy’s football team.

items.title: The Engrossed Essayist
items.description: Amy struggles to write her college essay. She decides to install wheelchair ramps around town for a better essay, but Holly and Savannah think the ramps are going overboard. Heather juggles dance and rugby and realizes that she can’t keep both.

items.title: The Vexed Volunteer
items.description: Shortly after her breakup with Oscar, Holly discovers that he’s deleted all of their pictures online. She’s forced to work with him at the pickle festival and suspects he’s already dating again. Heather worries she’s becoming a third wheel.

items.title: The Big City Belter
items.description: Holly gets an audition at NYU, but is blind sighted with a music theory test that she’s unprepared for. Robbie is faced with a decision between his own gain and treating his employees right.

items.title: The Vegan Veteran
items.description: Amy’s anxiety grows when she watches a documentary about climate change. She realizes that it goes too far when she protests a BBQ fundraiser organized by her friends. Heather gets hurt during rugby and learns to prioritize her health.

items.title: The Adamant Athlete
items.description: Heather discovers that her school gives 90% of its sports funding towards boys’ teams and decides to take a stand. Holly finds a gig for her band, but Amy and Savannah aren’t as enthusiastic.

items.title: The Disappointed Dreamer
items.description: Holly finds that teaching music at the Children’s Club is more difficult than she thought. Heather rushes to build the crib for the new baby so she could join her friends at the movies.

items.title: The Panicky Promgoer
items.description: Holly gets overwhelmed with post-grad plans and lets the stress interrupt her senior prom. Amy avoids going to prom to prepare for an important interview when she knows how much it means to Savannah.

items.title: A New Beginning
items.description: With the loss of her dream job, Holly searches for her calling that will satisfy her passions in life. She’s conflicted when it comes to songwriting and philanthropy. The Hobbie family prepares for the new baby.

items.title: What is "Holy"?
items.description: We introduce Justyna Hrabska and preview the nine "holy" adventures in the series.

items.title: The Center of the Center
items.description: Discover the complex and longtime significance of the circle and its "center" in Sicily. Find out what the "center of the center" is for Sicilians and learn about the short but inspirational life of Santa Lucia.

items.title: The Stone of Jacob
items.description: Discover the story of a sacred stone and its significance to the kings and queens of England.

items.title: Sacred Trail
items.description: Discover the stories and sacred Wyoming trail of the Martin and Willie handcart companies.

items.title: The Tsodilo Hills of Botswana
items.description: Travel to the Kalahari Desert to learn about the oldest "holy" site on Earth.

items.title: Holy Mathematics
items.description: Discover how several mathematical principles sprang from deep spiritual roots in India.

items.title: Sacred Landscapes
items.description: Learn about the American West landforms that are sacred to the Lakota Sioux.

items.title: Remembering, Part One: Yad Vashem
items.description: Explore Yad Vashem, the World Holocaust Remembrance Center in Jerusalem.

items.title: Remembering, Part Two: Joseph and Rebecca
items.description: Explore the recovery of the post-WWII Jewish community in Poland, Justyna's homeland.

items.title: Wise Men from the East
items.description: Discover the legacy of the Wise Men at the great cathedral of Cologne in Germany.

items.title: Hometown Remedy
items.description: Adele, a big-city surgeon set on furthering her career returns to her small hometown of Versailles for a week after her father becomes Mayor. She meets Grant, the local doctor who is trying to help the town, and romance sparks.

items.title: Hope Dances
items.description: Under pressure from her parents, Hope must choose between softball and ballet. After making her choice, she must navigate the tests of loyalty, dedication, and what it truly means to be both a competitor and a friend—even when challenges arise.

items.title: How I Got Here Season 1 Trailer
items.description: How I Got Here Season 1 Trailer

items.title: Zimbabwe: She Has Arrived
items.description: Fikile and her dad, Bangane, travel to his homeland in Zimbabwe for the first time. Bangane teaches Fikile the rich history of their family, and she gains a deeper appreciation for their Ndebele culture.

items.title: Italy: Making Peace and Pizza
items.description: Michael and his dad, John, travel to Italy together for the first time. Despite their sometimes rocky relationship, these two find themselves working together to explore the culture that has shaped each of them and may help them reconnect for good.

items.title: Zambia: Born for Greatness
items.description: Manasseh and his mom, Nelly, and return to Zambia to reconnect with family and tackle the unanswered questions in their own relationship. Manasseh gains a deeper appreciation of his Zambian heritage and makes peace with his own past.

items.title: Serbia: Two Rivers Intertwined
items.description: Aleksander returns to Serbia for the first time in almost 30 years, traveling with his son, Sebastian, to discover the places and people left behind during the Kosovo war. Sebastian searches for a better understanding of his heritage and his father.

items.title: Zimbabwe: Like Time Stood Still
items.description: Shaun travels back to Zimbabwe to face the land he loves and the political climate that forced him to leave. His daughter Shannon begins to embrace her personal identity as a bi-racial woman.

items.title: Slovakia: My Mom, the Mountain Goat
items.description: Simona returns to Slovakia, a country she left during a time of oppression, with her daughter, Vivian. Together they explore their Slovak heritage and Vivian learns about the sacrifices Simona made when she fled Slovakia over twenty years ago.

items.title: Ghana: That Name That You Live
items.description: Doris takes her daughter, Shetin, to Ghana to learn the truth behind her royal bloodline.

items.title: Chile: A Tree and Its Roots
items.description: Carolina travels to Chile with her mom, Ines, to uncover her heritage. Ines reveals the challenges she faced living under a dictatorship and introduces Carolina to the strong women in her family, giving her daughter insight into Ines’s fiery nature.

items.title: Israel: Young Man, Walking Up
items.description: Leo travels to Israel with his mom, Maya, to untangle his Israeli-Japanese heritage. On this adventure of a lifetime, Leo is ready to be thrown into a culture he’s had little connection with and is ready to watch his mom find herself as well.

items.title: Mexico: I Belong To This Land
items.description: Alma returns to Mexico with her daughter, Amanda to reunite with family and celebrate the life of a passed loved one. Amanda will join her mother in their shared love of traditional food and dance and a journey through Mexico’s magical heritage.

items.title: Cuba: Forgive the Past
items.description: After an eleven-year estrangement, Jordan and his father, Adonis, have reconnected. Now, they’ll travel to Adonis’ home country of Cuba for Jordan to discover their family’s rich musical legacy and reunite with generations of relatives.

items.title: Korea: A Forever Sense of Self
items.description: Kaelyn knows little of her Korean heritage. Her grandfather, Hae Suk, moved to Canada as a young man and hasn’t shared much of his difficult past with his family. Together, they travel to South Korea so Hae Suk can share his story with Kaelyn.

items.title: France: Say Their Names
items.description: Twenty years ago, Philippe left his homeland in the South of France. Now, he and his daughter, Valentine, travel back to uncover the truth about their family & reconnect with the vibrant French culture.

items.title: Trinidad: That's the Love
items.description: Andy and his daughter Alexandria travel to Andy’s home country of Trinidad. As they visit with family and friends, Alexandria learns about her father’s complicated childhood and Andy tries to reconcile with his feelings toward his father.

items.title: Kosovo: The Cry of Man is Singing
items.description: As a young journalist, Naser witnessed the atrocities of the war in Kosovo, his home country. Now, his fifteen-year-old son, Ander, feels his father has unresolved pain around his experiences. Together, the two travel back to Kosovo.

items.title: Vietnam: Pearls of the Dragon
items.description: Amy’s father, Dan, escaped the Vietnam War when he was a young boy. Amy knows little about her dad’s past and wishes she could connect with him better. Together, they travel to Vietnam to explore the country and Dan’s history.

items.title: Romania: A Secret Departure
items.description: Aleck cherishes his Romanian roots but is unaware of his mom’s past. After secretly escaping communist rule, Gabriela doesn’t talk about her life in Romania. Now, ready to open up, she takes Aleck to Romania to seek closure and embrace his identity.

items.title: Northern Ireland: Waves of Trouble
items.description: Bill grew up in the epicenter of Northern Ireland’s bloody conflict. Sophie, Bill’s teenage daughter, grew up in Canada and doesn’t feel connected to her Irish roots. Ready to help her dad heal, Sophie travels back to Northern Ireland with Bill.

items.title: Vietnam: The Kite Flies Free
items.description: Hannah escaped Vietnam during the war, leaving most of her family behind. Decades later, her trauma has clouded memories of her past. Now her daughter, Kyana, is seeking answers about her identity. Together they travel to Vietnam to find answers.

items.title: Kenya: Home Is a Feeling
items.description: Jamila is Kenyan-Canadian & feels very disconnected from her culture. Recently reunited with her dad, Abdul, after years apart, she’ll travel to Kenya with him to uncover her Kenyan identity and strengthen their relationship.

items.title: Tonga: Tomorrow Is Never Promised
items.description: Harboring resentment towards his father, Pasi hopes that traveling with him to native Tonga will provide a way for the two to make peace with their turbulent past.

items.title: Japan: Unmasking The Past
items.description: Knowing little of her Japanese heritage, Lacey travels to Japan with her father to reconnect with the sights, sounds, and flavors of his childhood.

items.title: Latvia: Newfound Family
items.description: Twins Ashley and Anthony grapple with the unresolved pain of their mother’s decision to leave her homeland of Latvia.

items.title: Thailand: Mom’s Home Cooking
items.description: On a trip to Thailand, Tyler uncovers his mother Diane's vibrant past and her deep culinary roots, while exploring her private connection to Buddhism and bridging the emotional distance left by grief and loss.

items.title: Poland: Secrets Revealed
items.description: Tula was shocked to learn of her mother’s bleak childhood with food rationing and poor living conditions under communism in Świdnica, Poland. Now with Tula hungry to know everything about her mother’s life, the two of them travel to Poland together.

items.title: Philippines: Voice of Generations
items.description: Angelina meets her Filipino family for the first time and discovers the hidden grief her mother carried for decades.

items.title: Germany: Where Do I Belong?
items.description: Wracked with generational guilt over her great-grandparents’ Nazi ties, Sarah and her father journey to the former East Germany, where she finds hope in ways she never expected.

items.title: Greece: Home is Here
items.description: Georgia’s mother parted from her parents in Greece on bad terms at only sixteen years old. Now, Georgia is desperate to connect with her Greek heritage and to have a better relationship with her own mother.

items.title: I Am: The Journey
items.description: A celebration of global Latter-day Saint voices through art, music, and dance that honors diverse cultural legacies within the artistic community. Presented by the Center for Latter-day Saint Arts.

items.title: I Need Thee Every Hour by BYU Men’s Chorus
items.description: Listen to the BYU Men's Chorus perform I Need Thee Every Hour, a beloved Christian hymn about seeking God's guidance, comfort, and strength. Rich choral harmonies bring a timeless prayer of faith to life in this reverent and uplifting performance.

items.title: In Christ Alone by BYU Concert Choir
items.description: Listen to the BYU Concert Choir perform In Christ Alone, a beloved Christian hymn celebrating hope, faith, and strength through Jesus Christ. Beautiful choral harmonies invite reflection on the Savior's love, grace, and resurrection. Listen in faith.

items.title: In the Bleak Midwinter by BYU Concert Choir and BYU Philharmonic
items.description: Listen to the BYU Concert Choir and BYU Philharmonic perform In the Bleak Midwinter, a beloved Christmas carol celebrating the humble birth of Jesus Christ. Choral harmonies and orchestral music bring warmth, peace, and wonder to the holiday season.

items.title: Fall Training Camp Begins (9-1-15)
items.description: The BYU football team arrives for fall training camp. Part 1 of 2.

items.title: Fall Training Camp Begins - Part 2 (9-1-15)
items.description: The BYU football team arrives for fall training camp. Part 2 of 2.

items.title: BYU Triumphs in Nebraska (9-8-15)
items.description: Follow the team off the field and get the emotional inside scoop on Taysom Hill's season-ending injury, and Tanner Mangum's game-winning pass.

items.title: BYU Gears Up for Boise State (9-15-15)
items.description: With an incredible win in its pocket and a new starting quarterback, the BYU football team is now up against rival Boise State.

items.title: BYU Tries to Extend Winning Streak in UCLA (9-22-15)
items.description: After a streak of exciting wins, the Cougars prepare for a showdown against tenth-ranked UCLA.

items.title: Cougars Rally after a Hard Loss (9-29-2015)
items.description: The Cougars turn the highs and lows of the rollercoaster season into learning opportunities.

items.title: The Bounce Back of BYU (10-6-2015)
items.description: Fueled by determination despite setbacks, the Cougars turn their attention to the UConn Huskies.

items.title: Homecoming Week (10-13-15)
items.description: The Cougars talk teamwork, commitment, and balance in preparation for their Homecoming win.

items.title: The Cougars Prep for the Bearcats (10-20-15)
items.description: See what a day in the life of a Cougar is like, and watch the team prepare to battle Cincinnati.

items.title: Crushing Home Victory (10-27-15)
items.description: With a home game against Wagner on the horizon, see how young players like Beau Hoge prepare to enter the contest.

items.title: Bye Week (11-3-15)
items.description: During their bye week, the Cougars stay focused but still make time for Halloween hijinks.

items.title: On the Road Again (11-10-15)
items.description: BYU ramps up the intensity of their workouts ahead of Friday's game against San Jose State.

items.title: Battle in Missouri (11-17-15)
items.description: Experience all the best action up close as the Cougars face off against the Missouri Tigers.

items.title: Senior Night (11-24-15)
items.description: It's the last home game of the season, and the Cougars play hard against Fresno State to remain undefeated at LaVell Edwards Stadium this year.

items.title: The Last Stretch (12-1-15)
items.description: Watch the Cougars celebrate Thanksgiving and take on rival Utah State this week.

items.title: Bowl Game against the Rivals (12-22-15)
items.description: News of Coach Mendenhall's departure breaks, and the team prepares for the bowl game in Las Vegas.

items.title: Bowl Game against the Rivals - Part 2 (12-22-15)
items.description: Join the team as they take on Utah at the Las Vegas Bowl and welcome Coach Kalani Sitake to BYU.

items.title: Isaiah 6
items.description: Religious scholars introduce the book of Isaiah and discuss Isaiah’s character, history, writing and prophesying styles and calling as found in chapter 6 in the book of Isaiah. With Richard Draper, Robert Millet, Ann Madsen, and Victor Ludlow.

items.title: Isaiah 1-2 S
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 1 and 2 which detail Isaiah’s prophetic teaching to Israel about repenting from their apostate state and remembering their covenants. With Richard Draper, Robert Millet, Ann Madsen, and Victor Ludlow.

items.title: Isaiah 3-5
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the pride and disobedience that is abundant among the children of Israel and the parable of the vineyard as described in Isaiah chapters 3 through 5. With Richard Draper, Robert Millet, Ann Madsen, and Victor Ludlow.

items.title: Isaiah 7 - 8
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 7 and 8 which detail Syria and Israel waging war against Judah and the Messianic sign given to King Ahaz. With Victor Ludlow, Terry Szink, Ann Madsen, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 9 - 11
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the Messianic prophecy listing many names of Christ and parallel of the destruction of Assyria as described in Isaiah chapters 9 through 11. With Victor Ludlow, Terry Szink, Ann Madsen, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 12 - 14
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 12 through 14 which detail the destruction of Babylon as a parallel to the Second Coming as well as the Millennium that will follow. With Victor Ludlow, Terry Szink, Ann Madsen, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 15 - 17
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the condemnation of the lands of Moab and Damascus as well as the scattering of Israel as described in Isaiah chapters 15 through 17. With Terry Ball, Terry Szink, Michael Rhodes, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 18 - 20
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 18 through 20 which detail the prophecy of the destruction and later restoration of the land of Egypt. With Terry Ball, Terry Szink, Michael Rhodes, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 21 - 23
items.description: Religious scholars discuss prophecies of destruction of many nations and of the captivity of the people of Jerusalem as illustrated in Isaiah chapters 21 through 23. With Terry Ball, Terry Szink, Michael Rhodes, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 24 - 26
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 24 through 26 which detail the earth’s state of apostasy before Christ’s Second Coming and the promise of resurrection for all. With Richard Draper, Paul Hoskisson, Michael Rhodes, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 27 - 28
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the chastening and gathering of Israel in the last days and the pride that caused the ten tribes to be lost as found in Isaiah chapters 27 and 28. With Richard Draper, Paul Hoskisson, Michael Rhodes, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 29
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapter 29 which prophesies the coming of the Book of Mormon and the restoration of the gospel after the apostasy. With Richard Draper, Paul Hoskisson, Michael Rhodes, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 30 - 31
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the chastisement and teaching Israel received from the Lord when they made an alliance with Egypt as described in Isaiah chapters 30 and 31. With Terry Ball, Jeff Chadwick, Michael Rhodes, and Ann Madsen.

items.title: Isaiah 32 - 33
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 32 and 33 which detail Christ’s reign as king, judge and lawgiver after His Second Coming and the types of Christ that exist in the scriptures. With Terry Ball, Jeff Chadwick, Michael Rhodes, and Ann Madsen.

items.title: Isaiah 34 - 35
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the destruction and judgment preceding the Second Coming of Jesus Christ and the redemption that will come after it as described in Isaiah chapters 34 and 35. With Terry Ball, Jeff Chadwick, Michael Rhodes, and Ann Madsen.

items.title: Isaiah 36 - 37
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 36 and 37 which details King Hezekiah’s conflict with Assyria and Isaiah’s prophecies the defeat of Assyria. With Paul Hoskisson, Jeff Chadwick, Ray Huntington, and Ann Madsen.

items.title: Isaiah 38 - 39
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Hezekiah’s life being lengthened due to his righteousness and faith and Isaiah’s prophecies regarding Babylon as described in Isaiah chapters 38 and 39. With Paul Hoskisson, Jeff Chadwick, Ray Huntington, and Ann Madsen.

items.title: Isaiah 40 - 41
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 40 and 41 where Isaiah speaks about the Messiah and how we need to prepare the way for His coming and how He will care for us. With Paul Hoskisson, Jeff Chadwick, Ray Huntington, and Ann Madsen.

items.title: Isaiah 42 - 43
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the servant songs found in Isaiah chapters 42 and 43 which describe the judgment of to the Gentiles and the power of the Savior. With Andrew Skinner, Richard Draper, Terry Ball, and Victor Ludlow.

items.title: Isaiah 44 - 45
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the Lord’s power to pour our blessings and His condemnation of idolatry and the prophecy of Cyrus ending Israel’s captivity in Isaiah chapters 44 and 45. With Andrew Skinner, Richard Draper, Terry Ball, and Victor Ludlow.

items.title: Isaiah 46 - 48
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 46 through 48 which detail the fall of Babylon and how idols are nothing as compared with the Lord, who can do all things. With Andrew Skinner, Richard Draper, Terry Ball, and Victor Ludlow.

items.title: Isaiah 49 - 51
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the elements of covenants and the relationship between Christ and His church as described in Isaiah chapters 49 through 51. With Victor Ludlow, Jeff Chadwick, Richard Draper, and Paul Hoskisson.

items.title: Isaiah 52 - 53
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the prophecies of redemption in the last days in Isaiah chapters 52 and 53 which are referenced in the Book of Mormon and the Doctrine and Covenants. With Victor Ludlow, Jeff Chadwick, Richard Draper, and Paul Hoskisson.

items.title: Seek Ye The Lord: Isa. 54-55
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 54 and 55 which detail the stakes of Zion that will be established in the last days to gather the lost tribes of Israel. With Victor Ludlow, Jeff Chadwick, Richard Draper, and Paul Hoskisson.

items.title: Isaiah 56 - 57
items.description: Religious scholars discuss how all who keep the commandments are welcome to join Israel regardless of personal or family history as taught in Isaiah chapters 56 and 57. With Terry Ball, Victor Ludlow, Terry Szink, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 58 - 59
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 58 and 59 which detail the proper way to fast and keep the Sabbath day as well as why Israel is separated from God and how they will return. With Terry Ball, Victor Ludlow, Terry Szink, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 60 - 61
items.description: Religious scholars discuss who is considered part of the House of Israel in the last days and Christ’s millennial reign as described in Isaiah chapters 60 and 61. With Terry Ball, Victor Ludlow, Terry Szink, and Ray Huntington.

items.title: Isaiah 62 - 64
items.description: Religious scholars discuss Isaiah chapters 62 through 64 which teach of the gathering of Israel using the metaphor of marriage and of the Second Coming as a day of vengeance. With Richard Draper, Jeff Chadwick, Victor Ludlow, and Andrew Skinner.

items.title: Isaiah 65 - 66
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the rejection of Ancient Israel and the rise of the great nation of Israel at the Second Coming of Christ as described in Isaiah chapters 65 and 66. With Richard Draper, Jeff Chadwick, Victor Ludlow, and Andrew Skinner.

items.title: My Soul Delighteth In His Words
items.description: Religious scholars discuss the Isaiah chapters in the Book of Mormon and the topics of covenants, the last days, and the Messiah that are covered in them. With Richard Draper, Jeff Chadwick, Victor Ludlow, and Andrew Skinner.

items.title: Instrument of War
items.description: First Lieutenant Clair Cline is taken as a prisoner of war in Germany, where he befriends the other prisoners and helps them and himself through this difficult time in creative and caring ways including building a violin to play for the camp.

items.title: Cyclone Impressions
items.description: ISU fans give their best Cyclone impressions.

items.title: Does Iowa Know BYU?
items.description: Malik Moore asks ISU fans what they know about BYU.

items.title: Emily Ryan at the 2023 Big 12 Media Days
items.description: Emily Ryan sits down with BYUSN to talk about past successes, her style of play, what makes Iowa State special, and the Big 12 conference.

items.title: How ISU Ice Cream is Made
items.description: Malik Moore learns how ISU Creamery Ice Cream is made on campus.

items.title: ISU Facts with Malik
items.description: Malik Moore gives fun facts about the ISU mascot.

items.title: Jack Trice’s Legacy with Malik Moore
items.description: Malik Moore reflects on Jack Trice’s legacy and what it means for him.

items.title: Malik Tries ISU Ice Cream
items.description: Malik Moore tries every ISU Ice Cream, and ranks his favorite.

items.title: Nyamer Diew at the 2023 Big 12 Media Days
items.description: Dyamer Diew sits down with BYUSN to discuss excitement for the season, the Iowa State atmosphere, excitement to visit Utah, and where to go in Ames.

items.title: Robert Jones at the 2023 Big 12 Media Days
items.description: Rober Jones sits down with BYUSN to talk about being a leader on the team, team chemistry, and playing at Hilton.

items.title: Tamin Lipsey at the 2023 Big 12 Media Days
items.description: Tamin Lipsey sits down with BYUSN to discuss growing up an Iowa State fan, being a returning player, and playing in Ames.

items.title: What Sport Does Malik Play
items.description: Malik Moore asks ISU fans what sport they think he plays.

items.title: Bill Fennelly: 2024 Media Days
items.description: BYUSN and Billy Fennelly discuss this year's excitement around Iowa State's football and basketball seasons.

items.title: Legato Line
items.description: Reid Nibley, the composer of the hymn “I Know My Father Lives” and an accomplished concert pianist, overcomes his fear of performing and a rocky relationship with his mother to create the legacy that still stands.

items.title: The Heart of Texas
items.description: After the tragic death of their young daughter, Grover Norwood and his family choose forgiveness when they learn a close friend was responsible, inspiring a community through faith, compassion, and grace.

items.title: Breaking The Curse
items.description: The remarkable story of Becky Douglas and Padma Venkataraman, whose efforts help people affected by leprosy in India build businesses, gain dignity, and create better futures for their children.

items.title: A Bridge to China
items.description: A group of youth dancers, singers, and musicians from China tour the United States to share their culture. They perform at BYU Hawaii with the Mormon Tabernacle Choir.

items.title: Adrian Anantawan: Story Behind The Notes
items.description: One-handed violinist Adrian Anatawan shares his story and his love for music. He has performed with the Toronto Symphony and the Cutis Institute of Music.

items.title: The Kennedy Way
items.description: Ambassador and Secretary of the Treasury for the United States David Kennedy lived a life that was devoted to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints. Friends and family share his story.

items.title: James Christensen
items.description: Fantastical artist James C. Christensen had to overcome family struggles and harsh criticism to achieve his dreams. Now he has painted for the Utah Shakespeare Festival and Governor Gary Herbert.

items.title: Soul of Kalaupapa: Voices in Exile
items.description: In Kalaupapa, Hawaii, leprosy survivors share their stories of what life was like being isolated from their families and building a community out of tragedy.

items.title: Wayne Quinton
items.description: Coming from very humble beginnings, Wayne Quinton invented kidney dialysis and many other inventions that saved thousands of lives. Some call him the original bioengineer.

items.title: Bill Child
items.description: President of RC Willey Bill Child shares his story of how he turned the biggest challenges of his life and turned them into success.

items.title: Honoring A Father's Dream
items.description: Milton Ochieng follows his father's dream to build the first health clinic in Iwala, Africa, by studying at Vanderbilt University Medical Center and Dartmouth University. He dreams to save the lives of many in his community.

items.title: Journey To Everest
items.description: A group of travelers dream of climbing Mount Everest. They encounter many struggles and tragedies along the way that may stop that dream from becoming a reality.

items.title: Africa Rising
items.description: Forty Ethiopian men and women use their skills to transform their community into a thriving society with tens of thousands of skilled workers.

items.title: A Song For Africa
items.description: Orphans in Uganda, Africa, are selected to join the Watoto Children’s Choir and perform on a tour across North America. Their song stands as a testament that music can overcome any tragedy.

items.title: Honeymoon In Kabul
items.description: Australian newlyweds Maggie Haertsch and Jean-Paul Bell bring medical aid and humor to a community in Afghanistan.

items.title: Caravan Of Books
items.description: Gellow, a camel in Kenya, Africa, transports books across the Semi Desert to bring stories to children and families in nomad communities.

items.title: Ordinary Life - Ben's Road to Glory
items.description: Ben Southern was born with down syndrome, but despite all the challenges, he has fought to compete in the Special Winter Olympics in figure skating for his country, New Zealand.

items.title: Ordinary Life - Journey of the Nz Wheelbacks
items.description: The New Zealand Wheel Blacks share their stories of being quadriplegic athletes and compete in the world wheelchair rugby championships.

items.title: It is Well with My Soul by BYU Concert Choir
items.description: Listen to the BYU Concert Choir perform It Is Well with My Soul, a beloved Christian hymn about finding peace and strength through faith. Beautiful choral harmonies bring a timeless message of hope, comfort, and trust in Jesus Christ to life.

items.title: Elementary
items.description: Itch obtains an unusual rock and discovers it could be a new element. But when everyone at school gets sick, Itch wonders if the rock is to blame.

items.title: Chronic Boom Boy
items.description: Itch is unimpressed by suave new boy Tim, but he has bigger fish to fry when Flowerdew arranges to have the rock sent away for testing. Itch must get the rock back before it's too late.

items.title: Trust No One
items.description: Itch discovers he is being followed by some scary-looking biker dudes. Tim helps Itch out, and Cake tells Itch the rock must be destroyed.

items.title: Rock 'n' Roll
items.description: Itch decides to get rid of the rock but instead is waylaid at the school rock concert where Chloe is playing.

items.title: Escape
items.description: Lucy, Jack, and Tim take the rock to the local mining institute for further testing in a bid to save Cake.

items.title: Hi-Tech, Lo-Fi
items.description: Helpless and lost in a new city, Itch, Tim, and Lucy try to track down Flowerdew and the rock. In Seaburgh, Darcy has an encounter with a biker.

items.title: Road Trip
items.description: While government agents question Lucy and Jack stalls Itch's mum, Itch continues his journey by bus, unaware that Tim is also on board.

items.title: Friends and Enemies
items.description: Itch and Tim struggle to survive in the harsh outback after evading police. Back in Seaburgh, Lucy, Jack, and Chloe work to uncover the truth about Greencorp.

items.title: End Game
items.description: After surviving the night in the outback, Itch hatches a plan to evade the evil powers trying to get the rock. Meanwhile, his dad and Australian Intelligence work to track him down.

items.title: 376 Down
items.description: A weak and sickly Itch risks his life by venturing into the dangerous unknown to ensure the rock remains hidden forever as Greencorp and the authorities close in.

items.title: Back with a Bang
items.description: Following an explosion and poisoned fish in the bay, Itch and his friends fear Greencorp are to blame and investigate.

items.title: Big Brother
items.description: Itch and his family move into a secure seafront mansion following an attack, while Itch and Lucy discover the beach water is toxic.

items.title: Confrontations
items.description: Tim throws a party to win back the trust of his friends and they hatch a plan to find out more about Greencorp’s plans.

items.title: A Game
items.description: Itch and Darcy go on a heist to the local Country Club, while Chloe gets to know her new friend Bella.

items.title: Small Town Hackers
items.description: In an effort to stall the grand beach reopening Itch and Jack try to prove the water is toxic, while Tim and Chloe access Lannister’s hard drive and make a major discovery.

items.title: Stakeout
items.description: The gang go on separate missions following information from Lannister laptop, leading them to uncover a secret location.

items.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
items.description: Itch and Tim meet a mysterious contact who holds valuable information on Greencorp, while Lucy uncovers a major secret that puts the gang at risk.

items.title: Special Ops
items.description: Itch, Lucy and Tim find out Greencorp’s evil plans and discover it could lead to widespread destruction.

items.title: No Turning Back
items.description: Itch, Tim and Lucy find themselves trapped at the hands of Greencorp, while Darcy and Jack race against time to get the only thing that can save them.

items.title: Last Goodbye
items.description: When Greencorp’s evil plan is put into action, the entire town of Seaburgh is at risk of major devastation, leaving Itch and the gang to save it before it’s too late.

items.title: Feeling the Beat
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Smith family to a game of Kitchen Charades, Sock Shuffleboard, and Shadow Guessing for a chance to win cash and prizes. Family friends surprise the Smiths with a life-changing prize.

items.title: Field of Jeans
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Sype family to a series of guessing games and friendly family competition for a chance to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Camp Tamburello
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Tamburello family to a game of Micro Money Maker, Taste Buds, Stairway Bowling, and Recycler Toss to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Dressed for Success
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Santos family to a game of kitchen addition, Coat Rack of Cash, Santos Sandwich Making Company, and Jeff’s Super-Duper Shuffle Game to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Sock It To Me
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Sanders family to a game of Channel Champs, Paper Towel Payout, Takeaway, Tabletop Drop, and Hallway “Sweep” Stakes to win cash and prizes.

items.title: You Gotta Have Faith
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Plescia family to a game of Toilet Paper Treasure Hunt, Refrigerator Recall, Gift Card Counter, and Weigh it and Pay it to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Yours, Mine, and Towers!
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Crother family to a game of Lucky Laundry, Now You See It, Pillow Tower, and Mini Golf Money Maker to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Floor of Lava!
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Smith family to a game of Hide and Seek, Cereal Train to Treasure, Stuffed Animal Instincts, and Floor of Lava to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Humpty Dumpty's Revenge
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Nollman family to a game of License Plate Lottery, Kitchen Magician, Picture Payday, House of Cards, and Humpty Dumpty to win cash and prizes.

items.title: The Family Who YouTubes Together
items.description: Host Jeff Rogers challenges the Riaz family to a game of Food Pyramid, Selective Memory, Lucky Call, Suck it Up, and Flip N’ Flyin’ Cereal to win cash and prizes.

items.title: Jimmer: The Lonely Master
items.description: This BYUtv original special features exclusive interviews with Jimmer Fredette on his NBA journey, his family, and his team. Footage of his personal life, childhood, and career give an inside look at the Shanghai Sharks basketball player’s career.

items.title: Joan of Arc
items.description: Joan of Arc was an inspired religious and military luminary who gave her life for the cause she was called to defend. Transcripts from her life and trial and experts are used to tell the story of this honorable symbol of resistance and faith.

items.title: Overview
items.description: The papers provide insights from Joseph through his correspondence, journals, discourses, and business dealings.

items.title: Joseph's Roots
items.description: Historians set the stage for Joseph Smith Jr.'s early years in New Hampshire and Vermont.

items.title: Joseph's America
items.description: Review the remarkable parallels between a young nation and its newest religion as they each struggled to develop their identity and destiny.

items.title: Palmyra
items.description: Palmyra is where young Joseph Smith and his family found themselves scraping to buy a farm, building a home, and then losing it all.

items.title: First Vision Beginnings
items.description: Hear the four versions of the First Vision given by the Prophet.

items.title: Four Accounts
items.description: Study Joseph's four accounts of the First Vision and the context that helps clarify the variations.

items.title: The Coming Forth of the Book of Mormon
items.description: Review the remarkable relationship between Joseph and the angel Moroni.

items.title: Harmony
items.description: Harmony is a story of miracles that would become the foundation for the restoration of the Church of Jesus Christ in the latter-days.

items.title: Priesthood
items.description: Review the remarkable events surrounding the restoration of the priesthood and pinpoint the appearance of the three ancient apostles.

items.title: The Papers People--Part 1
items.description: Meet five of the scholars whose work is central to compiling a complete and accurate documentary of Joseph Smith.

items.title: The Papers People--Part 2
items.description: Survey the complete process of gathering, scrutinizing, and organizing documents for publication.

items.title: The Translation of the Book of Mormon
items.description: Explore portions of the original manuscripts of the Book of Mormon and study the remarkable principles and questions that continue to surface.

items.title: Printing the Book of Mormon
items.description: Review the time-consuming process of typesetting a 600-page book with nineteenth-century equipment.

items.title: A Mother's Account
items.description: Examine the origin, motivation, and accuracy of "The History of the Prophet Joseph Smith" by Lucy Mack Smith.

items.title: History of a History
items.description: Dean Jesse discusses Joseph's anxiety over keeping the history of a work that would change human events forever.

items.title: Joseph's Journals
items.description: Explore the Prophet's personal journals to learn of his shortcomings, interpersonal conflicts, and challenges in leading the Saints into the future.

items.title: Oliver's Story
items.description: Study the life of Oliver Cowdery and witness his participation in the events of the Restoration, his apostasy, and his powerful closing testimony.

items.title: They Met the Prophet
items.description: Enjoy vibrant descriptions from those who met the Prophet. Whether one believed him or not, meeting Joseph Smith always left a deep impression.

items.title: Saving Joseph's Leg
items.description: Learn how Joseph and his family lived within a few miles of the only man alive who could have saved Joseph's life.

items.title: Joseph's New Translation--Part 1
items.description: Learn the history of Joseph's new translation of the Bible. Despite its significance, the manuscript was lost to the Church for over a century.

items.title: Joseph's New Translation--Part 2
items.description: Observe in detail the changes that Joseph made to restore the "plain and precious" meanings of the Bible.

items.title: The Letters of Joseph and Emma
items.description: Church history scholars review the papers that may have meant more to Joseph than any others: the letters between the Prophet and his wife.

items.title: Joseph Smith the Radical
items.description: The Prophet's claim to direct revelation was extremely radical. Nevertheless, the revelation he received restored doctrine and structured the Church.

items.title: April 6, 1830
items.description: Learn about the events surrounding the organization of the Church, including why six men were to become the founding fathers of Mormonism.

items.title: Kirtland Beginnings
items.description: Scholars discuss the years in Kirtland that were filled with miracles, divine revelation, and instruction.

items.title: Visions and Blessings, Tar and Feathers
items.description: Revisit the night when Joseph was tarred and feathered. Then, explore the difficulties and joys the Saints faced in their efforts to build a temple.

items.title: The Kirtland Temple: An Endowment of Power
items.description: Examine the few yet remarkable days in Kirtland that culminated with the appearance of the Savior.

items.title: Zion
items.description: Examine the idea of Zion and the role mobs and Mormons alike played in its failure. It was the greatest city that never came to be.

items.title: Zion's Camp
items.description: Travel through four states with 200 men to learn that the mission of Zion's Camp was more about the lessons of a journey than about the destination.

items.title: Crisis in Kirtland
items.description: Recount the dark days of Kirtland: financial failure, a riot in the temple, betrayal, and mutiny.

items.title: Joseph Smith and the Law--Part 1
items.description: Hundreds of newly discovered legal documents paint a new impression of the litigious environment surrounding the Mormon leader.

items.title: Joseph Smith and the Law--Part 2
items.description: Study the lawsuits Joseph faced throughout his life from his first encounter with the law at age 13 to the case of the Kirtland Safety Society.

items.title: The Mormon War
items.description: Historians recount the pivotal days that would eventually lead to expulsion from Missouri, captivity at Liberty, and a trek out West.

items.title: Liberty Jail
items.description: For Joseph Smith, Liberty Jail provided an experience that would be described as the most important leadership training the Prophet would receive.

items.title: Suffering and Salvation
items.description: With an extermination order in effect, thousands of destitute Saints huddled together in desperate circumstances in Missouri. The exodus begins.

items.title: The Mission of the Twelve to England
items.description: Detail the experience that transformed a group of faithful young men into a quorum who had great influence in the British Isles.

items.title: Land, Joseph and "Justice" in Missouri
items.description: Historians show how "the law" in Missouri held Joseph hostage to "legally" rid itself of Mormons.

items.title: Nauvoo Beginnings
items.description: Historians document the beginnings of Nauvoo, the beautiful city, and the implications from Joseph that it wouldn´t last for long.

items.title: "I Can Do Nothing for You."
items.description: Recount the meeting of the Prophet and the president in 1839, and learn Smith's candid assessment of the people and power of the nation's capital.

items.title: Joseph Smith's Sermons
items.description: Discuss how the Saints viewed the difference between Joseph's preaching and the revelations he received from God.

items.title: Jewel on the Mississippi
items.description: Review the remarkable design, organization of labor, and confluence of expertise that created the most notable structure along the Mississippi River.

items.title: A Pearl of Great Price
items.description: Recount the story of how a remarkable find in Egypt ended up half a world away in the hands of the one man who could translate the Abrahamic text.

items.title: Doctrines of Salvation
items.description: Examine a period of time in the early Church as Joseph introduces the doctrines that made the construction of a temple extremely urgent.

items.title: Joseph and the Relief Society
items.description: Scholars examine the first meetings of the Relief Society, including the admonition that the organization become a vital source in the church.

items.title: Living by the Law
items.description: Legal scholars document the legal wrangling that kept the Prophet on the defense during the Nauvoo years.

items.title: Going International
items.description: Explore the early foreign missions of the Church in Canada, the British Isles, Palestine, and the Pacific islands.

items.title: Gathering Clouds
items.description: Join scholars to discuss the fear and frustration of non-Mormons when Latter-day Saints became a political force.

items.title: Joseph Smith for President
items.description: Follow the Prophet's very unique entry into national politics including his opinions on the role of government.

items.title: Martyrdom
items.description: Learn about the events leading to the deaths of Joseph and Hyrum Smith.

items.title: Lamentation and Leadership
items.description: Scholars discuss the extraordinary events that led to consolidation of the Church's new leadership.

items.title: Who Will Lead? Who Will Follow?
items.description: Discuss the contention that arose over who would succeed Joseph Smith as the leader of the Church.

items.title: A Television Foreword
items.description: This intriguing documentary explores the ambitious effort to compile, transcribe, edit, and present the papers of, by, and directly related to the Latter-day Saint Prophet Joseph Smith.

items.title: Persona of a Prophet
items.description: Scholars address some compelling questions, such as how Joseph's physical stature may have impacted the way he worked, played, and defended himself.

items.title: Impressions of a Prophet--Part 1
items.description: Scholars recount the status of some of the many biographies and histories profiling the Prophet and his times.

items.title: Impressions of a Prophet--Part 2
items.description: Examine the increased interest in the Mormon prophet from those outside the faith, including the bicentennial celebration of Smith's birth, held at t

items.title: Joseph Smith Tour--Part 1: New England
items.description: Scholars visit New England, where the Smiths and the Macks, Joseph's noble heritage, originated.

items.title: Joseph Smith Tour Part 2: New York and Pennsylvania
items.description: Move through New York and Pennsylvania and through the beginnings of Mormonism.

items.title: Joseph Smith Tour--Part 3: Ohio
items.description: Visit places that figure prominently into what Latter-day Saints believe to be important to the restoration of Christ's gospel on the earth.

items.title: Joseph Smith Tour--Part 4: Missouri and Illinois
items.description: Discuss the significance of the City of Zion and recount the Saints' most severe persecution and hardship.

items.title: Joseph Smith Tour--Part 5: Illinois
items.description: Visit Nauvoo, Illinois, and learn of the significance of the original Nauvoo Temple and of the establishment of the Relief Society.

items.title: The Family of Joseph Smith--Part 1
items.description: Meet the two people who influenced Joseph Smith the most.

items.title: The Family of Joseph Smith--Part 2
items.description: Learn more about the Smith family, including which of Joseph's siblings stayed true to the faith and why some didn't.

items.title: The Family of Joseph Smith--Part 3
items.description: Acknowledge the thousands of descendants of Joseph and Emma and their divergent religious connections.

items.title: Teachings of Joseph Smith--Part 1
items.description: Examine the varied and exhaustive work undertaken to gather and make accessible the Prophet's teachings revealed to his people and to the world.

items.title: Teachings of Joseph Smith--Part 2
items.description: Learn of the monumental Teachings of the Presidents of the Church—Joseph Smith manual, which was the culmination of efforts by Latter-day Saint scholars.

items.title: The Music of Early Mormonism--Part 1
items.description: Scholars discuss the revelation directed to Emma Smith to compile a body of music that would reflect the doctrine and character of the faith.

items.title: The Music of Early Mormonism--Part 2
items.description: Examine the history of hymn books used and produced by early Latter-day Saints. Scholars discuss Joseph's love of music.

items.title: First Vision--Part 1
items.description: Scholars provide perspectives on how we have come to view the moment when a fourteen-year-old boy dared to ask God which church he should join.

items.title: First Vision--Part 2
items.description: Scholars present an intimate view of the actual document wherein Joseph describes the First Vision.

items.title: First Vision--Part 3
items.description: Scholars detail the emergence of the official version of the First Vision.

items.title: First Vision--Part 4
items.description: Scholars provide a panoramic view of the First Vision and address purported inconsistencies of the event.

items.title: First Vision--Part 5
items.description: Scholars discuss what Joseph learned about the physical nature of God and of discovering a personal relationship with Him.

items.title: Revelations and Translations--Part 1: Book of Mormon
items.description: Scholars discuss the revelations received by the Prophet and their eventual publication as part of the Latter-day Saint canon.

items.title: Revelations and Translations--Part 2: Book of Mormon
items.description: Scholars discuss Martin Harris and the lost manuscript and its dramatic impact on the Smith family.

items.title: Revelations and Translations--Part 3: Book of Mormon
items.description: Scholars examine the forms and structure of language in the Book of Mormon and challenge some common suppositions proposed by critics.

items.title: Revelations and Translations--Part 4: Doctrine and Covenants
items.description: Learn of the origins of the Doctrine and Covenants. Scholars discuss the unusual ways the early revelations were dispersed.

items.title: Revelations and Translations--Part 5: Coming Forth of the Doctrine and Covenants
items.description: Scholars discuss the genealogy of the Doctrine and Covenants in use today and why some rrevelations were canonized while others were not.

items.title: Pearl of Great Price
items.description: Scholars discuss the eventful history of the Pearl of Great Price, in particular its unusual beginnings.

items.title: Joseph Smith and His Papers--Part 1
items.description: Scholars describe the tools that provide readers with an exhaustive examination of content from original documents and the variety of annotations.

items.title: Joseph Smith and His Papers--Part 2
items.description: Scholars demonstrate how tools such as maps, chronologies, a biographical directory, and a Smith family pedigree can enrich reader's experiences.

items.title: Joseph Smith and His Papers--Part 3
items.description: Get introduced to the intricate treatment of documents containing the revelations received by Joseph Smith.

items.title: Word of Wisdom
items.description: Review the circumstances that led to the revelation on the Word of Wisdom and the difficulty many of the Saints had in abiding by its precepts.

items.title: Joseph Smith, the Statesman
items.description: Examine the Prophet's loyalty to the Constitution—a document he called "a glorious standard, a heavenly banner."

items.title: Doctrine and Covenants 76
items.description: Revisit the setting and circumstances of the revelation on the afterlife in Doctrine and Covenants 76.

items.title: Liberty Jail Letters
items.description: Dissect the letters dictated by Joseph Smith while in Liberty Jail.

items.title: The Pure Religion of Joseph Smith
items.description: Peer into the heart of the Prophet to examine how his Christian beliefs were reflected in his actions and his teachings and encased in his character.

items.title: Early Members--Part 1: Hyrum Smith
items.description: Recall the influential role Hyrum played in the Restoration and his unwavering support for his younger brother.

items.title: Early Members--Part 2: The Pratt Brothers, Parley and Orson
items.description: Meet Parley and Orson Pratt, who were instrumental in finding and baptizing future Latter-day Saints and their leaders.

items.title: Early Members--Part 3: William Clayton and the Knight Family
items.description: Review the lives of several prominent Latter-day Saints whose relationships with Joseph Smith were particularly close and steadfast.

items.title: Early Members, Part 4: Martin Harris and the John
items.description: Review the lives of several prominent Latter-day Saints whose relationships with Joseph Smith were particularly close and steadfast.

items.title: Early Members--Part 5: Eliza & Lorenzo Snow
items.description: Meet the Snows, whose deep imprints on the Church are still felt today.

items.title: Part 1, Question and Answer Forum, Conference Cent
items.description: Join a panel of Latter-day Saint scholars as they answer questions posed by students.

items.title: Part 2, Question and Answer Forum
items.description: Scholars from the project answer questions about skepticism, law and justice, and Joseph the businessman.

items.title: Season Finale
items.description: Get an overview of the whole project--the books, the website, and the television series; and meet the reason why it exists in the first place.

items.description: Jeremiah Morgan, Missouri Attorney General and Seventy, converted to the Church at 16. He attended BYU Law, met his wife, and built a legal career—playing a key role in the approval and construction of the Kansas City Missouri Temple.

items.title: Lexi Rydalch
items.description: Lexi Rydalch, former All-American BYU basketball star, opens up about the difficult decision she faced—whether to chase a pro career in the WBA or follow her lifelong dream of becoming a mom and raising a family.

items.title: Pete Grigsby
items.description: From high school hoops to weather maps — former ABC meteorologist Pete Grigsby discovered his passion for science and broadcasting early on, but it was during a mission in Utah that he truly found his calling in weather reporting.

items.title: Lauren Felker
items.description: High school junior Lauren Felker finds balance between her demanding broadcasting and medical classes by attending early morning seminary—and cherishes the chance to represent her faith in her home state of Missouri.

items.title: Jonathan Cutler
items.description: Jonathan Cutler shares how his faith and work in therapeutic horseback riding have shaped his journey—building deep connections with veterans and individuals with special needs, and revealing how every step in life prepares us for the next.

items.title: Cindy McDavitt
items.description: Cindy McDavitt, a member of the Kansas City Interfaith Council, is passionate about connecting civic and religious leaders. She frequently collaborates with church leaders on local initiatives, including the Light the World Campaign.

items.title: Shane Smeed
items.description: Shane Smeed, the President of Park University in Missouri, shares his passion on how education connects people to love of God. He shares his love for young adults, and how he and his wife have been able to serve a lot in many different respects.

items.title: Jenet Erickson
items.description: Dr. Jenet Jacob Erickson, a leading voice on motherhood and family, shares how her faith and research intersect. From BYU to national platforms, she offers heartfelt insights on why strong families shape lives—and why that work is sacred.

items.title: Charlene Farr & Wanda Mattox
items.description: Charlene Farr turned trials into testimony. At 87, she shares how a message of faith changed her life and inspired a legacy of service, storytelling, and connection across generations.

items.title: Kim Clark
items.description: Elder Kim B. Clark reflects on his path from Harvard to BYU–Idaho to Church leadership. His story highlights the power of faith, learning, and discipleship to transform lives.

items.title: Emily Peterson
items.description: Emily Peterson built Saranoni from love, grief, and hope. After her husband’s passing, she carried on their mission—bringing comfort to families worldwide through compassion and service.

items.title: BJ Allen
items.description: Dr. BJ Allen, marketing professor at Brigham Young University, and author of "The Compensating Power of Christ," discusses the power of Christ's Atonement to transform our human limits into divine possibilities.

items.title: John Fossum
items.description: John Fossum shares how Christ became his foundation through life’s challenges. His message of hope, drawn from personal experience and his book Spiritual Foundations, invites all to deepen their faith in uncertain times.

items.title: Shawn Stevens
items.description: Shawn Stevens left the spotlight to follow Christ. From TV fame to faith-driven sacrifice, his journey reveals how true peace comes from living with purpose—even when it means walking away from Hollywood.

items.title: Tom & Ali Durham
items.description: Tom and Ali Durham bring faith, family, and sci-fi together. The creative couple behind 95ers shares how their love of storytelling inspires uplifting projects—and a joy-filled life.

items.title: Hank Smith
items.description: Hank Smith, BYU professor, author, and co-founder of the Come, Follow Him podcast, shares how his journey led him to teaching, faith-filled storytelling, and a platform helping others engage more deeply with the scriptures.

items.title: Bruce Kusch
items.description: President Bruce C. Kusch reflects on nine years leading Ensign College and its transition from LDS Business College. He shares the story behind the name change, the school’s mission, and what it’s like directing a faith-centered college.

items.title: John Dye
items.description: John Dye works for Bonneville Distribution in premoting faith based material. With his skills in media, he is best known for his marketing and production talents. John is also known for speaking at faith based events about the ever growing media.

items.title: Lee Cummard
items.description: Lee Cummard, BYU women’s basketball head coach and former BYU player, shares his journey from being the sibling recruited to play college sports to competing professionally abroad, and how his education shaped his path to coaching women’s basketball.

items.title: Jonathan Wing
items.description: Jonathan Wing, a coordinator at FamilySearch, discusses his experiences with school and work, and reflects on growing up navigating multiple cultures.

items.title: Rod Gustafson
items.description: Rod Gustafson grew up in a family that loved television, sparking a passion that led him into broadcasting and movie rating, and eventually to the Church of Jesus Christ. He now works as a producer for BYUtv.

items.title: Roger Connors
items.description: Roger Connors, co-author of four New York Times and Wall Street Journal bestselling books on workplace accountability and culture change, and CEO of Human Performance Technologies, shares how joining the Church young shaped his path into leadership.

items.title: Devin Durrant
items.description: Devin Durrant shares his journey from the NBA to international basketball, real estate, serving as Texas Dallas Mission president, and the Sunday School General Presidency—reflecting on faith, leadership, and purpose along the way.

items.title: John Lewis
items.description: Join us as John Lewis discusses his journey from Mayor of Gilbert to Mission President in Cambodia. Now an Area Seventy, John shares insights on leadership, the explosive growth of the Church in Arizona, and the "Plan of Happiness" in Southeast Asia.

items.title: Cali Black
items.description: Join us as Cali Black discusses her journey from BYU educator to the creator of @ComeFollowMeStudy. Learn how her "One Minute Scripture Study" series and approachable teaching style are helping a new generation deeply root themselves in the Gospel.

items.title: Marc Lefevre
items.description: Join us for a conversation with Marc LeFevre, President of Outplacement Services at Careers Launch. Marc discusses the changing landscape of work, the power of professional branding, and how he uses his expertise to help people find new purpose.

items.title: Matt Riggs
items.description: Elder Matthew Riggs is an attorney who has shaped Arizona law and served as a Mission President, he shares how the Lord guided his career from driving a delivery truck to leading a major law firm and serving as an Area Seventy.

items.title: Jennifer Fenn
items.description: Join us as Arizona native Jennifer Fenn shares her experience serving as a missionary and coordinating FamilySearch at the Mesa Arizona Temple, offering a glimpse into the spirit and service visitors experience there.

items.title: Ryan Bingham
items.description: Ryan Bingham shares how lessons learned on the farm and during his mission in Chile helped shape his path in leadership, education, and business. Now a vice president at Honeywell, he reflects on his career journey through BYU–Idaho, BYU, and beyond.

items.title: Candice Copple
items.description: Candice Copple shares her journey from accounting to seminary education, local government, and public service, and how earning an MPA and President Nelson’s call to be a peacemaker shaped her leadership.

items.title: T.J. Packard
items.description: TJ Packard, CPA and partner at Packard, Appleby & Rogers P.C., shares how his upbringing in Arizona, years at BYU–Idaho, and mission in Brazil shaped his faith, career, and the relationships that helped lead him to where he is today.

items.title: Royce Bybee
items.description: Former BYU and Rick's College quarterback Royce Bybee shares the story of his conversion to the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and his current calling as Director of the Mesa Temple Visitors' Center in Arizona.

items.title: Jordan Abrams
items.description: Jordan Abrams shares his story growing up in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints in Idaho. Inspired by his family, he pursued this path and became an institute director for BYU Pathways in the southwest area.

items.title: Shima Baradaran Baughman
items.description: BYU Law professor Shima Baughman shares how her faith in Jesus Christ fuels her passion for criminal justice reform.

items.title: Ben Kjar
items.description: World Champion wrestler Ben Kjar describes the role of faith and resilience in his journey with Crouzon Syndrome.

items.title: Tanner Christensen
items.description: Director/Editor Tanner Christensen discusses the importance of faith in the film industry, and how he creates stories that testify of Christ.

items.title: Mary Richards
items.description: Church News reporter Mary Richards describes how she relies on the Savior to balance a career in journalism with raising five children.

items.title: Craig Manning
items.description: Sports psychologist and former D1 tennis coach Dr. Craig Manning describes how he elevates his faith through the same principles he teaches to high performance athletes.

items.title: Heather Nemelka
items.description: Heather Nemelka, CEO and founder of Elevare, discusses how faith in Christ allows women to embrace their full potential, even through family tragedy and career upheaval.

items.title: Latter-day Saint Image in the British Mind
items.description: How has The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints been perceived in Britain over the years? This film documents the efforts and faithfulness of the many who have contributed to the growth of this Christian faith within the British Isles.

items.title: Vulnerability
items.description: The journey begins for three groups of teens as they travel to Bolivia, Vanuatu, and Mongolia to serve the local people and find meaningful growth and spiritual healing.

items.title: The Outsiders
items.description: The teens in Bolivia and Vanuatu start building the foundation for new schools, while those in Mongolia begin work on a public bath with hot water. As they learn about the struggles of the locals, their own mental and spiritual trials are revealed.

items.title: The Pivot Point
items.description: The teens start finding joy in their service while facing their personal struggles. They begin constructing walls, laying foundations, and installing insulation. The teens also spend time with locals, and learn more about local culture.

items.title: The Good Path
items.description: In Bolivia, a teen learns how to serve when he can’t do physical labor. In Mongolia, another teen misses loved ones. In Vanuatu, a teen analyzes his relationship with God.

items.title: Yesterday's Scars
items.description: A teen in Mongolia struggles to connect with others. In Bolivia, a teen battles hopelessness. In Vanuatu, a teen works to overcome body image issues. Friendships are deepened and the final stages of their projects begin.

items.title: What We Carry Home
items.description: The groups finish their service projects and prepare for their return home, looking back on the personal growth, healing, and the friendships they've formed.

items.title: Vai Sikahema
items.description: Host Curt Doussett sits down with former BYU Football running back and return specialist Vai Sikahema and learns how his humble beginnings inspired his career as a professional football player.

items.title: Erin Thorn
items.description: Host Curt Doussett meets former BYU Women’s running guard Erin Thorn and learns how her experiences at BYU inspired her to play basketball professionally.

items.title: Tiffany Lott-Hogan
items.description: Olympian Tiffany Lott-Hogan shares how her experiences at the 2004 Athens Olympics shifted her perspective as a track and field athlete.

items.title: Tom Holmoe
items.description: BYU Athletic Director Tom Holmoe shares how his time playing for the San Francisco 49ers motivated him to return to his alma mater to mentor student athletes.

items.title: Ty Detmer
items.description: Heisman Trophy winner Ty Detmer shares how his experiences as a quarterback for BYU prepared him for his time in the NFL and for his career as a football coach.

items.title: Shauna Rohbock
items.description: Olympic bobsledder Shauna Rohbock sits down with Curt to discuss how her time as a BYU track star and soccer player led her to compete in the 2006 Winter Olympics.

items.title: Mike Schlappi
items.description: Mike Schlappi shares how his paralysis motivated him to become a successful Paralympian and motivational speaker.

items.title: Lavell Edwards
items.description: Host Curt Doussett sits down with legendary BYU Football coach LaVell Edwards and learns how Edwards created a lasting legacy after his 29 seasons as head coach for the Cougars.

items.title: Chad Lewis
items.description: Lewis may have been coaxed into his first BYU football tryout, but after joining the team his successes kept piling up.

items.title: Michele Fellows Lewis
items.description: Former BYU Volleyball star Michele Fellows Lewis describes her experience helping BYU to the 1993 Final Four and shares how her time on the court prepared her to be a mother.

items.title: Aleisha Cramer Rose
items.description: BYU Hall of Fame inductee Aleisha Cramer Rose talks about how she balanced playing for both the US Women’s National Soccer Team and BYU Women’s Soccer Team.

items.title: Ed Eyestone
items.description: Olympic marathoner Ed Eyestone shares his journey from cross country star to head coach of BYU Men’s Cross Country team.

items.title: Brandon Doman
items.description: Heisman Trophy winner Brandon Doman describes how he overcame his insecurities to become a star quarterback for the BYU Cougars.

items.title: Wally Joyner
items.description: Former MLB First Baseman Wally Joyner sits with host Curt Doussett to discuss his baseball career as he recounts his days as an underdog at BYU to his time playing professional baseball.

items.title: Jennifer Rockwood
items.description: Head coach for BYU Women’s Soccer Jennifer Rockwood shares how she led the team from club status to NCAA Division 1 champions.

items.title: Elaine Michaelis
items.description: Host Curt Doussett sits with BYU Legend Elaine Michaelis and learns how she made history as she paved the way for women's collegiate athletics across the nation.

items.title: Travis Hansen
items.description: Former BYU basketball star and shooting guard for the Atlanta Hawks Travis Hansen talks about his exciting career and the experiences that inspired him to devote his time to philanthropy.

items.title: Jason Buck
items.description: Super Bowl champion Jason Buck shares his inspirational story of coming from humble beginnings to life as a professional football player.

items.title: LIFT -- Connecting Humanity
items.description: Celebrating individuals who have made a difference through philanthropy; host Gary Sinise.

items.title: Light of My Soul by BYU Singers
items.description: Listen to BYU Singers perform Light of My Soul, a beautiful choral work by Robert Lucas Pearsall. Expressive harmonies and poetic lyrics create a moving musical experience celebrating love, devotion, and the timeless beauty of the human voice.

items.title: A Helping Hand
items.description: As we celebrate the birth of the Savior, BYUtv & BYUradio invite you and your family to #LightTheWorld through simple acts of kindness. For more information, visit LightTheWorld.org.

items.title: An Unexpected Delivery
items.description: As we celebrate the birth of the Savior, BYUtv & BYUradio invite you and your family to #LightTheWorld through simple acts of kindness. For more information, visit LightTheWorld.org.

items.title: Angel Advice
items.description: Dalton, Garet, and Kiri get holiday advice from a quirky 'Shoulder Angel' (Matt Meese) on how to spread joy and kindness to their neighbors this Christmas.

items.title: Gift Exchange
items.description: The Fixers help a Chicago Pastor by fixing his aging church steps and surprise a community advocate with a life-changing gift.

items.title: Giving Hope
items.description: Host Ben Lomu reflects on the loss of his father as a child and teams up to bring hope and support to single mothers, spreading the true spirit of Christmas.

items.title: Leo's Gift
items.description: Host Derek Campana gives the gift of mobility to Leo, a spirited rescue dog, with a custom front leg prosthetic.
