items.title: Seeking A Mentor
items.description: As we celebrate the birth of the Savior, BYUtv & BYUradio invite you and your family to #LightTheWorld through simple acts of kindness. For more information, visit LightTheWorld.org.

items.title: Simple Acts of Service
items.description: As we celebrate the birth of the Savior, BYUtv & BYUradio invite you and your family to #LightTheWorld through simple acts of kindness. For more information, visit LightTheWorld.org.

items.title: The Perfect Gift
items.description: As we celebrate the birth of the Savior, BYUtv & BYUradio invite you and your family to #LightTheWorld through simple acts of kindness. For more information, visit LightTheWorld.org.

items.title: Tyce's Triumph
items.description: Tyce Campbell lost his leg to cancer at just 2 years old, but he hasn’t let it hold him back. Tyce and his family came to Provo for a special BYUtv Sports Nation Gameday Big Story, unaware of the surprises we had in store for them.

items.title: More Than Football
items.description: Audience members share what makes coming to the live talk show BYU Football with Kalani Sitake a faith-promoting experience.

items.title: Naughty or Nice
items.description: As we celebrate the birth of the Savior, BYUtv & BYUradio invite you and your family to #LightTheWorld through simple acts of kindness. For more information, visit LightTheWorld.org.

items.title: Rob Gives Back
items.description: At 19, Rob left the Marines and met Felix, who offered guidance that changed his life. That mentorship led Rob to join The Fixers, building hope worldwide. Now Rob gives back, showing how gratitude and service can create a ripple of kindness.

items.title: She Finally Met Her Father at Christmas
items.description: Brittany’s Christmas wish comes when, after 30 years, she finally meets her birth father, Todd.

items.title: Two Worlds
items.description: Joseph Nelson learns to accept and enjoy his uniqueness. He gains perspective and shows generosity when he talks about a boy his older brother taught while serving a Church mission who has gone through many struggles in his life.

items.title: Stealing Home
items.description: Kellen talks about his father’s alcoholism and his parents’ divorce and how sports and his friends have helped him navigate these difficult situations and his depression.

items.title: One America
items.description: As a young Muslim growing up in the United States, Prottush experiences a lot of prejudice and it has affected his self-confidence and how he sees the world and his future. He shares his passion for music and the escape and peace it provides.

items.title: Brother Sister
items.description: Brother and sister Zoriah and Veda express gratitude for their dad after their mother left them. They then process the sudden death of their mother and realize how it has affected their daily lives.

items.title: Dreaming of America
items.description: After immigrating to the United States at age 11, Christian dreams of playing in the NBA while accepting that his dad will never leave Mexico to join him and his mom.

items.title: The Phoenix
items.description: After his parents divorced, Simon started a downward spiral and became addicted to drugs. He now travels the world and works to make lives and communities better.

items.title: Brotherhood
items.description: Simon, Zeke, and Eli are three brothers who want to rebuild their relationship after the addiction struggles of Zeke and Simon. They talk about the loss of the unity of their family and their desire to be a close family again.

items.title: Princess
items.description: Haley talks about losing her best friend really young and the anxiety she feels about getting into college. She also reflects on her personal health issues that will affect her for the rest of her life.

items.title: Touche
items.description: With dreams of being an Olympic fencer, Toby struggles to keep up with his schoolwork and sports demand. He opens up about the pressure he feels from his parents and friends.

items.title: Tabloid Scandal
items.description: Gennette opens up about the struggles she’s had with academics, drinking, depression, and a tabloid scandal. Despite her struggles, she can see the blessings in disguise that she has been given in her life.

items.title: Dreamcatcher
items.description: After years of struggling with addiction and a strained relationship with his father, Emilio talks about his recovery. The relationships with his mom and dad have improved as he has matured and healed.

items.title: Girl in the Mirror
items.description: After years of comparing herself to others and striving for physical perfection, Jade is diagnosed with Body Dysmorphic Disorder. The group discusses how they can help her feel valued and secure for who she is.

items.title: The Principal's Office
items.description: Rory is sent to the Principal's office.

items.title: The Dress Up Day
items.description: Battie dresses up as his own made-up superhero, Stretcho.

items.title: The Ya Ya
items.description: While Atticus' parents are away, his Ya-Ya (grandmother) looks after him.

items.title: The Monkey Bars
items.description: Tamara wants the monkey bars to herself, so she forbids Melanie from getting a turn. This triggers a dispute between them.

items.title: The Top of The Fireman's Pole
items.description: The kids must rescue Mrs. Gonsha from the playground.

items.title: The Lost and Found Box
items.description: The children discover their lost belongings.

items.title: The Milk Bar
items.description: Rory forgets his lunch and goes to the milk bar.

items.title: The Girls' Toilets
items.description: Melanie's friends stop speaking.

items.title: The Kiss Chasey Oval
items.description: Tamara tries to convince Battie to play a chase-and-kiss game that doesn't go as planned, so she tries a different approach.

items.title: The Thing in the Sand
items.description: Melanie thinks she discovered a possum's head in the sand.

items.title: The Band
items.description: Bored during a rainy little lunch, Atticus starts a band and makes Battie reluctantly join too.

items.title: The Beep Test
items.description: Tamara is excited about doing the beep test fitness assessment, but after she sprains her ankle she can't join in.

items.title: The Joke Competition
items.description: Atticus holds a joke telling competition.

items.title: The Old Climbing Tree
items.description: Debra Jo wants the old climbing tree chopped down.

items.title: The Oval
items.description: Rory wants other kids to play with him so devises an elaborate and confusing ball game on the oval.

items.title: The Pavlova
items.description: For the birthday party of Max and Elsa, Mrs. Gonsha makes a pavlova, which looks delicious.

items.title: The Germblock
items.description: Tamara accuses Melanie of not washing her hands, so Atticus and Debra-Jo investigate what happened.

items.title: The Grandparent's Day
items.description: Mrs. Gonsha asks Battie's grandfather to be the guest of honor at the Grandparent's Day celebration.

items.title: The Cake Stall
items.description: When Melanie decides to have a cake stall to raise money for homeless puppies, Atticus gets jealous and sets up a rival fundraiser.

items.title: The Walk-Athon
items.description: The children face the difficult task of finding the right partner to be their walking buddy for the walk-a-thon.

items.title: The Windy Day
items.description: Mrs. Gonsha insists the class comes inside and does yoga, much to Debra-Jo's horror.

items.title: The Body Bus
items.description: After the kids think they see a health van in the playground, Debra-Jo becomes anxious that she has head lice.

items.title: The Election
items.description: When Rory announces that he wants to be the Prime-Minister, Mrs Gonsha suggests they have their own election and that everyone run a campaign.

items.title: The Corridor Outside 6 E
items.description: When the weird twins suddenly leave class, rumors begin.

items.title: The Gap Behind the Dumpster
items.description: Atticus tries to start a secret club with Rory.

items.title: The Relationship
items.description: Rory is confused when a grade six girl likes him.

items.title: The Halloween Horror Story
items.description: Atticus is excited to be starring in the Halloween play at school, but he finds out that the day of the play will be his last day of school because his mother got a new job in Singapore.

items.title: The Nightmare Before Graduation
items.description: Mrs. Gonsha's class is is excited about going to high school, but they learn that Rory is unable to graduate with them.

items.title: Living Legends Keeps Traditions Alive
items.description: Through music and dance, Living Legends celebrates cultural heritage while inspiring young people to embrace their identity, pursue their education, and see a world of possibilities beyond what they imagined for themselves.

items.title: People of Faith: Pioneers of Brazil
items.description: From humble beginnings with only a few members, the Church in Brazil has grown into a thriving community of faith. This episode highlights the resilience, devotion, and gratitude of its members as they face life’s challenges.

items.title: People of Faith: Pioneers of Hawaii
items.description: Celeste Ha'o, Mufi Hannemann, and Ryan Tanaka share pivotal moments and personal stories from their lives as members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Hawai'i, revealing how faith shapes their journeys and daily experiences.

items.title: People of Faith: Pioneers of the Philippines
items.description: Lani Misalucha, Lilian Villamor, and Alex Castillo share key moments in their faith journeys and everyday life as members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in the Philippines, showing how faith shapes and inspires them daily.

items.title: Harvest of Faith: Welfare Farms
items.description: From Idaho to Texas, welfare farms grow more than crops. They cultivate healing, miracles, and hope. Deep bonds bring strength through loss, orchards defy nature, and volunteers uplift communities. Every harvest helps feed the world -- and hearts.

items.title: Harvest of Faith: Processing & Distribution
items.description: Staffed almost entirely by volunteers, welfare facilities transform donated crops into life-saving goods. From miracles in mills to factories, witness how service, sacrifice, and faith fuel a global mission to care for God’s children.

items.title: Harvest of Faith: AgReserves
items.description: Across Brazil, Washington, and Chile, for-profit farms power a greater purpose, funding a global humanitarian mission. From life-changing education to tech innovation and national sustainability, witness AgReserves' farms transform lives and futures.

items.title: Voices of Faith: In Defense of Religious Freedom
items.description: Stories from LDS members in Ghana, Rabbi Diana Gerson, Professor Robert P. George, and leading scholars reveal the challenges facing religious freedom and the determined efforts to uphold faith amid global threats.

items.title: Voices for Faith: An Approach of Religious Freedom
items.description: A compassionate exploration of religious freedom through the personal faith stories of Kori Porter, Dean G. Marcus Cole, Asma T. Uddin, Simmer Singh, and other respected scholars and thought leaders.

items.title: Voices for Faith: Joined in Religious Freedom
items.description: A hopeful look at the strength found in unity for religious freedom, shared through the personal faith stories of Marian Edmonds-Allen, Amos C. Brown, the Commission of Religious Leaders in New York City, and Elder Quentin L. Cook.

items.title: Love by Accident
items.description: A young woman finds unexpected romance with a handsome mechanic while taking a road trip with her godmother.

items.title: Lux Aurumque by BYU Men’s Chorus
items.description: Listen to the BYU Men's Chorus perform Lux Aurumque by Eric Whitacre, a beautiful choral work inspired by the birth of Jesus Christ. Gentle harmonies and luminous Latin poetry create a peaceful celebration of Christmas, light, and hope.

items.title: Night 1 (11-7-20)
items.description: This special virtual edition of Luz de las Naciones celebrates culture, faith, family, and hope through music, dance, and inspiring messages, including counsel from President Russell M. Nelson.

items.title: Night 2 (12-19-20)
items.description: This special Christmas edition of Luz de las Naciones celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ through traditional music, dance, scripture, and holiday customs from across the Spanish-speaking world.

items.title: Old Skool Cafe
items.description: Kirby travels to San Francisco to join a restaurant run entirely by at-risk youth. From cooking and serving to entertaining, Kirby learns how to put together the perfect dinner, and how working at the cafe has changed many kids’ lives for the better.

items.title: Operation BBQ Relief
items.description: In the wake of Hurricane Florence, Kirby travels to Wilmington, North Carolina to join a team of BBQ pitmasters delivering hot meals to victims. Kirby helps prepare and deliver meals, and gets a firsthand look at the devastation.

items.title: Home Works of America
items.description: In South Carolina, Kirby helps a charity that rebuilds homes in disrepair. After gathering materials and packing the trailer full of gear, Kirby joins a team of volunteers to clear weeds, fill holes in the floor, and reconstruct a broken roof.

items.title: Muttville
items.description: In San Francisco, Kirby joins a group of dog-lovers that help senior dogs find new homes. Kirby learns that the world of senior pet care is sometimes messy. After falling in love with a pup named Sierra, Kirby works hard to find her a loving owner.

items.title: Reach 4 the Stars
items.description: In Palm Springs, Kirby joins an organization that flies a wheelchair accessible hot air balloon. Kirby learns how much hard work goes into inflating, flying, and packing up the balloon, and how lives can be changed with a ride in the sky.

items.title: Free Bikes 4 Kidz
items.description: In Madison, WI, Kirby joins a group giving free bikes to disadvantaged kids. While loading up a delivery of donated bikes, Kirby finds a special bike to give away. After a whole day of repair, Kirby’s ready to find the perfect match for his bike.

items.title: Veterans Oceans Adventures
items.description: Kirby travels to Miami to join a group giving veterans access to the ocean. Kirby gets his feet wet learning to be a buddy diver for disabled divers, joins the crew for an ocean dive, and learns how diving can be a healing experience for veterans.

items.title: Loving Thunder
items.description: Kirby travels to Albuquerque, New Mexico, and joins a therapeutic riding ranch. While Kirby has always loved horses, he learns quickly that it takes a lot of work to keep a riding ranch going. Kirby then gets a chance to work with some riders.

items.title: Raising Men Lawn Care Service
items.description: In Sanford, Florida, Kirby joins a nationwide group of kids mowing lawns for the elderly, people with disabilities, veterans, and single mothers. Kirby decides to take on the “50 Yard Challenge”, though he only has 3 days to do it.

items.title: Christmas Special
items.description: Kirby goes to the Utah State Prison to conduct an inmate orchestra as part of an inmate music school. With the help of a hardworking program leader and a personal hero, Kirby helps the band prepare a Christmas medley for the holiday recital.

items.title: The Bloc
items.description: In Chicago, Kirby joins The Bloc, a boxing club and mentor service. Kirby, training to be a coach, learns that through the discipline of boxing, the Bloc helps kids get their schoolwork as strong as their punches.

items.title: Island Dolphin Care
items.description: Kirby travels to Key Largo, Florida to join Island Dolphin Care, a dolphin therapy organization. After a long day preparing their food and their medicine, Kirby finally gets to meet the dolphins. On the last day, Kirby sees dolphin therapy in action.

items.title: Trenton Circus Squad
items.description: In Trenton, New Jersey, Kirby’s ready for a day at the circus. But he’s not just there to watch. Kirby works with the kids at the Trenton Circus Squad to prepare his circus skills in time for the final performance.

items.title: CoachArt
items.description: In Los Angeles, Kirby joins CoachArt, a group matching up kids in medical families with mentors. After trying out a few different mentoring options, Kirby finds just the right kids to mentor. Together, they create a creative surprise for their mom.

items.title: Wild West Wildlife
items.description: Kirby goes to Amarillo, Texas to join the Wild West Wildlife Rehabilitation Center. Kirby helps clean the badger pens, feed the owls, and give medicine to a vulture. After a hairy encounter with a possum, Kirby releases it back to the wild.

items.title: No Limits for Deaf Kids
items.description: In Hollywood, Kirby joins No Limits for Deaf Kids, a unique organization helping children with hearing loss and their families. Kirby sees a chance to write a play for the kids to perform at their graduation ceremony.

items.title: Cars that Care
items.description: In Salt Lake City, Kirby joins Cars that Care, a non-profit that collects donated cars, repairs them, and gives them away to mothers who need transport. Kirby learns how to repair a car, and makes his fair share of mistakes along the way.

items.title: GlamourGals
items.description: In New York, Kirby joins GlamourGals, a group organizing makeovers by young women for senior women. Kirby tries to throw the most glamourous party he can, organizing decorations and music, as well as learning the intricacies of nail polish.

items.title: Icing Smiles
items.description: Kirby travels to San Diego to join Icing Smiles, a group making special cakes for medical kids and their families. The plan is for a pretty big cake, so Kirby and the team have to work pretty quick to get it done in time.

items.title: Soul
items.description: In New Orleans, Kirby joins SOUL, a group replanting trees the city lost in Hurricane Katrina. Kirby learns firsthand what the devastation of Katrina did to New Orlean’s tree population, and how it is still felt years later.

items.title: Farm Rescue
items.description: In Minot, North Dakota, Kirby helps out a farmer recovering from an illness. He joins Farm Rescue, a group of farmers and agriculture professionals who plant and harvest crops at no cost for farmers who are ill, injured, or unable to work.

items.title: Trash Fishing
items.description: Kirby goes to Detroit to join Trash Fishing, a group of dedicated boat owners who compete against each other to take the most trash out of the city’s waterways. Kirby pits himself against the other teams to win the coveted “Most Trash” award.

items.title: Blind Grilling
items.description: Kirby travels to Springfield, Missouri, to join Blind Grilling, an organization that educates and provides accessible grilling kits for people with visual impairments. With a blindfold on, Kirby learns firsthand how hard it is to cook without sight.

items.title: Special Kneads
items.description: In Lawrenceville, Georgia, Kirby helps a bakery called Special Kneads and Treats with their grand re-opening. Kirby tries his best to keep up in a professional bakery kitchen and works alongside the team to bake enough cupcakes for the re-opening.

items.title: Art 4 New York
items.description: Kirby joins Art 4 New York, a group making personalized gift baskets for isolated seniors in elderly care and frontline workers. Kirby spends time with artists, photographers, and musicians, all working to make meaningful memories with their gifts.

items.title: Dream Adaptive
items.description: Kirby travels to Whitefish, Montana to partner with DREAM Adaptive Recreation, an organization which seeks to enhance the quality of life of individuals with disabilities by providing year round outdoor adaptive recreational opportunities.

items.title: Blessing Bike
items.description: Kirby joins The Blessing Bike in Boise, Idaho to provide access to passenger bikes to families with loved ones experiencing age, health or disability related barriers.

items.title: Gardopia Gardens
items.description: At Gardopia Gardens, Kirby digs deep into the world of urban gardening, bringing the cultivation of fresh vegetables to low income neighborhoods. Kirby learns about planting, fertilizing, and even faces one of his greatest fears––bees!

items.title: Jumping Dreams Double Dutch
items.description: Kirby travels to North Carolina to join Jumping Dreams, a nonprofit that uses competitive Double Dutch jump roping to teach kids about fitness, nutrition, and friendship.

items.title: Canes for Veterans Central Texas
items.description: Kirby heads to Copperas Cove, Texas where he tries his hand at carving Christmas trees into canes for wounded veterans. Despite his fear of power tools, Kirby puts his wood working skills to the test, hustling to finish a cane for a veteran in need.

items.title: Hoop.Camp
items.description: Kirby goes to Portland, Oregon to join Hoop.Camp, a volunteer-run basketball camp for athletes with developmental disabilities.

items.title: Urban Boatbuilders
items.description: In Minneapolis, Minnesota, Kirby works with Urban Boatbuilders to make a canoe in time for their graduation. Kirby learns about how the program teaches skills in the woodshop and in life.

items.title: The Other Side Academy
items.description: In Salt Lake City, Utah, Kirby works with The Other Side Academy, an organization that helps people turn their lives around. He joins the Academy’s moving company, and sees first-hand how a little elbow grease can go a long way.

items.title: Sleep in Heavenly Peace
items.description: In Lakeville, Minnesota, Kirby volunteers with Sleep in Heavenly Peace, which builds, assembles, and delivers bunk beds to families in need.

items.title: Little Wanderers
items.description: In New York City, Kirby joins Little Wanderers, an organization that helps sick and injured feral cats. Deep in the Big Apple, Kirby and the team work to find cats in need, get them medical attention, and help them on their way to a better life.

items.title: Gaining Ground Book Bus
items.description: Kirby heads to Tulsa, Oklahoma, to team up with the Gaining Ground Book Bus, a school bus converted into a free book delivery service. Kirby and a team of educators tour the city and deliver 3,000 books.

items.title: Memphis Rox
items.description: Kirby heads to Memphis Rox, a climbing and community center in Memphis. As he learns rock climbing, Kirby witnesses how the center is building up the Soulsville community, both on and off the climbing wall.

items.title: The Welcome to America Project
items.description: Kirby joins The Welcome to America Project, an organization dedicated to helping refugees thrive. As Kirby tracks down and delivers basic household items needed by the newly arrived families, he experiences what it really means to be a good neighbor.

items.title: Warfighter Made
items.description: Kirby travels to Temecula, California, to work with Warfighter Made, a nonprofit dedicated to putting wounded veterans behind the wheels of off-road vehicles to provide "adrenaline therapy".

items.title: The Roots of Music
items.description: Kirby joins The Roots of Music, a nonprofit empowering youth through music education, academic support, and mentorship. Kirby earns a spot in the Marching Crusaders, the organization's youth marching band, and prepares for his first big parade.

items.title: San Diego Chill
items.description: Kirby travels to San Diego to work with San Diego Chill, an organization that helps kids with disabilities learn how to play ice hockey. Kirby trains to be a goalie.

items.title: Mascot Miracles
items.description: Kirby travels to West Jordan, Utah, to work with Mascot Miracles Foundation, an organization that hosts events with mascots for kids with debilitating conditions.

items.title: Morgan's Wonderland
items.description: Kirby goes to San Antonio, Texas, to volunteer at Morgan’s Wonderland, the one and only “Ultra-Accessible Theme Park” for guests of all ages and abilities.

items.title: Saddles in Service
items.description: Kirby goes to Wyoming to help Saddles in Service to assist Veterans, Firefighters, Law Enforcement Officers, and First Responders the unique opportunity to explore their own healing alongside a rescue horse.

items.title: Life Rolls On
items.description: Kirby goes to San Diego to work with Life Rolls On, an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people living with various disabilities through adaptive surfing and skating.

items.title: Wrap Ukraine with Quilts
items.description: Kirby goes to Poland to work with Wrap Ukraine With Quilts, an organization that is dedicated to making and donating quilts to refugees from Ukraine.

items.title: Music Mends Minds
items.description: Kirby goes to Los Angeles to discover Music Mends Minds, an organization that creates musical support groups for people with Alzheimer’s, dementia, Parkinson’s, traumatic brain injury, PTSD, and other neurological disorders.

items.title: Helpful Hands and Hearts
items.description: Kirby travels to Littleton, North Carolina, to work with Helpful Hands and Hearts, a organization in the Lake Gaston and Roanake River Valley that helps everyday people deal with their challenging access and transportation circumstances.

items.title: SevaTruck Foundation
items.description: Kirby travels to Fairfax, Virginia, to work with SevaTruck Foundation, an organization committed to fighting hunger in communities by serving hot, nutritious meals to anyone in need.

items.title: Windy's Ranch and Rescue
items.description: In Overton, Nevada, Kirby goes hog wild in his efforts to help Windy's Ranch & Rescue save abandoned and mistreated pot-bellied pigs. Kirby learns how sweet pigs can be, and how rich they can make the lives of the people who care for them.

items.title: Carol
items.description: Host Kirby Heyborne uses JustServe.org to bring some holiday cheer to an old friend.

items.title: Pepperell Community Arts
items.description: Kirby heads to Pepperell, Massachusetts to join Pepperell Community Arts––an organization dedicated to an inclusive approach to youth theater, music, and dance. Channeling his inner thespian, Kirby takes on the daunting task of stage-managing a play.

items.title: River Discovery
items.description: Kirby heads to Idaho to join River Discovery, an organization that provides whitewater rafting adventures for cancer survivors. Kirby gets thrown into the deep end, trying to keep up with the demands and dangers associated with the extreme sport.

items.title: Hope Renovations
items.description: In North Carolina, Kirby joins an organization called Hope Renovations which empowers women to pursue careers in the construction trades. Donning his tool belt, Kirby sees firsthand how impactful it can be to give someone a new skill set.

items.title: Laughing Bear Bakery
items.description: Kirby travels to Laughing Bear Bakery, a bakery empowering ex-offenders with job opportunities. Rolling up his sleeves, Kirby bakes pies alongside those getting a second chance.

items.title: Need to Believe
items.description: Kirby finds the Need to Believe Foundation–an organization in California that trains kids with special needs in jiu-jitsu and other martial arts. With guidance from an ex-MMA fighter, Kirby helps the students prepare for their upcoming tournament.

items.title: Peace of Mind Dog Rescue
items.description: Kirby travels to California to help Peace of Mind Dog Rescue, an organization that assists senior citizens with caring for their dogs. As Kirby serves people in need, he learns just how big of an impact the dogs have on their owners' wellness.

items.title: Southside Blooms
items.description: Kirby volunteers at Southside Blooms, a farm-to-vase floral shop dedicated to creating jobs for at-risk youth in some of Chicago's toughest neighborhoods. Kirby sees firsthand how growing flowers can be surprisingly effective at growing communities.

items.title: Honor Flight
items.description: Kirby joins Honor Flight in Washington D.C., an organization dedicated to honoring veterans by taking them on trips to see the national monuments. Planning a surprise welcome home for the veterans will be one of Kirby's biggest challenges yet!

items.title: C.A.S.T. for Kids
items.description: Kirby joins C.A.S.T. for Kids in Texas, helping kids with special needs go fishing. As Kirby helps orchestrate the big fishing derby, he witnesses the joy that comes from celebrating accomplishments–a rare treat for some of the participants.

items.title: Free Guitars 4 Kids
items.description: Kirby travels to Austin, Texas to help Free Guitars 4 Kids–an organization striving to put guitars in the hands of kids, regardless of their financial situations. Kirby sees the joy that instruments can bring to young musicians.

items.title: RODS Heroes
items.description: In Armenia, Kirby celebrates the spirit of children with Down syndrome. Alongside RODS Heroes, he visits an orphanage filled with love, experiences traditional food and dance, and embraces a nation’s warmth in this unforgettable Making Good.

items.title: Nurturing Nations - Ghana
items.description: Kirby visits Ghana, where local hero Percy and Nurturing Nations rescue hundreds of children from slavery and hunger, offering safety, meals, and education. Welcomed as family, Kirby makes banku, learns dances, and invites a king to their ceremony.

items.title: Trailer: Season 6
items.description: Watch the trailer for season 6 of Malory Towers!

items.title: The First Day
items.description: In awe of Malory Towers, Darrell keeps her past at her old school a close secret. Always in the thick of it, Darrell has a hairy start at the train station and when odd sounds are heard in the dorm, learns about the ghost of Lady Jane Malory.

items.title: The New Girls
items.description: When Gwen leaves the school to learn about Darrell’s past, Darrell must try to stop her before it's too late. Meanwhile, not knowing where their dormmates are, the North Tower girls do all they can to cover when Matron comes for lights out.

items.title: The Trick
items.description: In an attempt to impress Alicia, Darrell unleashes a prank in Mam'zelle's class. Trick sweets sent by Alicia's brothers cause havoc in the school, and strange happenings continue when a mysterious red handprint appears in the dorm.

items.title: The Slap
items.description: On a scorching hot day at Malory Towers, Miss Potts lets the first form girls go down to the pool. Jealous of Darrell and Alicia's new friendship, Gwen takes the fun and games too far.

items.title: The Match
items.description: Darrell is up to play in the lacrosse game, but her excitement is short lived when she finds out they'll be playing against her old school. Darrell must face her past and overcome her temper if she wants to win the match.

items.title: The Midnight Feast
items.description: Alicia's family sends a bounty of food, and the girls are all set to have their first North Tower midnight feast. But when Matron wakes during the feast, all Darrell’s worst fears are realized. Will the girls escape?

items.title: The Open Day
items.description: On open day, Malory Towers bursts with energy and visiting families. But Darrell's joy is short lived when she finds out her half-term results. She is determined to keep them a secret from her parents.

items.title: The Push
items.description: After a confrontation with Darrell about her family, Sally is found hiding in pain. However, her injuries are far more serious than first thought. Fearing she is at fault, Darrell leaves the school to find a doctor.

items.title: The Letter
items.description: Darrell is itching to get to the bottom of Sally's relationship with her family, but when Sally goes missing, the first form rally together to comb the grounds. Darrell and Sally finally discover the real reason Sally was sent to Malory Towers.

items.title: The Dress
items.description: A beautiful dress arrives at Malory Towers: one of the girls is a debutante, destined to marry into aristocracy. When Darrell finds out who the mystery girl is, she's determined to prove the girl is a poor choice.

items.title: The Spider
items.description: Feeling guilty for lashing out at Mary-Lou, Darrell and Sally hatch a plan to give Mary-Lou the confidence she needs. But will the plan backfire and make Mary-Lou less courageous?

items.title: The Ghost
items.description: In the dead of night Mary-Lou faints when she sees a hooded figure in the dorm bathroom. Not wanting Mary-Lou's courage to be crushed, Darrell and Sally are determined to get to the bottom of the mystery.

items.title: The Last Day
items.description: May-Lou is devastated to find her courage pen smashed on the floor. When Darrell's shoes are found with ink on them, Darrell is the prime suspect, and the North Tower holds a class court.

items.title: The Head of Form
items.description: Darrell and her class return to Malory Towers. The first order of business: elect a new class leader. Gwen decides to take the new girl under her wing and become her best friend.

items.title: The Dunce's Cap
items.description: Alicia convinces Darrell to help her play a prank on their teachers with invisible chalk. Meanwhile, Mr. Parker becomes more strict. Mary-Lou finds her voice and stands up for herself.

items.title: The Stray
items.description: The girls' attempt to make Ellen feel more included but their efforts backfire. Miss Grayling has a secret that might put Malory Towers in danger.

items.title: The Auditions
items.description: In an attempt to impress her parents, Gwen auditions for the lead role in the upcoming school play. Darrell and Sally devise a plan to save the school.

items.title: The Caricatures
items.description: When Alicia’s birthday gift from her parents doesn’t arrive, she take it out on her teachers. Gwen becomes more tangled in her lies.

items.title: The Runaway
items.description: Ellen is stressed that she’ll lose her scholarship and stays up all night studying for an exam. Gwen gets her hands on Darrell’s diary and discovers Darrell's secret.

items.title: The Play
items.description: Darrell shows a potential investor around Malory Towers. Gwen is confronted with her lies when her mother visits.

items.title: The Measles
items.description: A teacher and Gwen are quarantined after finding out they have the measles. Darrell finds out disturbing news about the future of Malory Towers. Sally takes on extra responsibilities.

items.title: The Sneezing Trick
items.description: Alicia and Darrell pull a sneezing prank on their French teacher, which disappoints Sally. Someone has stolen important possessions from the girls.

items.title: The School Trip
items.description: Gwen resorts to drastic measures to hide what she’s stolen. Darrell and Sally find a clue that could finally lead them to Lady Jane Malory’s treasure.

items.title: The Quiz
items.description: Malory Towers competes with the local boys' school in a competition. Ellen suffers a panic attack when she is accused of Gwen's misdeeds.

items.title: The Heroine
items.description: The girls doubt Ellen’s innocence. Gwen attempts to get rid of the items she stole, endangering Mary-Lou in the process.

items.title: The Lost Treasure
items.description: Miss Grayling reveals disheartening news. In one last attempt to save the school, Darrell and Sally try to find Lady Jane’s lost treasure. Gwen’s secrets come to light.

items.title: The New Arrivals
items.description: The girls welcome Bill and her horse, Thunder, to Malory Towers, but Bill’s place in the third form is under threat when she is accused of spending too much time in the stables. Gwen’s father is offered the position as head of board at the school.

items.title: The Trials
items.description: Darrell scouts out players for the lacrosse team, and discovers that Gwen has some hidden talents. Mary-Lou discovers a skin condition that worries her. Matron must fill in for the biology teacher.

items.title: The Surprise Picnic
items.description: Darrell suggests a midnight feast in the stables, but they’re afraid of horse poachers. Mavis, a sixth former, is on the hunt for someone to accompany her on the piano for an important audition, and Irene might fit the bill.

items.title: The Accident
items.description: Bill struggles to balance her schoolwork with time spent at the stables with her horse, Thunder. Bill and Darrell need Thunder's help when someone at the school has a serious accident.

items.title: The New Headmistress
items.description: Miss Johnson enforces a list of tough new rules which get the better Darrell’s temper. An important lacrosse match is at stake when Darrell is given a particularly difficult punishment.

items.title: The Voice
items.description: Sally returns to a very different Malory Towers after her case of the mumps. The strict new rules keep Mavis and Irene from their audition, but the girls have a plan to cover for them and keep Miss Johnson at bay.

items.title: The Dance
items.description: Gwen goes a little overboard when she organizes a dance lesson with the Thackerton boys. Mary-Lou discovers a mysterious statue in the woods when Gwen asks her to break the rules to gather ivy.

items.title: The Sisters
items.description: Darrell’s sister Felicity visits to take an exam that will determine her acceptance at Malory Towers. Darrell wants to enjoy time with her sister but Miss Johnson's strict rules stand in the way.

items.title: The Hamper
items.description: Alicia sends a package for the girls filled with goodies and prank materials, plus a secret message. Darrell prepares for the lacrosse trial and sneaks in practice time.

items.title: The Peaches
items.description: With the third form on a trip to the circus, Darrell and Sally attempt to recover the confiscated peaches from Miss Johnson’s office, but they find more than they expected...

items.title: The Ride
items.description: Bill will stop at nothing when she discovers that her horse Thunder is sick with colic. Gwen is charged with keeping Bill away from the stables or else they will both be punished.

items.title: The Arrest
items.description: Ron shows Darrell and Sally a stash of art found in the stables, but where did it come from? Miss Johnson is caught off-guard when Miss Grayling arrives back at Malory Towers.

items.title: The Thief
items.description: With Darrell focused on clearing Ron’s name, Mary-Lou and Ellen uncover new information that changes everything they thought about the art thefts.

items.title: Christmas at Malory Towers
items.description: While stranded at Malory Towers for the Christmas holiday, Gwen receives some devastating news while Darrell, Mary Lou, Sally and Ellen solve a ghostly mystery.

items.title: The Rivers Sisters
items.description: After being selected as head of lower school, Darrell soon feels the demands of leadership when Felicity, her younger sister just starting at Malory Towers, gets into trouble.

items.title: The Doubloon
items.description: Darrell enlists the help of the first year students when facing her first challenge to her authority as head of lower school.

items.title: The Inter-Tower Match
items.description: Preparing for the inter-tower lacrosse match leads to disappointment for Darrell and Felicity. The rest of the team speculates why breakout star Clarissa is hesitant to play.

items.title: The Essay
items.description: Ruth lets her sister Connie take credit for her essay. The first forms try to evade Darrell while searching for treasure.

items.title: The Kiss
items.description: The first formers try to prank their teachers with Irene's help. Mademoiselle's reaction to the prank raises suspicions for Irene.

items.title: The Midnight Surprise
items.description: Alicia plans an outdoor midnight feast for her and Darrell. Felicity and June sneak out to search for a hidden room within Malory Towers.

items.title: The Speech
items.description: Darrell struggles to prepare a speech she is to give in front of the whole school. Sally and Bill organize a lacrosse match. Irene’s father delivers news Irene has not been looking forward to.

items.title: The Connie Affair
items.description: June makes some itching powder for a prank that gets out of hand. Connie blames June for the unfortunate things that keep happening to her, even though June insists she had nothing to do with them.

items.title: The Strong Heart
items.description: When Clarissa receives troubling news that her pony has been sold, she breaks the rules to rescue him. Irene and Mademoiselle Rougier make efforts to strengthen their relationship.

items.title: The Field Trip
items.description: Instead of going on a field trip, Gwen chooses to stay at school to care for Mr. Parker’s pregnant wife. June gives Darrell a scare by wandering off.

items.title: The Exam
items.description: Darrell and her classmates await their exam while Felicity and June continue to explore the secret room. Gwen pretends to have heart issues to get out of the exam, but then finds herself in a dangerous situation.

items.title: The Terrible Day
items.description: Ruth’s bullying of Connie reaches a new low when June is wrongly accused of playing pranks. Darrell encourages the lower form to find who is responsible and the whole class gets a lesson on accountability.

items.title: The Wedding Day
items.description: June and Darrell find themselves in danger when they leave the school to continue the search for the treasure in a cave during high tide. The rest of the school prepares for the wedding. Irene is given an important task by her father.

items.title: The Rivers Sisters Return
items.description: Felicity struggles to get out of Darrell's shadow in her second year at Malory Towers. Newcomer Jo struggles to follow the rules, getting Felicity caught in the crosshairs. Mary Lou debates how strict to be after becoming head of lower school.

items.title: The Monitor Strike
items.description: June leads the second form girls in a strike to protect Clarissa from Gwen's constant demands, resulting in a big change. When a pipe bursts, old memories resurface and a new friend is made. Archeological research is to begin at Malory Towers.

items.title: The Circus
items.description: Felicity and Jo meet a young acrobat girl and Jo promises to take Felicity to the circus. When Jo breaks the rules to fulfill her promise, Miss Grayling teaches her a lesson about friendship. Twins Ruth and Connie start to notice their differences.

items.title: The Beautiful Game
items.description: Clarissa goes undercover to prove that girls can play soccer just as good as boys. Darrell and Susan help Mr. Murray look for ancient symbols in the garden as they continue their archeology research.

items.title: The Pocket Money
items.description: Jo and Connie trick Felicity into helping them retrieve Jo's confiscated pocket money from Matron's safe. The Second Form girls protest Jo's rule-breaking.

items.title: The Fugitives
items.description: Afraid of being accused of stealing, Jo and Connie run away to the village. Darrell helps a worried Ruth search for her sister. When the girls return to Malory Towers, Jo's father learns about her misdeeds.

items.title: The Babysitter
items.description: Gwen has plans with Ron--until she gets stuck watching Mr. Parker's baby. Alicia recruits Felicity to the cross-country team, much to Darrell's dismay. When baby Kathleen goes missing, Gwen attempts to pass off the blame.

items.title: The Malory Oak
items.description: June pulls a daring stunt to save the beloved Malory Oak from being chopped down by Mr. Murray. The Second Form girls learn about chores and hard work. Jo trusts Felicity and Connie with a secret about her mother.

items.title: The Unexpected Visitor
items.description: Mrs. Heather appears suddenly to take Susan home. The Second Form girls start a prank war with Mam'zelle. Ruth and Clarissa find a way for Susan to stay at Malory Towers.

items.title: The Race
items.description: On the day of the big race, Felicity cracks under the pressure of Alicia's tough coaching. Matron goes on vacation to see her family. The new nurse, Nurse Jane, has her hands full right away when Darrell gets injured looking for Felicity.

items.title: The New Matron
items.description: As Nurse Jane adjusts to her new job at Malory Towers, Darrell adjusts to her new injury and missing lacrosse trials. During a nit breakout, Jo and the second formers prank Nurse Jane to get out of treatment.

items.title: The Maypole
items.description: Jo's mischief leads the second formers to take out the Maypole for the first time since the war. When Jo is named May Queen, she struggles to accept the traditions. Darrell's suspicion of Nurse Jane grows as more information is uncovered.

items.title: The Investigation
items.description: Darrell's suspicions are confirmed when she discovers that Nurse Jane isn't who she claims to be. Matron returns to Malory Towers early, prompting an unexpected reunion. June and Clarissa attempt to save the life of a lost donkey.

items.title: The Penalty
items.description: Ruth takes an exam that could mean skipping a form--meaning she would leave Connie and her friends behind. Jane and Clarissa rally the second formers to compete in a football tournament for prize money that could save George the donkey.

items.title: The Dream
items.description: Gwen is directing the school play and considers giving Jo a bigger role to take advantage of her father's donations. Felicity juggles rehearsing the play and helping Darrell rehabilitate her ankle. Susan and Ruth help Mr. Murray with his excavation.

items.title: The Birthday Surprise
items.description: Ruth and Connie celebrate a birthday together and Jo learns the joy of sharing and teamwork. A mysterious package containing a camera causes all sorts of mischief and hijinks. Mr. Murray seems to be hiding secrets about the excavation.

items.title: The Challenge
items.description: Darrell is nervous about racing against Alicia on her ankle until Jean encourages her. Susan and Ruth question Mr. Murray about the secrets he's been keeping. The obstacle course ends with teamwork, reconciliation, and a new Games Captain.

items.title: The Poison Pen
items.description: With the play coming up quickly, Gwen dials up the intensity during play rehearsals, causing Jo, Felicity, and the others to rebel. June and Connie help Jean with the backdrops.

items.title: The Last Letter
items.description: Gwen finds the girl behind the poison pen letters and learns a lesson about forgiveness and second chances. Susan and Ruth get some guidance from Mr. Parker that helps them find the ancient chamber.

items.title: The Chamber
items.description: As the girls make their final preparations for the play, Jo and Gwen connect over their family situations. Felicity feels the impact of stage fright. Ruth and Susan finally discover the ancient chamber as well as Mr. Murray's true colors.

items.title: The First Day of the Last Year
items.description: After a bustling first day back at school, best friends Darrell and Sally contend for Head Girl, while new girl Celeste arrives from France and quickly gets into trouble with Matron.

items.title: The Malory Times
items.description: Friendships are tested when Alicia, Jean, and Mary-Lou set out to make their mark on Malory Towers by restarting the school newsletter, the Malory Times. Jo and Susan try to fix Mr. Parker's new typewriter before he finds out they broke it.

items.title: Le Petit Paris
items.description: When Celeste discovers she must stay at school for the full term, Jo, Susan, and June plan a France-themed party to cheer her up. Mary-Lou shadows her teachers as she explores a potential career path.

items.title: The Band
items.description: Alicia prepares for her Oxford exam while Irene plays piano for Ron's band. June and Felicity receive a riddle that might lead them to the time capsule hidden at the school.

items.title: The Birthday
items.description: It's Celeste's birthday, and when she doesn't receive anything from her Maman, the Malory Tower girls spring into action, causing tension between Celeste and Jo. Sally suspects Matron may not be telling the truth when Matron ends up in danger.

items.title: The Nurse
items.description: Celeste lies about the fire as a way to see her mother. Matron confides in Sally, pushing Sally to make a decision about her future.

items.title: The Debate
items.description: Gwen fills in for Matron, resulting in disaster. June and Felicity start a pillow fight with Darrell and Alicia over some contested school rules. Darrell and Felicity have a sisterly talk.

items.title: The Ward
items.description: Matron Maher returns to Malory Towers, bringing her ward, Nancy, with her. Gwen attempts several strategies to persuade Matron to stay. Nancy helps the Third Form figure out more clues to the time capsule, unearthing another layer of mystery.

items.title: The Best Friend
items.description: Jo is reluctant to say goodbye to her best friend. Nancy, June, and Felicity search for clues about the time capsule, which leads them to Fred. Celeste is sent off with the promise of a pen pal.

items.title: The Photograph
items.description: Alicia and Irene discover who got accepted to Oxford. The Malory Towers time capsule is found with an important and timely message inside. Irene finds support in her band mate.

items.title: The Spelling Bee
items.description: Gwen’s plans to go to finishing school are thrown into chaos when an unexpected obstacle gets in her way. A spelling bee causes Darrell to doubt her future plans and strains her relationship with Felicity.

items.title: The Champions
items.description: When Clarissa's brother insults her, she challenges his team of boys to a lacrosse match. And Mr. Parker worries about Nancy when she is put in goal.

items.title: The Movie Star
items.description: Gwen plots for movie star, and Miss Grayling’s cousin, Lily Vernon to visit the school, unaware of their family feud. Meanwhile, Susan and Nancy devise a plan to get out of eating carrots.

items.title: The Riding Mistress
items.description: Bill’s mother puts Thunder up for sale, and Bill attempts a desperate ploy to foil her. The third formers prank Miss Vernon, but she brings in reinforcements.

items.title: The Scoop
items.description: Jean reveals uncomfortable truths about the Grayling family, shocking Lily and stirring up trouble. Meanwhile, Darrell and Alicia attempt the ultimate prank.

items.title: The Shoot
items.description: The girls make a film in an effort to prove Lily is a good teacher. But Lily has her own agenda, and at the peak of filming, things go terribly awry.

items.title: The Intruder
items.description: When Felicity and June are forced to stay in the san, Felicity sees a mysterious girl in uniform sneaking around the school.

items.title: The Abandoned Cottage
items.description: Smoke from an abandoned cottage leads Lily to an old, and dangerous, friend. Alicia takes on the challenge of helping Darrell relax and plans a midnight feast.

items.title: The Traitor
items.description: Gwen is furious with her father when he tells her she won't be going to finishing school. Meanwhile, a mysterious will throws the future of the school into doubt.

items.title: The Last Day of Malory Towers
items.description: Darrell seeks Jo’s and Felicity’s help to reveal Lily’s plans before Malory Towers is lost forever. Gwen learns Ron is leaving and is forced to confront her own future.

items.title: Man from Snowy River by BYU Chamber Orchestra
items.description: Listen to the BYU Chamber Orchestra perform Man from Snowy River, an adventurous orchestral selection inspired by an Australian story. Sweeping melodies and expressive music capture the beauty of the landscape and the spirit of courage and discovery.

items.title: Mary 4 Mayor
items.description: In a final bid to save Echo Harbor and reunite her fractured family, Mary Parson runs for mayor—against her own father. Can her bold campaign heal old wounds, or will the price of change be more than she’s willing to pay?

items.title: "Before Abraham Was": Premortal Savior
items.description: Latter-day Saint scholars discuss Jesus Christ's role in the war in Heaven before He came to Earth. They consider the contributions of The Logos Hymn and the story of the woman at the well.

items.title: "Knowest Thou The Condescension of God?": Birth and Childhood
items.description: While reconciling both Matthew and Luke’s versions of Christ’s birth, Latter-day Saint scholars discuss the religious and secular context surrounding the childhood of Jesus.

items.title: "If Thou Be The Son of God": Power and Authority
items.description: Jesus' ministry begins after he is baptized and tempted in the wilderness, and Latter-day Saint scholars explain the significance of these events by joining scholarship and the Bible.

items.title: "He Went Up Into A Mountain": Sermon on the Mount
items.description: Latter-day Saint scholars discuss the symbolism and significance behind Jesus’ miracles, including the marriage at Cana, healing the paralytic, the calming of the stormy sea, the feeding of the 5000, and the raising of Lazarus.

items.title: "I Have Trodden The Wine Press Alone": Atonement
items.description: In the last days of Christ’s life, he suffers the pains of Gethsemane and is betrayed by one of his beloved apostles. Latter-day Saint scholars describe the crucifixion of Jesus in a scriptural and contemporary context.

items.title: He Is Not Here; for He Is Risen: Resurrection
items.description: The resurrection follows Christ’s crucifixion, and Latter-day Saint scholars discuss the witnesses and effects of Jesus conquering death.

items.title: "Behold The Bridegroom Cometh": Second Coming
items.description: After Jesus’ ascension to Heaven, the world falls into an age of apostasy. Latter-day scholars converse about the Restoration and the scriptural references to Armageddon and the Millennium.

items.title: Miracle at Manchester
items.description: A high school student’s cancer battle inspires a community to unite in faith, hope, and prayer as miracles unfold in unexpected ways. Based on a true story.

items.title: Miss Austen Regrets
items.description: Readers of her novels are charmed by their flirtatious sentiments, but Jane must confront reality—and the pressing challenge of supporting her family while she herself remains an impoverished spinster.

items.title: Montana Saints
items.description: This short historical documentary explores what has mattered most to members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints for over 150 years in the state of Montana. From the late 1800s to the present day, a heartwarming story emerges.

items.title: We Need a Little Christmas featuring Angela Lansbury
items.description: British-American actress and singer Angela Lansbury joins The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square in “We Need a Little Christmas”. Lansbury sings “We Need a Little Christmas,” “Not While I’m Around,” and many more . Plus, the story of Luke II.

items.title: A Christmas Celebration with Bryn Terfel
items.description: Guest artist Bryn Terfel with The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square present “A Christmas Celebration”. Songs included “Away in the Manger,”, and “O, Come All Ye Faithful," and more.

items.title: Celebrate Christmas with Audra McDonald
items.description: Christmas is a time to celebrate and remember those who gave us life and love. But mostly, it's a time to raise our voices in songs of praise. Don’t miss the world renowned Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square and guest star Audra McDonald.

items.title: Christmas Light with Sissel
items.description: Norwegian-born singing sensation Sissel joined The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square for their annual Christmas concerts in a performance described as “a match made in heaven.”

items.title: O Holy Night with Sandi Patty
items.description: Christmas is a time of year to gather together, to set cares aside and bask in the warmth and cheer of family and friends. Enjoy “O Holy Night,” with special guest Sandi Patty and the world renowned Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square.

items.title: Rejoice and Be Glad featuring the King Singers
items.description: Rejoice and Be Glad with the King’s Singers, The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square as they present some of the most beloved Christmas songs in history. Join us for this inspiring performance.

items.title: A Tradition of Christmas
items.description: Joy to the World – “O, Come All Ye Faithful” – “Angels from the Realms of Glory” – “I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day” and more.

items.title: The Spirit of Christmas with Brian Stokes Mitchell
items.description: Join Broadway star Brian Stokes Mitchell for “The Spirit of Christmas”, with The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square, as they celebrate the timeless message of peace on earth good will to men.

items.title: Carols Then and Now with Natalie Cole
items.description: Join internationally renowned recording artist Natalie Cole in “Carols Then and Now”, with The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square, as they celebrate the enchanting music of Christmas.

items.title: Wondrous Christmas with David Archuleta
items.description: Join international singing sensation David Archuleta and the world-renowned Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square as they perform the enchantingly beautiful music of the season in, A Wondrous Christmas, a Music and the Spoken Word special program.

items.title: A Decade of Christmas
items.description: Celebrate the past decade of Christmas music on Temple Square with special guest artists Natalie Cole, Angela Lansbury, David Archuleta and many more, as they join the world renowned Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square, Orchestra at Temple Square.

items.title: The Spirit of Giving with Jane Seymour
items.description: Celebrate the holidays with The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square and acclaimed actress Jayne Seymour in a beautiful Music & the Spoken Word Christmas program “The Spirit of Giving”.

items.title: A Magical Season with Nathan Gunn
items.description: Celebrate the holiday season with The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square and acclaimed baritone Nathan Gunn, in a beautiful Music & the Spoken Word Christmas program “A Magical Season”.

items.title: Christmas in the Air with Tom Brokaw
items.description: Christmas in the Air, narrated by veteran newscaster Tom Brokaw, tells the heartwarming true story of Gail Halvorsen, the Berlin Candy Bomber.

items.title: Home for the Holidays with Alfie Boe
items.description: English tenor Alfie Boe joins The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square for this masterful Christmas special “Home for the Holidays”. Boe sings songs of the season “Hark! The Hearld Angles Sing” – “Angels, From the Realms of Glory” and more.

items.title: Christmas Favorites Featuring Deborah Voigt
items.description: Deborah Voigt joins The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square for this Christmas special. Recognized as one of the world’s most versatile dramatic sopranos and one of music’s most endearing personalities.

items.title: A Dickens Christmas featuring John Rhys-Davies
items.description: Music & the Spoken Word Christmas Special, A Dickens Christmas featuring John Rhys-Davies.

items.title: The Wonder of Christmas featuring Santino Fontana
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square joins with Broadway star Santino Fontana to sing joyfully of the magic of Christmas and the excitement of its traditions.

items.title: A Christmas to Remember featuring Laura Osnes
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square joins with Tony-nominated Broadway star, Laura Osnes. Also featuring narrator Martin Jarvis.

items.title: The Messiah Story
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square performs songs of hope, faith, and inspiration. Enjoy sacred hymns, both old and new; music from around the world; and uplifting selections from the American songbook.

items.title: O Come, Little Children featuring Rolando Villazon
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square performs songs of hope, faith, and inspiration. Enjoy sacred hymns, both old and new; music from around the world; and uplifting selections from the American songbook.

items.title: Christmas Organ Pipes
items.description: Choir Organist Rick Elliott’s fun, crazy original arrangements of seven favorite Christmas carols.

items.title: Blessing of Christmas featuring Hugh Bonneville
items.description: Tabernacle Choir & Orchestra at Temple Square present “Blessings of Christmas” with special guest Hugh Bonneville and Gabriel Trumpet Ensemble. Music includes “Joy to the World”, “Silent Night”, and “Sing!” based on Toccata from Organ Symphony no. 5.

items.title: A Merry Little Christmas featuring Sutton Foster
items.description: Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square present a Music & the Spoken Word special, “A Merry Little Christmas”, featuring Sutton Foster, with special guest Hugh Bonneville. Music includes “Christmas Time is Here”, “Unfold Ye Portals”, and more

items.title: Season of Light: Lea Salonga
items.description: Lea Salonga joins The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square in singing cherished Christmas carols, hymns and holiday classics.

items.title: Because of Christmas Day
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir, Orchestra at Temple Square, and the Bells on Temple Square perform, directed by Mack Walberg, with special guests Kelli O’Hara, Richard Thomas, and the Gabriel Trumpet Ensemble for this special: Because of Christmas Day.

items.title: Christmas Day in the Morning
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir, Orchestra at Temple Square, and the Bells on Temple Square perform, directed by Mack Walberg, with special guests Kelli O’Hara, Richard Thomas, and the Gabriel Trumpet Ensemble for this special: Christmas Day in the Morning.

items.title: Joy, Christmas with the Tabernacle Choir - Michael Maliakel & Lesley Nicol
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square performs songs of hope, faith, and inspiration. Enjoy sacred hymns, both old and new; music from around the world; and uplifting selections from the American songbook.

items.title: This Holy Night featuring Megan Hilty and Neal McDonough
items.description: The Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square present a Music & the Spoken Word special, This Holy Night, featuring Megan Hilty & Neal McDonough.

items.title: Our Silent Night
items.description: "Silent Night" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Holy moments are often created by the silent moments preceding them."

items.title: Depth of Gratitude
items.description: "Now Thank We All Our God" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "No life is free from hardship, but blessings can flow from the trials of life."

items.title: Christmas Blessings Never to be Forgotten
items.description: "Carol to the King" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "This Christmas season, may we each look for those who may feel alone."

items.title: Finding Christ in Christmas
items.description: "Sussex Carol" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "It is because of Him that Christmas truly is the most wonderful time of the year."

items.title: The Christmas Star
items.description: "’Tis Joy When Moon and Stars Above" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Thanks be to God for the gift of His Son and for the Christmas star that pointed to Him."

items.title: Gathering Christmas
items.description: "Hallelujah, from Messiah" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "As we gather, we feel God’s love, because it’s His love, ultimately, that draws us together."

items.title: Waging Peace
items.description: "Come Ye Children of the Lord" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "As we work to wage peace in our own hearts we become better prepared to practice it in our homes."

items.title: True Wisdom
items.description: "Dearest Children, God Is Near You" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "As we seek and act on God’s wisdom, we discover that He will show us the way forward."

items.title: My Brother's Keeper
items.description: "With Songs of Praise" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "May we each, as a beloved hymn pleads, 'be [our] brother’s keeper.'”

items.title: Moments that Matter
items.description: "This Day Is a Good Day, Lord" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Brought together, these millions of moments become the story of our lives."

items.title: The Accumulation of Our Decisions
items.description: "Guide Us, O Thou Great Jehovah" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Day by day, decision by decision, we gradually become who we will be at the end of our lives."

items.title: His Eye Is On The Sparrow
items.description: "The Ash Grove" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "God is aware of our lives—and not only our lives, but the details of our lives."

items.title: Love Is a Verb
items.description: "What a Wonderful World" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Love is both extended and received through our choices and actions."

items.title: Learning from Living
items.description: "For the Beauty of the Earth" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "As we look toward the future, let us also look to the past, seeking the wisdom of those who have lived before us."

items.title: Water the Roots
items.description: "When You Wish Upon a Star" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Taking time today to nourish our spiritual roots ensures that we can stand strong tomorrow."

items.title: Becoming Brave
items.description: "I Think the World Is Glorious" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "As we work to become brave, we can be armed with faith that runs deep. Faith sustains bravery."

items.title: This Is Jesus
items.description: "Consider the Lilies" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "This is Jesus—the Son of God, the Savior of the world, the King of Kings."

items.title: Easter is Hope
items.description: "That Easter Day with Joy Was Bright" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Because of Him, 'all that is unfair in life can be made right through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.'"

items.title: Remembering: An Anecdote
items.description: "Hornpipe, from Water Music" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Choosing to remember God mutes our murmuring. Focusing on Him and acting on His promises points us forward."

items.title: The Joy We Share
items.description: "Amazing Grace" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "We were made to lift and bless one another—and when we do, true joy follows."

items.title: Inspiration from Heaven
items.description: "To God Be the Glory" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "They encourage us to move forward instead of anchoring us forever in the past."

items.title: Sit and Eat
items.description: "Great Is Thy Faithfulness" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "God’s love always—always—bids each of us welcome. And when we feel least worthy to enter, that may be the very moment He is inviting us to sit—and eat."

items.title: Love’s Currency
items.description: "Love Bless Our Home" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "We are surrounded by those who need our sacrifice, our time, and our care. These are the currency of love."

items.title: Songs of Hope
items.description: "My God Is So High" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Through the music, the Spirit of God had simultaneously touched the hearts of a multitude."

items.title: Gently Raise the Sacred Strain
items.description: "Gently Raise the Sacred Strain" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. ""As the psalmist said, 'Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee. "As the psalmist said, 'Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.'"

items.title: Friends at Last
items.description: "I Would Be True" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. “Come on, dear brother, since the war is past, for friends at first are friends again at last.”

items.title: Get Understanding
items.description: "This Is My Father’s World" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "True understanding helps the complex become simple."

items.title: Evidence of Hard Challenges
items.description: "Rejoice, The Lord is King" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Some of life’s greatest lessons come from experiences we would never choose."

items.title: If Not You, Then Who
items.description: "Amazing Grace" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "At one time or another, we all are 'come … for such a time as this.'"

items.title: A More Perfect Union
items.description: "God Bless America" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. We can help build a "more perfect union", a nation under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.

items.title: #blessed
items.description: "Press Forward, Saints" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. God's blessings are an extention of His hand in our lives, guiding, supporting, and preparing us according to His will.

items.title: Dios de Amor
items.description: "Hymn of Praise" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Dios de amor. God of love. His love is greater than all the sorrow and tragedy on this earth combined".

items.title: Eliminating Distractions
items.description: "I Surrender All" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "When we put God first, all other things fall into their proper place..." -Ezra Taft Benson.

items.title: Think A Sacred Song
items.description: "How Firm A Foundation" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Some of the greatest sermons are preached by the singing of hymns.

items.title: Being Teachable
items.description: "Shenandoah" sung by the Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square. "A teachable spirit opens the door for lasting wisdom."

items.title: Another Perspective
items.description: "Over the Rainbow" from The Wizard of Oz, sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "A change in perspective can bring hope".

items.title: No Man Is an Island
items.description: "No Man Is an Island" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "We each have the power to choose, the power to serve, the power to influence. As John Donne reminded us, “No man is an island. [Each of us] is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.”

items.title: The Ordinary Life
items.description: "To the Endless Day!" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Here is the power statement: Every extraordinary journey begins with an ordinary step.

items.title: Repairers of the Breach
items.description: "Sing!" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "When the walls of life give way, the bonds we share can hold us together."

items.title: Setbacks and Setups
items.description: "Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Sometimes what looks like a setback really may be a setup for something greater."

items.title: The Lower Lights
items.description: "Standing on the Promises" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "The Lighthouse of God's love shines brightly, sending forth His mercy to all who will receive it."

items.title: Getting Past the Past
items.description: "One Person" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "When we make peace with the past, we make room for the future."

items.title: Spiritual Solutions
items.description: "I Surrender All" is sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Indeed, when we turn to the Lord, we find that every problem ultimately has a perfect solution, and it is found in Him."

items.title: Embracing Happiness
items.description: "O Love That Will Not Let Me Go" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Happiness can be found all around us, but we must choose to see it and then embrace it."

items.title: The Faith That Unites Us
items.description: "Praise the Lord! His Glories Show" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "Hope, peace, compassion and courage. These are among the strengths born of faith. And wherever they are found, there is common ground. Faith’s virtues truly can unite us."

items.title: The Heart's Condition
items.description: "There is Sunshine in My Soul Today" sung by the Tabernacle Choir on Temple Square. "We have the power to determine how we'll respond to difficult experiences."

items.title: Making the Most
items.description: "Redeemer of Israel" sung by the Tabernacle Choir on Temple Square. "When life gives you rain, choose to dance in it."

items.title: The Beauty of the Earth
items.description: "He's Got the Whole World in His Hands" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "As we take time to see and discover the gift of nature's beauty, we discover humility deep in our hearts, waiting to be uncovered."

items.title: To Teach and Let Go
items.description: "How Firm A Foundation" sung by the Tabernacle Choir. "His trust is evidence of His love. He knows that the most valuable learning comes through individual choice—responding to an invitation rather than being driven by compulsion."

items.title: Episode 1
items.description: Breeder Joe Spicer and trainer Neil McDonald play matchmaker for five sweet, energetic kelpies, as they strive to pick the perfect handler for each one.

items.title: Episode 2
items.description: As the four-month assessment approaches, the handlers test different ways of connecting with their pups; one naughty kelpie gets a devilish new name.

items.title: Episode 3
items.description: At six months, the pups have strong bonds with their handlers; they face big tests as they learn how to herd livestock and respond to calls.

items.title: Episode 4
items.description: With the year now completed, the kelpie siblings reunite for their final herding test.

items.title: Episode 1
items.description: Debbie and Snip become the mother and father of the newborn litter of pups in Goondy Creek, NSW; these pups are sent to five Australian graziers, who will each attempt to train their pup in less than a year.

items.title: Episode 2
items.description: The five-month assessment looms, and the handlers struggle to dedicate focused time to their pups; some trainers stumble while others leap through the tasks; the pups and trainers have a long road ahead of them.

items.title: Episode 3
items.description: At seven months, the pups have a strong bond with their handlers; but they face big tests as they learn to herd livestock and respond to calls.

items.title: Episode 4
items.description: At 10 months, the dogs have hit puberty and start to show some new teenage rebelliousness; there are mixed levels of success in the assessment and one of the pups falls gravely ill.

items.title: Episode 5
items.description: The 12 month experiment is complete, the Australian border Collie siblings reunite for the first time to face their final challenge; it's neck and neck but one dog shines brighter than the pack and is crowned Champion Muster Dog.

items.title: Episode 1
items.description: Six Border Collie and Kelpie pups are trained by graziers across Australia in a year-long challenge, guided by expert trainers, to test which will become the ultimate Champion Muster Dog.

items.title: Episode 2
items.description: Six trainers face unique challenges with their pups as they prepare for the five-month assessment. Balancing life and training, they must prove bond, obedience, calmness, and instinct to advance.

items.title: Episode 3
items.description: Six pups face their five-month test. Banjo shines, Pockets struggles, Hudson and Chief thrive, Banksi bonds with Blythe, and Pesto lags. Results surprise Mick and Neil as trainers prepare for the next stage.

items.title: Episode 4
items.description: The pups face their eight-month assessment. Handlers juggle farms, family, and school while Kelpies and Collies battle flaws. With surprising results, the race to crown the Champion Muster Dog heats up.

items.title: Episode 5
items.description: Mick and Neil travel to assess their teams as the ten-month deadline nears. From Nathan’s struggles with Chief to Kim’s standout with Banjo, each gains vital feedback. Team Kelpie and Team Collie face a fierce finish.

items.title: Episode 6
items.description: Six pups and trainers face their final test in Warialda. With judges watching closely, the challenges are fierce. One team rises above the rest, earning the title of Champion Muster Dog.

items.title: My Heavenly Father Loves Me by BYU Concert Choir
items.description: Listen to the BYU Concert Choir perform My Heavenly Father Loves Me, a beloved song celebrating God's love through the beauty of nature and everyday blessings. Beautiful choral harmonies invite gratitude, wonder, and peaceful reflection.

items.title: Ringo
items.description: In their search to find Paul a rescue dog, Joel and Laura are drawn to Ringo - a vocal young German Shepherd/Siberian Husky-cross. He is both big and black, and the hardest type of dog to rehome.

items.title: Memphis
items.description: Memphis faces being euthanized unless the right foster carer can be found. No-one can get close to this seemingly aggressive hound except Derek. Can Laura and Joel win Memphis' trust and help find Memphis a new home?

items.title: Jade
items.description: After a terrible accident, Tracy is looking for a canine to restore purpose in her life again. She's open to any dog as long as it's not a small, yappy dog. Can she overcome her aversion to a pint-sized pair?

items.title: Arty
items.description: Grieving migrant nurse, Rosey, wants to get a large rescue dog to help fill the void of losing her husband. Will big, beautiful but very anxious Arty be too much for first-time dog owner Rosey to handle?

items.title: Bailey
items.description: Host Joel Creasey and dog expert Laura V help loved up couple, Ian and Gail who need a small dog to keep lonely Ian company while Gail's at work.

items.title: Scout
items.description: After a series of traumatic and tragic events, newlyweds Ned and Gabriella want to start a new chapter with a dog who'll give them comfort and joy. Will they connect with Scout, the handsome comedian of a dog?

items.title: New Life
items.description: At 7 years old, Benjamin Morton discovers that Ava, the spunky little girl next door, is the love of his life. As they journey together through the seasons of life, a tragedy occurs that puts their entire future in jeopardy.

items.title: John-Michael Wright at the 2023 Big 12 Media Days
items.description: John-Michael Wright sits down with BYUSN to talk about this year's team, work to improve his game, and places to visit in Stillwater.

items.title: One Girl's Dream: Beverley Taylor Sorenson
items.description: Learn about the life and goals of Beverley Taylor Sorenson and how her legacy has changed the world for good.

items.title: One Sweet Baby by BYU Singers
items.description: BYU Singers performs One Sweet Baby, a tender Christmas song celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ. Gentle choral harmonies reflect the wonder of the Nativity and the hope, peace, and love at the heart of the Christmas season for families all over.

items.title: Heroes' Day
items.description: Ella has a condition that requires medicine through IVs. She made the Medi Teddy, a stuffed animal that covers IV bags to help kids with similar conditions feel at ease. The team meets in Fairfield, Connecticut to help Ella honor her town's heroes.

items.title: Give Back
items.description: Operation Awesome visits Philadelphia, Pennsylvania to meet their newest member, Anna Miller. The team joins forces with Tom and Hakeem, owners of The Block Gives Back.

items.title: Branch Out
items.description: Operation Awesome begins their next operation in Altoona, Pennsylvania where they meet 14-year-old Jakob Zernick, owner of Seedz 4 Needz. Jakob's organization grows and sells vegetables to provide toys for the children's hospital.

items.title: Puppy Love
